EXAMINATION:
CT ABD AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were obtained from the lung bases to the pubic
symphysis after administration of 130cc intravenous contrast.  Axial images
were interpreted in conjunction with coronal and sagittal reformats.

DLP:
404 mGy-cm
CTDIvol:  8 mGy

FINDINGS:


CHEST:
The visualized lung bases are clear.  There is no pleural or pericardial
effusion.

ABDOMEN:
The liver and gallbladder are normal.  The portal and hepatic veins are
patent. The pancreas and spleen are unremarkable.  The adrenal glands are
normal bilaterally.  The kidneys enhance symmetrically with no hydronephrosis.

The stomach and small bowel are normal in caliber. Within the right lower
quadrant, there is a dilated, hyperdense structure rising from the base of the
cecum, which measures up to 9 mm, likely representing the appendix
demonstrating mucosal hyperenhancment with respect to adjacent bowel.  What is
most striking is hyperenhancement and wall thickening rather than fluid
content.  Inflammatory changes are noted at the base of the cecum, and
adjacent to the whole wall of the appendix, and probably particularly at the
tip, which has an indistinct appearance.

Within the mesentery adjacent to the ascending colon, there are two strikingly
enlarged and briskly enhancing lymph nodes measuring 1.4 and 1.8 cm, the
former with low-density material centrally, and both demonstrate surrounding
inflammatory changes, including marked fat stranding about the node with
suspected necrotic or suppurative changes.

The ascending, transverse, and descending colon are unremarkable. There is no
mesenteric free air.

PELVIS:
The urinary bladder, and adnexa are unremarkable. The uterus contains
an intrauterine device, and standard position. Small amount of simple free
fluid is seen in the pelvis, likely physiologic.

VESSELS:
The aorta is normal in caliber and its major branches are patent.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
No focal lytic or sclerotic lesion concerning for
malignancy.

NOTIFICATION:
Findings were discussed with Dr. ___ by Dr. ___
telephone at 23:52 on ___.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were obtained of the abdomen and pelvis after the
administration of intravenous contrast.  Reformatted coronal and sagittal
images were reviewed.

FINDINGS:


CT ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:
The bases of the lungs are clear.  Within the
liver, there are calcifications within the left hepatic lobe which are
oriented in a linear configuration and possibly represent prior trauma or
infection.   No suspicious focal lesions are identified within the liver.  The
portal vein is patent.  The gallbladder is unremarkable.  There is no intra or
extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  The pancreas, bilateral adrenal
glands, spleen and bilateral kidneys are normal in appearance.  The stomach,
duodenum and small bowel are also normal in appearance with no evidence of
wall thickening or obstruction.

Within the right lower quadrant, there is an enlarged and fluid-filled
appendix with apparent fecal material within the base of the appendix,
measuring up to 2.1 cm in greatest diameter at the base (2:49).  Surrounding
inflammatory fat stranding is also present.  There is no evidence of
extraluminal air or drainable fluid collection.  Multiple small reactive lymph
nodes are also present within the right lower quadrant.  The remaining large
bowel is unremarkable with no evidence of wall thickening or obstruction. 
There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymph node enlargement.  The
intra-abdominal vasculature demonstrates a normal caliber aorta throughout and
a widely patent celiac axis, superior mesenteric and inferior mesenteric
artery.  Two right renal arteries are present.  There is relative atrophy of
the left rectus abdominis muscle, likely secondary to prior surgery with
multiple left-sided abdominal wall clips in place.

CT PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:
The terminal ureters are unremarkable.  The
bladder wall is slightly thickened, possibly due to incomplete distention. 
The rectum and sigmoid are unremarkable.  There is no pelvic sidewall or
inguinal lymphadenopathy.  A small fat-containing left inguinal hernia is
present.  There is no pelvic free fluid.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is evidence of prior spinal fusion at the L4-L5
level with apparent donor graft site within the right iliac bone.  No
suspicious lytic or sclerotic lesion is present.   There has been interval
removal of orthopedic hardware from the lumbar spine.

text:
LEFT UPPER EXTREMITY ULTRASOUND:
Gray-scale, color, and Doppler ultrasound
were used to evaluate the left internal jugular, subclavian, axillary,
basilic, brachial and cephalic veins.  Vessels in the forearm are also
evaluated.  The cephalic vein contains expansile echogenic material, extending
from the forearm to the mid upper arm, compatible with occlusive thrombus. 
More proximally in the upper arm, cephalic vein is compressible and
demonstrates flow.  Clot does not extend to the deep system.

Deep veins of the left upper extremity, including the basilic, brachial,
axillary and subclavian veins are compressible (where applicable) with normal
waveforms.

RIGHT UPPER EXTREMITY VENOUS ULTRASOUND.:


FINDINGS:
Grayscale and color sonograms of bilateral subclavian and

were evaluated.  There is unchanged appearance of the waveforms in the
subclavian veins.  Remaining vessels demonstrated normal flow,
compressibility, and augmentation.

EXAM:
Abdomen and pelvis CT.

TECHNIQUE:
This is an interpretation of images acquired at an outside
institution, for second opinion reading.  Data was acquired from the abdomen
and pelvis after the administration of intravenous contrast.  Images were
displayed in the axial and coronal planes.  Sagittal reformats were not
included with the outside hospital images as is protocol at ___.

FINDINGS:
There is bilateral dependent atelectasis in the lung bases.  The
heart is grossly normal.

ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST:
There are two hypodensities within the liver
parenchyma, the more superior in segment VIII (2:14) measures 5 x 8 mm and is
too small to fully characterize.  There is a second lobulated hypodensity
within segment IVb (2:33), which measures 14 x 14 mm, not fully characterized
on this single phase study, but may represent a cyst.  However, consider
ultrasound if there is history of malignancy for further evaluation.
Comparison with prior CT studies would be helpful.  The gallbladder is normal.
The pancreas, spleen, and adrenal glands are normal.  The kidneys enhance
symmetrically.  There is a 32 x 27 mm cyst in the upper pole of the right
kidney.  No bowel obstruction is seen.  There is no ascites.  There is no free
abdominal air.

PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:
There is a hyperemic dilated appendix with a maximum
diameter of 16 mm (2:61).  There is a proximal appendicolith (2:58) and
adjacent cecal wall thickening.  There is surrounding mesenteric stranding and
a small amount of adjacent free fluid without a well-defined rim (2:62).  No
drainable fluid collection or extraluminal gas is seen.

High density material in the prostate which are most likely brachytherapy
seeds.  The bladder and rectum are normal.  There is no pelvic
lymphadenopathy.

BONE WINDOWS:
There are no fractures, lytic or sclerotic lesions.

EXAM:
Chest AP upright portable view.

FINDINGS:
Single AP upright portable view of the chest was obtained.  There
are relatively low lung volumes.  Patchy left base opacity is seen which could
relate to atelectasis although consolidation from pneumonia or aspiration is
not excluded.  There is also patchy right base opacity and minimal streaky
medial right upper lobe opacity, both of which could be due to atelectasis,
aspiration or infection.  No pneumothorax is seen.  There is no evidence of
large pleural effusion.  The aorta is calcified and tortuous.  The cardiac
silhouette is not enlarged.

FINDINGS:
Portable semi-upright AP radiograph of the chest is submitted for
review.  Nasogastric tube is seen with distal tip in the proximal stomach and
proximal side port located at or slightly above the gastroesophageal junction.
It should be advanced for optimal positioning.  Relatively low lung volumes
are again noted.  

Patchy streak-like opacities are noted within the right and left bases as well
as right upper lobe and likely represent atelectasis.  There has been interval
development of bilateral pleural effusions along with interstitial opacities,
more prominent on the right than the left, consistent with pulmonary edema. 
The cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal in appearance.  There is no
pneumothorax.

FINDINGS:
Sonographic evaluation of the right lower abdominal quadrant in the
region of the patient's pain demonstrates a noncompressible blind-ending
tubular structure arising from the expected location of the cecum, likely the
appendix.  This structure measures up to 1.3 cm in caliber and contains
heterogeneous debris.  There is no significant surrounding hyperemia.  No
periappendiceal fluid collection is identified.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were obtained from the lung bases to the pubic
symphysis after administration of 150 cc of IV Omnipaque contrast.  Axial
images were interpreted in conjunction with coronal and sagittal reformats.

FINDINGS:
The visualized heart is normal. Lung bases are clear.  No pericardial or
pleural effusion.

ABDOMEN:
The liver is normal without focal or diffuse abnormality. The gallbladder,
intra- and extra-hepatic bile ducts, pancreas, and bilateral adrenal glands
are normal.  The spleen is top normal size, 13.0 cm.  The kidneys enhance
symmetrically and excrete contrast promptly.  The ureters are normal in course
and caliber.

The stomach is normal.  The small and large bowel enhance homogeneously and
have a normal course and calibur.  

The appendix is dilated to 9 mm, is fluid filled, and has periappendiceal
stranding.  No extraluminal gas or periappendiceal collection.  

No retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  The portal and
intra-abdominal systemic vasculature are normal.  The left renal vein is
retroaortic.  No abdominal wall hernia, pneumoperitoneum, or free abdominal
fluid.

PELVIS:
The bladder and terminal ureters are normal.  The prostate gland is
unremarkable.  2.2 cm hypodense structure in the right inguinal canal (2: 97)
extending into the right pelvis is compatible with the right testis.  A
bilobed hypodense structure anterior to the left external iliac vessels (2:83)
extending into the left inguinal canal is compatible with undescended
testicles.  No pelvic side-wall or inguinal lymphadenopathy. No free pelvic
fluid or inguinal hernia.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
No focal lytic or sclerotic lesion concerning for
malignancy.

TARGETED RIGHT LOWER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND:
In the region of patient's pain,
trace free fluid is identified.  The appendix was not visualized.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT axial images of the abdomen and pelvis were obtained with
intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were prepared.

CT ABDOMEN WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
Minimal pleural thickening is seen
within the left lung base.  No suspicious pulmonary nodule or mass is
identified.  The cardiac apex is within normal limits.

The liver demonstrates homogenous parenchymal enhancement without suspicious
focal lesion.  Mild periportal edema is identified.  Hepatic veins and portal
venous system are grossly patent.  No intra- or extra-hepatic biliary ductal
dilatation is identified.  The gallbladder, spleen, pancreas, and adrenal
glands are normal.  There is symmetric enhancement and excretion fdrom both
kidneys without suspicious focal lesion or hydronephrosis.  Abdominal aorta
and branch vessels are non-aneurysmal and grossly patent.  No concerning
adenopathy is identified.

There is an 11 mm dilated fluid-filled appendix within the right lower
quadrant with hyperemic walls, findings compatible with ____. 
There is a small pocket of free fluid adjacent to the appendix, however, no
extraluminal free air is identified to suggest perforation.  Minimal free
fluid is also identified within the deep pelvis.  Stomach and small bowel
loops are normal in caliber and configuration without evidence of obstruction
or inflammation.

CT PELVIS WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
Rectum and colon are normal in caliber
and configuration without evidence of obstruction or inflammation.  The
bladder is distended and appears normal.  Prostate and seminal vesicles are
unremarkable.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:
No bone destructive lesion or acute fracture is
identified.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT contrast-enhanced axial images obtained from the lung bases
to the pelvic outlet.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed.

FINDINGS:
The visualized portions of the lungs and mediastinum are unremarkable.
 The liver is homogenous in attenuation without discrete masses or lesions. 
The gallbladder, pancreas, and spleen are unremarkable.  The bilateral adrenal
glands have normal limb thickness without convex margin to suggest mass.  The
kidneys are normal in size and excrete contrast symmetrically.  The stomach is
unremarkable.  
  In the right lower quadrant, a dilated appendix measures 12 mm in diameter
(300B:29, 2:62), full course not optimally seen, but with a hyperdense focus
at the distal aspect which may represent an appendicolith.  Periappendiceal
fluid is seen.  The adjacent terminal ileum is markedly thickened, likely
reactive.  A small amount of free fluid is noted within the pelvis with
minimal enhancement of the adjacent peritoneum (2:69) which may represent
early peritonitis. Overall, findings are suspicious for perforated
____ with adjacent reactive changes within the ileum.  The large bowel
is unremarkable.  No diverticula are identified.  No drainable fluid
collections or free air identified. Multiple mesenteric lymph nodes are
identified, none of which meet CT criteria for pathologic enlargement.  No
portacaval or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy identified.
  The uterus, adnexa, bladder, distal ureters and rectum are unremarkable. 
The aorta, vena cava, main portal vein and their major branches are patent.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
No suspicious lytic or blastic lesions are identified.

Upright and supine radiographs of the abdomen.

FINDINGS:
Air and stool are seen filling the large bowel with multiple air
fluid levels seen suggestive of ileus.  There is perhaps a trace amount of air

unremarkable.  The imaged portion of the lung bases are clear.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT axial imaging was obtained from the lung bases through the
pubic symphysis following the administration of intravenous contrast material.
Coronal and sagittal reformats were completed.

FINDINGS:


CT ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST:
The visualized heart and pericardium are
unremarkable.  The lung bases are clear.  There is no pericardial or pleural

vein is patent.  The gallbladder, pancreas, and spleen are unremarkable.  The

In the upper pole of the right kidney is a small sub-cm hypodense lesion that

are unremarkable.  There is no free fluid or free air or lymphadenopathy

CT PELVIS:
The appendix is dilated to 8 mm and fluid filled with a
hyperenhancing wall consistent with ____.  Also seen is a
proximal obstructing appendicolith, image 601B:17.  Distally is a small amount
of trapped air, image 601B:11.  There is no evidence of perforation or abscess

There are no suspicious lytic or sclerotic lesions.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were obtained from the lung bases to the lesser
trochanters after the administration of oral contrast. IV contrast was not
administered.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were prepared. DLP:  456.45
mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:


CT ABDOMEN:
The lung bases are clear. The visualized portions of the heart
pericardium are normal. The liver enhances homogeneously and there is no focal
liver lesion. The hepatic and portal veins are patent. The gallbladder,
pancreas, spleen, and adrenals are normal.  There is no hydronephrosis or

CT PELVIS:
The appendix is mildly dilated up to 9 mm in diameter with mild
surrounding fat stranding. Oral contrast does not fill the lumen and there is

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is no lytic or blastic lesion worrisome for

EXAMINATION:
CT ABD AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were obtained from the lung bases to the lesser
trochanters .  IV and oral contrast was administered. Coronal and sagittal
reformations were prepared.

DOSE:
DLP: 633 mGy-cm

FINDINGS:


THORAX:
The lung bases are clear bilaterally. The visualized heart and
pericardium are normal.

LIVER:
The liver is normal in size and attenuation. No focal hepatic lesions
are identified. The portal vein is patent. There is no intra or extrahepatic
biliary duct dilatation.

GALLBLADDER:
The patient is status post cholecystectomy with clips in the
gallbladder fossa.

SPLEEN:
The spleen is normal in size and enhancement.

PANCREAS:
The pancreas shows normal enhancement. There is no pancreatic duct
dilatation or peripancreatic fat stranding.

ADRENALS:
The adrenal glands are unremarkable bilaterally.

KIDNEYS:
The kidneys display symmetric nephrograms with no evidence of
hydronephrosis or mass lesion in either kidney.  The ureters are symmetrical
in their course to the bladder.

BOWEL:
The appendix is dilated up to 9 mm with enhancing wall. The appendix is
fluid-filled with adjacent fat stranding consistent with ____.
(Series 2, image 57 and series 601b, image 25) There is no evidence of
appendiceal rupture or intra-abdominal fluid collection. The small bowel is
normal appearing. The colon is unremarkable.

VESSELS:
There is no aneurysmal dilatation of the abdominal aorta. The aorta
and its major branches are patent.

LYMPH NODES:
There are no pathologically enlarged retroperitoneal or
mesenteric lymph nodes by CT size criteria.

PELVIS:
The bladder is unremarkable. There is mild diverticulosis of the
sigmoid colon with no evidence of diverticulitis. The rectum is normal.  There
is no pelvic sidewall lymphadenopathy

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES/ SOFT TISSUES: There are no suspicious lytic or blastic

Contiguous non-contrast axial images were acquired through the
brain with multiplanar reformations.

FINDINGS:
Current examination is somewhat limited due to motion particularly
in the posterior fossa.  Allowing for such, there is no evidence of
hemorrhage, mass effect, edema, or shift of normally midline structures.  A
large area of right MCA territory encephalomalacia is new since ___, sequela of interval infarct.  Away from this area, the gray-white matter
differentiation is preserved.  Ventricles and sulci away from the area of

Allowing for significant motion, paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells

Comparison is made with a prior study from ___ as well as a CT from ___.

AP upright portable chest radiograph is obtained.  Low lung volumes

MDCT images were acquired from the lung bases through the pubic

Bibasilar dependent atelectasis is present.  There is no pleural

There is stable mild intrahepatic biliary dilatation, unchanged as compared to
___.  The common duct is normal in caliber.  The gallbladder, spleen,
pancreas, and adrenal glands appear within normal limits.  Bilateral kidneys
enhance symmetrically without hydronephrosis or hydroureter.  A subcentimeter
probable cyst in the lower pole of the right kidney is unchanged.  Moderate
atherosclerotic disease is present along the aorta.  Patient is status post
aortobifemoral bypass, with interval resolution of much of previously seen
para-aortic fluid since ___.

CT PELVIS:
There is inflammation extending inferomedially from the cecal tip
into the pelvis, with multiple small locules of extraluminal air, for example
(300B, 25),  suggestive of complicated ____ with contained
perforation.  There is inflammatory fat stranding and phlegmonous change in
this region without discrete fluid collection. This process extends into the
pelvis, with moderate hyperemia and wall thickening along the rectum and
sigmoid colon, likely secondary inflammation. There is no inguinal or pelvic
sidewall lymphadenopathy.  Mild presacral stranding is redemonstrated.  A
small amount of low-density fluid within the deep pelvis appears decreased in
amount as compared to ___ and likely reresents residual
hematoma/seroma.

BONE WINDOW:
No focal concerning lesion.  Mild multilevel spondylosis is
present in the thoracic and lumbar spine.

STUDY:
CT of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast; coronal and sagittal
reformatted images were also generated.

FINDINGS:


ABDOMEN:
The visualized portion of the heart and lungs appear unremarkable.

The liver demonstrates no focal lesion or biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder
shows no wall thickening, stones or pericholecystic fluid.  The spleen is
normal in size and appearance.  The pancreas is normal appearing.  The adrenal
glands appear normal bilaterally.  The kidneys enhance with and excrete
contrast symmetrically.  Multiple subcentimeter hypodensities within the left
kidney are most consistent with cysts, but are too small to completely
characterize.  The small and large intestine show no evidence of obstruction
or wall thickening.  No lymphadenopathy is seen.  No free air or free fluid is
noted.

PELVIS:
The bladder and rectum appear unremarkable.  A prostate calcification
is noted.

The appendix is identified, it measures up to 9 mm in diameter and is fluid
filled distally.  The appendiceal wall is hyperemic.  There is also
surrounding fat stranding in this area.  There is no evidence of an abscess or
extraluminal gas.

BONES:
No concerning osteolytic or sclerotic lesions are seen.

EXAM:
Chest frontal and lateral views.

FINDINGS:
Frontal and lateral views of the chest are obtained.  Lungs are clear without
focal consolidation.  No pleural effusion or pneumothorax is seen.  The
cardiac and mediastinal silhouettes demonstrate a top normal heart size.  The
mediastinum is not widened.  The aorta is slightly tortuous.

EXAMINATION:
CT ABD AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:

TECHNIQUE:
Axial helical MDCT scan of the abdomen and pelvis was obtained
following the intravenous administration of 150 cc of Omnipaque in a split
bolus .  Coronal and sagittal reformatted images were also generated for
review.

DOSE:
936 mGy-cm

FINDINGS:


LOWER CHEST:
The lung bases are clear. A calcified granuloma is seen in the
right lower lobe. The visualized portions of the heart and pericardium are
unremarkable. There is no pleural effusion.

LIVER:
The liver enhances homogeneously, with no focal lesions or
intrahepatic biliary duct dilatation. The gallbladder is unremarkable and the
portal vein is patent.

PANCREAS:
The pancreas does not demonstrate focal lesions or peripancreatic
stranding or fluid collection.

SPLEEN  The spleen is homogeneous and normal in size.

ADRENALS:
The adrenal glands are unremarkable.

KIDNEYS:
The kidneys do not show solid or cystic lesions and demonstrate
symmetric nephrograms and excretion of contrast.  No pelvicaliceal dilatation
or perinephric abnormalities are present.

GI TRACT:
The stomach, duodenum, and small bowel are within normal limits,
without evidence of wall thickening or obstruction. The colon is non-dilated
without obstructive lesions. The appendix is mildly dilated measuring up to 8
mm with hyperemia.  There is mild surrounding fat stranding, particularly at
the appendiceal tip.

VASCULAR:
The aorta is normal in caliber without aneurysmal dilatation. The
origins of the celiac axis, SMA, bilateral renal arteries, and ___ are patent.

RETROPERITONEUM AND ABDOMEN:
There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymph
node enlargement.  No ascites, free air, or abdominal wall hernias are noted.

PELVIC CT:
The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable.  No
pelvic wall or inguinal lymph node enlargement is seen. There is no pelvic
free fluid.  The uterus and bilateral adnexa are unremarkable. An IUD is seen
within the uterus.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
No blastic or lytic lesions suspicious for malignancy is
present.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were acquired from the lung bases to the pubic
symphysis after administration of IV contrast.  No oral contrast was
administered.  Multiplanar reformatted images were obtained for evaluation.

CT ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:
The visualized lung bases are clear without
pleural effusions.  The liver enhances homogeneously without focal lesions. 
There is no intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  The
gallbladder, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands and kidneys are normal.  There
is prompt excretion of IV contrast into the collecting system bilaterally,
without hydronephrosis or hydroureter.  The stomach, duodenum and loops of
small bowel are normal.  There is no free air, fluid or intra-abdominal
lymphadenopathy.

CT PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:
The fluid-filled, retrocecal appendix measures up to
10 mm in diameter, with moderate periappendiceal fat stranding, compatible
with ____ (image 2:46).  There is no free air or abscess.

The colon is grossly unremarkable with normal bowel gas and fecal matter.  The
uterus is normal in size for female of childbearing age.  The urinary bladder
is normally distended without focal abnormalities.  The distal ureters are
patent with excreted IV contrast.  There is no free air, fluid or
lymphadenopathy.

BONE WINDOW:
There are no suspicious osteolytic or sclerotic lesions.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH:


FINDINGS:
The lung volumes are low.  There are no pleural effusions.  No
pneumothorax.  No focal parenchymal opacities suggesting pneumonia.  No
evidence of atelectasis.  Normal size of the cardiac silhouette.  Normal hilar
and mediastinal structures.

TECHNIQUE:
Multidetector CT of the abdomen and pelvis was performed without
contrast.  Multiplanar reformations were provided.

DOSE:
DLP 337.79 mGy-cm

FINDINGS:
Lung Bases:  On series 2, image 3, there is a ground-glass nodule in the left
lower lobe measuring 3.6 mm. Mild bibasilar atelectasis noted. The imaged
portion of the heart is normal.

Abdomen: A tiny hypodensity within the hepatic dome is too small to
characterize and the liver otherwise enhances normally. No biliary ductal
dilation. The gallbladder is unremarkable as is the spleen and pancreas.
Adrenal glands appear normal. The kidneys enhance symmetrically and excrete
contrast promptly. The abdominal aorta is normal in course and caliber with
widely patent major branches.

The stomach and duodenum appear normal.

Pelvis: There is a large fluid collection within the right hemipelvis seen
best on series 2, image 60 measuring approximately 4.2 x 6.8 x 5.1 cm. 
Surrounding fat stranding is present and adjacent bowel wall thickening is
seen along the cecum and portions of the ascending colon, likely reactive. On
series 2, image 56, a rounded structure is seen centrally in the abdomen
adjacent to this large collection which likely represents a portion of the
appendix which has likely perforated resulting in this fluid collection.  No
gross free air.  No signs of bowel obstruction.  No significant free pelvic
fluid is seen. The urinary bladder is well distended appearing normal.

Bones: No worrisome lytic or blastic osseous lesion is seen. Transitional
anatomy is noted at the lumbosacral junction with partially lumbarized S1
noted.

TECHNIQUE:
Contiguous MDCT images of the abdomen and pelvis were performed
after administration of intravenous contrast.  Axial, coronal, and sagittal
reformats were acquired.

FINDINGS:


CT OF THE ABDOMEN:
The lung bases are clear.  The liver, gallbladder,
pancreas, spleen, bilateral adrenal glands, and kidneys are normal.  The
kidneys are homogeneously enhancing and excreting urine without evidence of
stones.
There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  The systemic
arterial, systemic venous and portal venous system of the abdomen and pelvis
are normal.  The esophagus, stomach, and small bowel are normal.  There is no
free air and no free fluid.

CT OF THE PELVIS:
The appendix is dilated and fluid filled measuring up to 10
mm in maximal dimension.  There is minimal periappendiceal fat stranding, but

RIGHT UPPER EXTREMITY ULTRASOUND:
The right arm is erythematous and
edematous, with multiple blisters on the medial aspect several centimeters
proximal to the elbow.  Grayscale, color, and pulse wave Doppler ultrasound of
the right upper extremity were performed to evaluate for deep venous
thrombosis.

A right PICC line enters the basilic vein, and courses beyond the subclavian
vein into the superior vena cava.  The subclavian vein demonstrates thrombus
on grayscale images, with minimal flow distally.  Except for where
instrumented by ___, the right basilic and axillary veins are compressible
and demonstrate color flow with appropriate waveforms.  No augmentation
maneuvers were performed due to thrombus in the subclavian vein, and the
patient was unable to perform Valsalva maneuvers.  However, flow in the
basilic, axillary, internal jugular, and brachial veins demonstrate
respiratory phasicity. Although compression of the brachial veins was somewhat
difficult, they were somewhat compressible and demonstrated normal flow with
appropriate waveforms and respiratory variation, and likely do not contain
thrombus.  The left subclavian vein was evaluated for comparison, and
demonstrate wall-to-wall flow and collapsibility during the respiratory cycle.

FINDINGS:
In comparison with study of ___, there has been placement of a left
subclavian PICC line that extends to the upper portion of the SVC.  Persistent
prominent bilateral pleural effusions.  The pulmonary vascular congestion
appears to have substantially reduced.

protocol.  Sagittal and coronal reformatted images were obtained and reviewed.

FINDINGS:

complications.

EXAMINATION:

PROCEDURE:
Ultrasound-guided drainage of pelvic collection.

TECHNIQUE:
The risks, benefits, and alternatives of the procedure were
explained to the patient. After a detailed discussion, informed written
consent was obtained. A pre-procedure timeout using three patient identifiers
was performed per ___ protocol.

The patient was placed in a supine position on the US scan table. Limited
preprocedure ultrasound was performed to localize the collection. Based on the
ultrasound findings an appropriate skin entry site for the drain placement was
chosen. The site was marked. Local anesthesia was administered with 1%
Lidocaine solution.

Using continuous sonographic guidance, ___ drainage catheter was
advanced via trocar technique into the collection. A sample of fluid was
aspirated, confirming catheter position within the collection. The pigtail was
deployed. The position of the pigtail was confirmed within the collection via
ultrasound.

Approximately 1000 cc of mildly cloudy serosanguineous fluid was drained with
a sample sent for microbiology evaluation. The catheter was secured by a
StatLock. The catheter was attached to bag. Sterile dressing was applied.

The procedure was tolerated well, and there were no immediate post-procedural

The risks, benefits, and alternatives of the procedure were

consent was obtained.  A pre-procedure timeout using three patient identifiers

for the drain placement was chosen.  The site was marked.  Local anesthesia
was administered with 1% Lidocaine solution.

advanced via trocar technique into the collection.  A sample of fluid was
aspirated, confirming catheter position within the collection.  The pigtail
was deployed.  The position of the pigtail was confirmed within the collection
via ultrasound.

microbiology evaluation. The catheter was secured by a StatLock. The catheter
was attached to suction bulb. Sterile dressing was applied.

complications.

minutes during which patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse.

EXAMINATION:
Ultrasound-guided drainage and catheter placement, right lower
quadrant abscess

PROCEDURE:
Ultrasound-guided drainage of right lower quadrant collection.

TECHNIQUE:
The risks, benefits, and alternatives of the procedure were
explained to the patient.  After a detailed discussion, informed written
consent was obtained.  A pre-procedure timeout using three patient identifiers
was performed per ___ protocol.

The patient was placed in a supine position on the US scan table. Limited
preprocedure ultrasound was performed to localize the collection.  Based on
the ultrasound findings an appropriate skin entry site for the drain placement
was chosen.  The site was marked.  Local anesthesia was administered with 1%
Lidocaine solution.

Using continuous sonographic guidance, ___ Exodus drainage catheter was
advanced via trocar technique into the collection.  A sample of fluid was
aspirated, confirming catheter position within the collection.  The pigtail
was deployed.  The position of the pigtail was confirmed within the collection
via ultrasound.

Approximately 55 cc of purulent fluid was drained with a sample sent for
microbiology evaluation.  Postprocedure ultrasound demonstrated that the
collection had been aspirated to completion.  No residual fluid collection was
identified.  On the postprocedure images, the catheter is anterior to the
adjacent colon within the collapsed cavity.  Postprocedure positioning of the
catheter outside the bowel lumen was confirmed by injection of a small volume
of normal saline, which was subsequently reaspirated.  The catheter was
secured by a StatLock. The catheter was attached to suction bulb. Sterile
dressing was applied.

The procedure was tolerated well, and there were no immediate post-procedural
complications.

SEDATION:
Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
1.5 mg Versed and 75 mcg fentanyl throughout the total intra-service time of
10 minutes during which patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse.

FINDINGS:
Technically successful ultrasound-guided drainage of right lower quadrant
abscess and catheter placement.  No immediate postprocedure complication.

reconstructions including volume rendered images, maximum intensity

workstation by the 3D imaging lab and reviewed.

___.07 mGy-cm

CT ABDOMEN:
Visualized lung bases demonstrate dependent bibasilar atelectasis.

Evaluation of the intra-abdominal organs is limited by the phase of contrast. 
Within this limitation, the liver is unremarkable. The gallbladder is
surgically absent.  The imaged spleen is unremarkable.  A 12 mm cystic lesion
in the pancreatic head (3a:32) is most likely a side branch IPMN.  The
pancreatic duct is normal in caliber.  The bilateral adrenal glands are
normal. The kidneys enhance symmetrically without hydronephrosis. The small
and large bowel are normal in course and caliber without obstruction.  There
is no free fluid.  Subcutaneous emphysema and foci of free intraperitoneal air
are likely related to recent laparoscopic cholecystectomy.  No pathologically
enlarged mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymph nodes are identified.

CT PELVIS:
The rectum, sigmoid colon, and bladder are unremarkable. The uterus is not
well seen, perhaps atrophic versus absent. No adnexal mass is seen. There is
no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

CT ANGIOGRAM:
The infrarenal abdominal aorta is ectatic to 2.0 cm with mural thrombus,
resulting in luminal narrowing to 1.4 x 1.0 cm (3a:39-40). The celiac artery
and SMA are patent at their origins with mild atherosclerotic plaque. The ___
is occluded just beyond its origin (3a:49-50).

On the right, there is short, approximately 1cm, segment of severe stenosis
(likely >75%) with trickle flow of the right common iliac artery (3a:74). The
right external iliac artery is patent.  The right superficial femoral artery
is very diminutive with intermittent high grade stenosis from its origin to
the point at which it is effectively occluded.  There is an approximately 9 cm
segment of SFA occlusion with reconstitution at the adductor canal although
the distal SFA remains narrow in caliber ("VR ROTATION, ___, image 1").  
The popliteal artery is very diminutive. The tibioperoneal trunk is patent.
The 3 vessel runoff demonstrates patent calf vessels without significant
atherosclerotic disease.

On the left, there is complete occlusion of the left common iliac artery from
the aortic bifurcation extending to the external iliac artery with
reconstitution of the common femoral artery via collaterals from the lumbar
and left abdominal wall arteries ("VR ROTATION, ___, image 1"). The left
superficial femoral artery is somewhat diminutive with intermittent
mild-moderate stenosis but remains patent along its course.  At the adductor
canal, there is multifocal atherosclerotic change with a dominant above-knee
stenosis likely greater than 50-75%.  The popliteal artery is narrow in
caliber with a focus where the artery becomes even narrower (3a:271) and is
likely functionally stenotic.  The tibioperoneal trunk is patent. The
three-vessel runoff demonstrates small caliber calf vessels, but they are
patent  without significant atherosclerotic disease.

BONE WINDOWS:
No bone finding suspicious for infection or malignancy is seen. 
Degenerative change is noted at the pubic symphysis with a small extrusion of
disc material indenting the inferior bladder (401b:22).

Preliminary findings discussed Dr. ___
(vascular surgery) by phone at 6:37pm ___.

increased echogenicity, suggesting mild fatty infiltration.  The main portal

However, no evidence of gallbladder wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid
is seen.  ___ sign was not present.  The gallbladder again had a folded

Visualized portions of the IVC are within normal limits.

The liver demonstrates homogeneous attenuation throughout.  A

represent pocket of fluid or a side branch IPMN (1401:82).

The spleen is normal in size.
Cortical renal cysts are seen bilaterally.  The adrenals are normal.
There is a small amount of free perihepatic fluid.
There is no concerning retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.
The bone marrow signal is normal.

ERCP:
Six spot fluoroscopic images were obtained without a presence of a
radiologist.  Following cannulation of the ampulla, contrast was injected into
the biliary system.  The intrahepatic biliary system is unremarkable.  The
common bile duct is normal in appearance.  No dilation or stricture is
identified.  According to the ERCP report in the GI Reports section of
CareWeb, biliary sphincter manometry was performed, demonstrating a markedly
elevated baseline sphincter pressure of 65-140 mmHg.

TECHNIQUE:
Multiple contiguous 5-mm thick axial CT images of the abdomen and
pelvis were obtained from lung bases to pubic symphysis utilizing 130 mL of IV
Optiray.  Prior to this, non-contrast set through the abdomen was also
obtained.  Subsequently, coronal and sagittal reformations were performed.

ABDOMEN FINDINGS:
The visualized lung bases are clear.

There is no extraluminal air.  The liver, spleen, adrenal glands, and right
kidney are unremarkable.  There are three small hypodense lesions, two in the
interpolar and one in the upper pole region in the left kidney.  There is no
renal calculus, hydronephrosis or hydroureter.  The pancreatic parenchyma is
enhancing homogeneously.  There is no definite inflammatory changes, or
abnormal fluid collection to suggest pseudocyst or abscess.  There is minimal
distention of the pancreatic duct within body and tail.  Pancreatic ductal
stent is in place draining into the duodenum.  The patient is status post
cholecystectomy.

There is no abdominal lymphadenopathy.  Stomach and small bowel are grossly
unremarkable, so is the large bowel.  The appendix is not clearly visualized,
however, there is no evidence of appendicitis.

The abdominal aorta and its major branches are within normal limits.

PELVIS FINDINGS:
There is a small amount of fluid in the cul-de-sac. Central
hypodensity within the uterus is likely related to products of menses.  There
is no pelvic lymphadenopathy.  The urinary bladder is grossly unremarkable.
There is dropped surgical clip lying in the pelvis.

The subcutaneous tissues are unremarkable.  The osseous structures are intact.

STUDY:
Fluoroscopic ERCP biliary and pancreas by GI unit.

FINDINGS:
A single fluoroscopic image is available for review obtained
without a radiologist present.  There are cholecystectomy clips within the
right upper quadrant.  A pancreatic stent is detected in the expected course
of the pancreatic duct.

STUDY:
ERCP.:

FINDINGS:
A single fluoroscopic spot image of the abdomen obtained at the
fluoroscopy suite without the presence of a radiologist is submitted for
review.  This image demonstrates a stent projecting over the expected location
of the pancreatic duct.  A few surgical clips are located in the right upper
quadrant of the abdomen and probably correlate to a history of previous
cholecystectomy.

TECHNIQUE:
Contiguous axial MDCT images were obtained through the abdomen and
pelvis after the administration of IV contrast.  Sagittal and coronal
reformatted images were obtained and reviewed.

TOTAL DLP:
402.65 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:


LUNG BASES:
There are trace bilateral pleural effusions and associated
dependent atelectasis.  The bases of the lungs are otherwise clear.  The base
of the heart is normal in size.  There is no pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:
The liver is normal in shape and contour.  There are no focal
hepatic lesions.  The portal veins are patent.  There is no intra- or
extra-hepatic biliary duct dilation.  No stone is visualized within the common
bile duct.  Multiple stones are seen in the gallbladder.  The gallbladder is
collapsed.  The spleen is normal in size.  The bilateral adrenal glands and
kidneys are normal.  There are no renal lesions, hydronephrosis, or
pyelonephritis.  They enhance and excrete contrast symmetrically.

The pancreas is enlarged and edematous.  There is significant surrounding fat
stranding as well as a large amount of free fluid surrounding the pancreas and
tracking into the bilateral paracolic gutters and along the left upper
abdomen.  This is most consistent with an ____.  There is no
evidence of a discrete fluid collection to suggest a pseudocyst.  The splenic
vein is patent.  The splenic artery appears normal without evidence of an
aneurysm.  There are no calcifications in the pancreas to suggest a component
of chronic ____.

The stomach and small bowel are normal in course and caliber.  There are no
specific abnormalities in the left lower quadrant to explain the patient's
focal pain, other than the fluid tracking along the paracolic gutter from the
____.  There is no evidence of obstruction.  There is no free air. 
The abdominal vasculature is normal in caliber.

PELVIS:
The large bowel is normal without evidence of a mass or focal
inflammatory changes.  The appendix is not definitely visualized, though there
are no secondary signs of appendicitis.  The bladder is mildly distended,
though it is otherwise normal.  The uterus is mildly enlarged, consistent with
a recent pregnancy and cesarean section.  The adnexa are normal.  There are no
adnexal masses.  There is trace free fluid in the pelvis.  There is no pelvic
or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There are no concerning lytic or sclerotic osseous
lesions.  No fracture is identified.  There are no significant degenerative
changes.

MR OF THE ABDOMEN FROM ___:


TECHNIQUE:
Multiplanar T1- and T2-weighted MR images of the abdomen were
obtained on a 1.5 Tesla magnet including dynamic 3D imaging prior to, during,
and after the administration of 7 mL Gadavist gadolinium-based contrast.  1 mL
Gadavist mixed with 50 mL water was also administered for oral contrast.

FINDINGS:
The liver is normal in signal intensity without evidence of focal mass. 
Multiple small layering stones are noted within the gallbladder lumen.  There
is minimal gallbladder wall edema and thickening with no surrounding
inflammatory change.  Note is made of a stone in the gallbladder neck or
distal cystic duct with some surrounding hyperenhancement.

The pancreas is diffusely decreased in signal intensity on T1 pre-contrast
images and demonstrates hyperintense signal diffusely on T2-weighted images
compatible with ____.  Surrounding peripancreatic inflammatory
change and edema is also noted.  There is no evidence of pancreatic mass or
ductal dilatation.  The pancreas enhances throughout its course without
findings to suggest necrosis.  The common bile duct is borderline dilated,
measuring 6.8 mm.  There is no significant intrahepatic biliary ductal
dilatation.  There is no evidence of choledocholithiasis.

The spleen, adrenal glands, and kidneys are normal in appearance.  The
visualized bowel loops and mesentery are normal.  There is no significant
mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.  The abdominal vasculature
appears widely patent.  The osseous structures are unremarkable.  The lung
bases are grossly clear.  There is a small amount of ascites in the upper
abdomen.  Small bilateral pleural effusions are also noted.

TECHNIQUE:
Grayscale and Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

FINDINGS:
The liver demonstrates diffuse increase in echogenicity. A hypoechoic lesion
measuring 1.8 x 0.9 cm is seen within the right hepatic lobe and likely
represents a region of focal fatty sparing.  There is no evidence of
intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The common bile duct
measures 0.4 cm.  The gallbladder is normal and without evidence of stones or
gallbladder wall thickening.  Evaluation of the pancreas is limited by the
patient's body habitus and by adjacent bowel gas, but the visualized portions
appears within normal limits and without evidence of choledocholithiasis or
pancreatic ductal dilatation.  The right kidney measures 11.4 cm, and is
without evidence of hydronephrosis or solid renal mass. There is no ascites.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH:


FINDINGS:
The lung volumes are low.  Bilateral pleural effusions, better seen
on the lateral than on the frontal radiograph.  Subsequent areas of mild
atelectasis at the lung bases.  Borderline size of the cardiac silhouette
without evidence of fluid overload.

exam_name: CT ABD & PELVIS W & W/O CONTRAST, ADDL SECTIONS
text:
TECHNIQUE:
Axial MDCT images were obtained through the abdomen and pelvis
with and without IV contrast as per ____ protocol.  Sagittal and
coronal reformats were generated.

TOTAL EXAM DLP:
1244 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:
There are bilateral small-to-moderate pleural effusions with associated
compressive atelectasis, left worse than right.  Visualized portions of the
heart and pericardium are within normal limits.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN:
The liver is low density on noncontrast images consistent
with moderate steatosis, and enhances homogeneously with no evidence of focal
hepatic lesions.  There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary ductal
dilatation.  The gallbladder is normal.  There is no evidence of gallstones. 
The adrenal glands are normal.  The spleen is homogeneous and top normal in
size. Kidneys enhance symmetrically and excrete contrast without evidence of
hydronephrosis or renal masses.

There is diffuse inflammatory peripancreatic stranding. Peripancreatic fluid
extend from the lesser sac into the anterior pararenal spaces and dissects
inferiorly, left worse than right, and along the paracolic gutters bilaterally
into the pelvis, but without well defined or walled-off collections. The
pancreas in itself demonstrates normal enhancement, although the head and neck
of the pancreas have a slightly lower enhancement when compared to the body
and tail.  No pancreatic calcifications.  The pancreatic duct is not dilated.
There is no evidence of pseudocyst formation, splenic artery pseudo aneurysms,
portal vein or splenic vein thrombosis. Splenic vein may be mildly narrowed.

The stomach is collapsed and contains a feeding tube which ends in the
proximal jejunum.  There is no evidence of small-bowel obstruction.  Oral
contrast courses freely into the colon with no evidence of bowel wall
abnormalities.  

The abdominal aorta is of normal diameter.  The celiac axis, SMA, bilateral
renal arteries and ___ are patent.  There are scattered small mesenteric and
retroperitoneal lymph nodes, which are likely secondary to the surrounding
inflammatory changes.

CT OF THE PELVIS:
The urinary bladder and terminal ureters are within normal
limits.  Small amount of stranding and fluid is noted in the pelvis, extending
from the abdomen.   Scattered inguinal lymph nodes are noted, none of which
meet CT size criteria for lymphadenopathy.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
No blastic or lytic lesion concerning for malignancy.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH:


FINDINGS:
The lung volumes are relatively small.  Moderate cardiomegaly with
mild fluid overload.  Plate-like areas of atelectasis in the retrocardiac lung
areas.  No pleural effusions.  No evidence of pneumonia.

SINGLE PORTABLE VIEW OF THE CHEST:
Comparison to the prior radiograph, there
is new increased vascular congestion and pulmonary edema.  Lung volumes remain
relatively low.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette and hilar contours are
unremarkable.  There are no pleural effusions or pneumothoraces.  Plate-like
atelectasis is again seen.

FINDINGS:
Supine and upright abdominal radiographs demonstrate a nonspecific
bowel gas pattern.  There are surgical clips in the right upper quadrant,
likely from cholecystectomy.  Additional surgical clips are noted in the
pelvis.  There is no evidence of pneumoperitoneum.  Plate-like atelectasis at
the left lung base is again visualized.  Osseous structures are unremarkable.

FINDINGS:
The liver is diffusely increased in echogenicity consistent with
fatty infiltration.  The main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow. 
The patient is status post cholecystectomy.  The common bile duct is
visualized and appears dilated up to 13 mm.  No stones are seen in the
visualized portions of the common bile duct, though the distal duct is not
well visualized. No intrahepatic biliary duct dilatation is present. The
visualized portions of the pancreas are normal, however, portions of the
pancreatic body and tail obscured by bowel gas and overlying soft tissues. 
The spleen is normal in size measuring 10.2 cm.

TECHNIQUE:
Helical MDCT images were acquired from the lung bases through the
greater trochanters with intravenous and without oral contrast.  5 mm axial,
coronal, and sagittal multiplanar reformats were generated.

FINDINGS:
Mild atelectasis is noted at the lung bases.  The heart is normal
in size.  There are no pleural or pericardial effusions.  Note is made of a
moderate sliding hiatal hernia.

ABDOMEN:
Diffuse fat stranding and soft tissue density are noted surrounding
the pancreas, overall increased since ___. This extends to the root of the
mesentery, and throughout the retroperitoneum, surrounding the abdominal
aorta, proximal iliac arteries, and celiac and superior mesenteric artery
takeoffs.  The superior mesenteric, splenic, portal, hepatic veins and IVC are
patent.  There is no parenchymal hypoenhancement suspicious for necrosis.  No
intra- or extra-hepatic biliary dilatation is present.

Again seen throughout the liver are multiple lobulated, hypoenhancing lesions,
previously demonstrated to be hemangiomas.  A new 1.5 x 1.3 cm hyperenhancing
focus is noted in segment VII, which also has a lobulated appaarance. 
Gallbladder is surgically absent.

The spleen is normal in size, with scattered ill-defined hypodensities in the
posterior aspect, which were not definitely visualized on prior examination. 
Note is made of a tiny splenule in the left upper quadrant, anterior to the
main splenic tip.

The adrenals are normal.  The kidneys enhance and excrete contrast promptly
and symmetrically, without masses or hydronephrosis.  Renal hypodensities are
too small to characterize, but likely represent cysts.

Again noted is a partially distended stomach, with retained fluid and air. 
Mild wall edema is noted at the C-sweep of the duodenum, adjacent to the area
of pancreatic head inflammation.  However, there is no transition point to
suggest obstruction.  Distal small bowel loops are fluid filled and
nondilated.

Sequelae of abdominal wall incisional hernia repair are present, with multiple
surgical staples and residual fat stranding in the anterior abdominal wall.

PELVIS:
Again noted is a prominent and fluid-filled appendix, measuring up to
7 mm in diameter, without wall thickening or fat stranding to suggest acute
inflammation.  The transverse and sigmoid colon are markedly redundant.  The
bladder is partially distended, with stable small right posterolateral
diverticulum that fills with contrast.  The prostate is slightly heterogeneous
and enlarged, with coarse central calcifications.  Note is made of bilateral
fat-containing small inguinal hernias, with a varicocele noted on the right. 
There is no free fluid or air.

The bones are demineralized, with mild S-shaped thoracolumbar scoliosis and
multilevel degenerative changes.  No suspicious lytic or sclerotic osseous
lesions are identified.

CHEST ___:


FINDINGS:
Frontal view of the chest demonstrates mild bibasilar atelectasis, new since
the prior study from ___.  Remainder of the lungs are clear.  No free
intraperitoneal air is identified on this upright portable view.  Heart and
mediastinum are within normal limits.

FINDINGS:
No previous images.  Bibasilar opacifications, more prominent on
the left, are consistent with atelectasis and effusion.  In the appropriate
clinical setting, the possibility of superimposed pneumonia would have to be
considered.

No evidence of vascular congestion or pneumothorax.  There is a prosthesis in
the right shoulder.

FINDINGS:
In comparison with the earlier study of this date, there has been
placement of a left subclavian line that extends to the lower portion of the
SVC.  Continued bibasilar opacification, more prominent on the left,
consistent with atelectasis and effusion.

RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND:
The liver is diffusely hypoechoic with
scattered punctate areas of echogenicity ("starry sky" appearance), suggestive
of acute hepatitis.  There is trace perihepatic ascites and a small right
pleural effusion, likely reactive.  There is normal hepatopetal flow in the
portal vein.  The gallbladder is partially distended, with equivocal wall
thickening and nonmobile calcified stones measuring up to 7 mm.  The common
duct is nondilated at 4 mm.  The pancreas was not well visualized.

FINDINGS:
Comparison to prior portable radiograph dated ___.  Calcified
pleural plaques, a moderately large left pleural effusion, left lower and
right lower lobe atelectasis, mild cardiomegaly and tortuosity of the thoracic
aorta are unchanged since the previous radiographs.  The left upper lobe
appears denser than the previous radiograph, which may either represent
posterior pooling of pleural fluid on this semi-upright radiograph or
developing infection.  The position of the central venous catheter tip is
satisfactory and likely lies at the level of the cavoatrial junction.  A right
shoulder prosthesis is unchanged.

TECHNIQUE:
Multidetector helical scanning of the abdomen and pelvis was
performed following the administration of oral and 30 cc of IV Optiray
contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformats were displayed.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN:
There are tiny bilateral pleural effusions and new patchy
opacities at the lung bases, which may represent pneumonia or aspiration. 
Anteriorly and in a subpleural location within the lingula and right middle
lobe are more fibrotic changes that are unchanged from the prior exam.  There
are also calcified pleural plaques suggesting prior asbestos exposure.

Evaluation of the upper abdomen is limited due to motion.  The liver, spleen,
and adrenal glands are normal.  There are gallstones within the neck of a
nondistended gallbladder.  

There is extensive inflammatory change associated with the pancreas.  The
pancreas itself enhances homogeneously.  In fact the pancreas is overall
intact with normal morphology.  There is less fluid and stranding within the
pericolic gutters, however more extensive inflammatory change in mesenteric
root and lesser sac.  

A peripancreatic fluid collection inferior to the body of the pancreas is
becoming more discrete and measures 4 x 2.6 cm.  Thickening of the splenic
flexure and descending colon as well as the duodenum are likely reactive.  The
SMA, SMV and splenic vein are grossly patent.  No pseudoaneurysms are
identified.  

The kidneys enhance and excrete contrast symmetrically, with a tiny 6-mm
hypodensity noted in the lower pole of the right kidney which is too small to
further characterize but likely a cyst.  No free air.  Mild-to-moderate
atherosclerotic disease is seen within the aorta.

CT OF THE PELVIS:
Foley catheter and air are seen within the bladder.  The
prostate is enlarged measuring 6.4 x 4.9 cm in the axial plane.  There is a
moderate amount of free fluid extending into the pelvis.  The sigmoid colon is
decompressed, however unremarkable.  There is a fat-containing right inguinal
hernia.  No pelvic lymphadenopathy.

The bones are osteopenic and there are multilevel degenerative changes, worse
in the lower lumbar spine.  There are also mild compression deformities of the
superior endplates at L1 and L2, unchanged from ___ and age
indeterminate.  No retropulsed bony fragments within the spinal canal.

FINDINGS:
In comparison with the study of ___, there has been placement of a
right PICC line that extends to the lower portion of the SVC.  Nasogastric
tube extends to the upper stomach, with the side hole just distal to the
esophagogastric junction.  Left subclavian catheter remains in place.

Bibasilar opacifications persist, more prominent on the left, with apparent
calcification of the hemidiaphragmatic pleura on the right.

FINDINGS:
Small right pleural effusion, with associated atelectasis, and moderate left
pleural effusion, are unchnaged.  Retrocardiac opacity obscuring the left
hemidiaphragm may represent atelectasis, pleural fluid or pneumonia if
clinically appropriate.  Lungs are otherwise clear without focal
consolidations.  Hilar and mediastinal silhouettes are stable.  No
pneumothorax is present.  Pulmonary vasculature is normal.

NG tube is in nondistended stomach.  Right PICC line tip projects over low
SVC.  Right shoulder hardware is noted.

EXAM:
Non-contrast head CT.

TECHNIQUE:
Axial images obtained through the head without contrast.

FINDINGS:
In comparison with the study of ___, there is little overall
change.  Small right and moderate left pleural effusions persist. 
Retrocardiac opacification again could represent atelectasis, pleural fluid,
or, if clinically appropriate, pneumonia.  Calcification of the
hemidiaphragmatic pleura on the right is again seen.  Nasogastric tube extends
well into the stomach.  Of incidental note is a prosthesis in the right
shoulder.

FINDINGS:
Residual contrast material is seen in non-dilated colon.  Relative
paucity of small bowel without evidence of dilatation to suggest obstruction. 
No definite gas is seen within the stomach.

The current examination is essentially within normal limits.  However, if
there is strong clinical suspicion of dilated completely fluid-filled loops of
small bowel, CT could be considered.

FINDINGS:
No pleural effusions, focal consolidations or pulmonary edema is present. 
Hilar mediastinal and cardiac silhouettes are unchanged.  Persistent right
basal opacity silhuetting right hemidiaphram likely represents atelectasis. 
Right basal pleural calcifications are unchanged.

Right PIC catheter tip projects over low SVC.  NG tube has been removed. 
Right shoulder prosthesis is noted.

TECHNIQUE:
Nine fluoroscopic spot views obtained during an ERCP without
radiologist present.

CHEST SINGLE VIEW ON ___:


FINDINGS:
There is a feeding tube in the distal duodenum with contrast seen
in the bowel.  There is volume loss at both bases.  Pleural calcifications are
again visualized.  The right-sided PICC catheter tip projects over the SVC. 
There continues to be bilateral lower lobe volume loss versus infiltrate.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the chest,
abdomen, and pelvis with intravenous and oral contrast.  Coronal and sagittal
reformations were evaluated.

CT OF THE CHEST WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
Moderate atherosclerotic
calcification is noted involving the aortic arch, with the heart and great
vessels appearing otherwise unremarkable and no pathologically enlarged
supraclavicular, or axillary nodes identified.  Scattered mediastinal nodes
are present up to 12 mm in the lower right paratracheal chain.  Trace
bilateral pleural effusions remain, and there is fairly extensive bilateral
noncalcified and calcified pleural plaques in the setting of peripheral
interstitial lung fibrosis as depicted by increased peripheral reticular
markings extending to the pleural surface and mild subpleural honeycombing
predominantly involving the right and left lower lobes with milder involvement
of the lingula and right middle lobe.  Superimposed patchy parenchymal
opacities within the lower lobes are again noted clearly progressed from the
___ outside CT examination and slightly progressed from the more recent
___ exam.  Mild right and left lower lobe atelectasis is also noted.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH INTRAVENOUS AND ORAL CONTRAST:
Moderate inflammatory
changes surrounding the pancreas are again noted with the parenchyma
displaying predominantly homogeneous enhancement with the exception of partial
heterogeneous enhancement noted within the pancreatic body-tail junction
(2:55).  The splenic artery and vein remain patent and no arterial
pseudoaneurysms are identified with the splenic artery again noted to be
markedly ectatic and tortuous.  The overall size of peripancreatic fluid
collections is slightly diminished from the most recent exam with no
well-defined rim-enhancing organized collection identified.  The largest fluid
collection is again noted to extend from the tail of the pancreas towards the
spleen, currently 21 x 32 mm (301B:59).  Reactive edema around the greater
curvature and mesenteric root is also slightly improved with persistent
scattered mesenteric and peripancreatic nodes identified.  No free air is
identified with the remaining intra-abdominal organs including the kidneys and
adrenal glands as well as the atherosclerotic disease of the intra-abdominal
aorta appearing unchanged.  A feeding tube is noted to be terminating distal
to the ligament of Treitz.  Oral contrast is present within the gallbladder
likely related to prior ERCP, no clear fistula noted.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH INTRAVENOUS AND ORAL CONTRAST:
Amount of intrapelvic
free fluid has diminished from the most recent examination and does not appear
organized.  Air is noted within the urinary bladder likely related to recent
Foley placement.  The prostate is also again noted to be enlarged.  Contrast
has progressed into the rectum with the large bowel displaying some mild
continued reactive edema about the splenic flexure and distal transverse
colon, but otherwise unremarkable.

BONE WINDOWS:
Multilevel degenerative changes are again seen with no
aggressive-appearing osseous lesions identified.  Streak artifact from prior
right shoulder arthroplasty is noted.

ABDOMINAL RADIOGRAPHS, SUPINE AND LATERAL DECUBITUS VIEWS:
Residual oral
contrast is visualized within the colon and rectum.  There is a normal bowel
gas pattern without evidence of small bowel dilatation.  There is no evidence
of obstruction.  No free air is identified to suggest perforation.  There is
diffuse demineralization of the bones.  Degenerative changes are seen in the
lower lumbar spine.

STUDY:
Abdominal ultrasound.

FINDINGS:
The liver demonstrates a normal echotexture without focal lesion or
intrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The portal vein is patent with hepatopetal
flow.

The gallbladder is distended, but shows no stones, wall edema or
pericholecystic fluid.  The common bile duct is 2 mm in caliber.

Pancreatic head and body appear normal and the tail is mildly obscured by
overlying bowel gas.

The IVC appears unremarkable.

The spleen measures 7.4 cm in its long axis.  It is normal appearing.

CTA PANCREAS PROTOCOL CT DATED ___:


TECHNIQUE:
CTA pancreas protocol.  Axial CT images were acquired after the
uneventful administration of 150 mL of Optiray 350 contrast material without
reported complication.  Pancreatic CTA examination was performed utilizing
standard departmental protocol with reformations in the sagittal and coronal
plane.  No oral contrast material was administered.  A limited non-contrast CT
through the lung bases, pancreas and mid abdomen was performed prior to the
administration of intravenous contrast material.

FINDINGS:
The lung bases are clear.

Non-contrast images through the level of the pancreas demonstrate no
significant abnormalities or calcifications.

CTA PANCREAS:
There is enhancement of the liver parenchyma with multiple 1-5 mm scattered
areas of hypoattenuation throughout the hepatic parenchyma.  The liver is
otherwise unremarkable without mass lesions.  The portal veins are patent. 
There is minimal central intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation (4:26).  No
extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  The gallbladder is normal in
appearance without gallstones.  The adrenal glands, spleen, pancreas, and
kidneys enhance normally.  No peripancreatic fluid or peripancreatic fat
stranding. No pancreatic ductal dilatation.  No signs of pancreatic divisum.
There is no hydronephrosis.  There is a tiny left interpolar 5-mm area of
hypoattenuation, too small to further characterize, but statistically most
likely represents a simple left renal cyst.

Evaluation of the arterial vasculature demonstrates a patent aorta in the
abdomen, without dissection.  Patent celiac axis and branch vessels and patent
superior mesenteric artery and branch vessels, where seen.  The bowel
including stomach, visualized portions of small and large bowel are within
normal limits.  No significant abdominal or retroperitoneal lymph nodes are
identified.

The osseous structures are unremarkable with normal-appearing vertebral body
heights and disc spaces were seen.

TECHNIQUE:
Helical MDCT images were acquired from the lung bases to the pubic
symphysis after administration of oral and IV contrast.  Multiplanar
reformatted images were obtained.

FINDINGS:


CT ABDOMEN:
There are tiny bilateral pleural effusions with bibasilar
atelectasis in the visualized lung base.  The lungs are otherwise
unremarkable.  The visualized heart appears unchanged, without pericardial
effusion.

In the abdomen, the liver is normal without focal lesions or evidence of
intrahepatic biilary dilatation.  There are two small gallstones in the
dependent position of a non- distended gallbladder without evidence of acute
cholecystitis.  The spleen and adrenal glands are unremarkable.  The kidneys
appear atrophic bilaterally, with the known cystic structure unchanged.  The
suspicious small renal lesion in the right interpolar region is again seen
without any short interval changes. The stomach, duodenum and loops of
nondistended small bowel are within normal limits.

In the pancreas, there is a metallic stent with the one end in the head of the
pancreas and the other end in the proximal CBD adjacent to the gallbladder.
Interval development of fat stranding along the CDB in the porta hepatis, but
no definite collection suspicious for abscess.  The fat stranding area
approximately measures 4 x 3cm, best visualized in image 2:24.

There is no free fluid or air in the intra- abdominal cavity. There are
scattered small mesenteric nodes, but none of them are pathologically enlarged
by CT criteria.

CT PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:
The colon is patent with oral contrast and bowel
gas.  The bladder is normally distended without focal abnormality.  The
prostate is unremarkable.  The loops of small bowel in the pelvis are grossly
unremarkable.  The left common iliac has an aneurysmal dilatation, measuring
3.5 cm in diameter, inferior to the imaged volume of prior study .  There is
no free fluid or air in the pelvis. There is no lymphadenopathy.

BONE WINDOW:
There is significant degenerative disease in the underlying
thoracolumbar spine, with multilevel ntervertebral disc space narrowingi and
osteophytosis.  Levoscoliosis of the lumbar spine, unchanged.  No acute
fracture or dislocation.  No lytic or sclerotic bony lesion suspicious for
metastasis.  Moderate aortic calcification is seen but unchanged.

FINDINGS:
There is prominence of the pulmonary vasculature with mild
cephalization.  Additionally, there are bilateral increased interstitial
markings.  These findings are suggestive of mild pulmonary edema. 
Cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal.  No acute fractures are identified.

STUDY:
Abdominal sonogram.

TECHNIQUE:
Real-time grayscale images of the abdominal organs was performed
and reviewed.

FINDINGS:
The liver demonstrates normal echotexture.  No focal hepatic
lesions are seen.  Portal venous flow is hepatopetal.  Patient is status post
cholecystectomy.  Spleen is within normal limits in size.

There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  The CBD

The liver is normal in echotexture.  There is no intra- or extra-

Six spot fluoroscopic images were obtained during ERCP performed by
Dr. ___ on ___, without a radiologist present.  Initial
images demonstrate appropriate position of the endoscope with subsequent
cannulation and opacification of the biliary tree.  Subsequent images
demonstrate no stricture, filling defect, or extrinsic compression of the
common bile duct or intrahepatic ducts.  Per the ERCP report, a few small

Single portable supine abdominal radiograph.

FINDINGS:
This is a technically limited study with the right lateral aspect
of the abdomen incompletely imaged.  Note is made of a nasogastric tube with
tip coursing well below the diaphragm, in good position.  Prominent gaseous

unremarkable. Visualized portions of the osseous structures are normal.
Limited evaluation of the lung bases. Recommend correlation with dedicated

CHEST RADIOGRAPH:


FINDINGS:
The endotracheal tube and the nasogastric tube are in unchanged
position.  The lung volumes have slightly increased; however, moderate
bilateral pleural effusions are still present, as is a massive retrocardiac
atelectasis with air bronchograms.  The presence of a coexisting infectious
parenchymal process cannot be excluded.  No evidence of pneumothorax.

FINDINGS:
The patient has been extubated.  The NGT has been removed.

Reduced effusions are seen bilaterally.  Comparing the frontal view, although
residual effusions are present, left greater than right.  Some left basilar
atelectasis is seen, but there is no patchy consolidation.  Pulmonary vascular
markings, cardiac silhouette and mediastinal contours are normal.

FINDINGS:
The liver is normal in echogenicity.  There is no intrahepatic
biliary duct dilatation.   The portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow. 
The gallbladder is normal.  There are gallstones in the gallbladder.  The
common bile duct measures 5 mm.  There are 2 small cysts in the left lobe of
the liver measuring 9 and 8 mm.  The visualized portions of the right kidney
are unremarkable.  The spleen measures 12 cm and is homogeneous.  The pancreas
appears unremarkable.  No peripancreatic fluid collections are seen.

TECHNIQUE:
Contrast-enhanced axial MDCT images through the abdomen and pelvis
with coronal and sagittal reformats.

FINDINGS:
Lung bases are notable for minimal dependent atelectasis.  There is no pleural
effusion.

Liver enhances homogeneously without focal lesions.  However, there is
moderate intra- and extra-hepatic biliary dilatation with the common bile duct
measuring up to 9 mm in diameter and extends to the ampula.  No definite
obstructing lesion is identified.  The gallbladder is not clearly visualized. 
A small amount of free fluid is noted inferior to the liver in proximity to
the duodenal sweep. The proximal duodenum demonstrates wall thickening, from
primary duodenitis or reactive. The spleen is normal.  Pancreas is mildly
atrophic but contains a normal caliber duct.  Bilateral adrenal nodules
measure 13 x 20 mm on the right (2:27) and 23 x 37 mm on the left. Kidneys
enhance and excrete symmetrically, containing subcentimeter hypodensities that
are too small to characterize.  There is no hydronephrosis.

The stomach is largely collapsed; again mild wall thickening is noted in the
region of the distal stomach and proximal duodenum. This area is in close
proximity to the common hepatic duct.  The remaining loops of small bowel are
normal in course and caliber without wall thickening or signs of obstruction. 
Multiple surgical anastomotic sutures are noted within the colon which is
otherwise unremarkable.  The sigmoid colon is notable for diverticulosis
without diverticulitis.

There is no mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.  There is no free
air.  Extensive atherosclerotic calcifications are noted along the abdominal
aorta and its major branches, without evidence of aneurysmal dilatation.

The bladder is partially collapsed.  The uterus is not well visualized and
there are no adnexal masses.  There is no pelvic lymphadenopathy or free
fluid.

Bones are notable for multilevel degenerative changes in the spine including
grade I anterolisthesis of L3 on L4 and minimal anterolisthesis of L4 on L5. 
Degenerative changes are also noted in the hips and the SI joints bilaterally.

FINDINGS:
PA and lateral images of the chest demonstrate well-expanded lungs.
Cardiomediastinal silhouette including moderate cardiomegaly is unchanged. 
There is no focal consolidation, pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT acquired axial images were obtained through the abdomen and
pelvis following administration of intravenous contrast material.  No oral
contrast was administered.  Multiplanar reformatted images were also obtained.

FINDINGS:
At the lung bases, bilateral pleural effusions are present, left
greater than right.  Associated atelectasis is also seen, left greater than
right.  Additional airspace opacity/infiltrate is present in the dependent
portion of the lungs.  The heart is normal in size, without pericardial
effusion.  There are no hilar or mediastinal lymph nodes that meet CT criteria
for pathologic enlargement.

In the abdomen, the body of the pancreas is swollen, but there are no areas of
under perfusion of the head, body or tail of the pancreas.  Inflammatory
changes and fat stranding are seen in the peripancreatic and anterior
perirenal spaces.  A focal fluid collection without well defined walls or air
bubbles is present superior to the tail of the pancreas and posterior to the
stomach.  Additionally, a mild-to-moderate degree of intra-abdominal ascites
is present.

The gallbladder contains contrast material from the ERCP of two days
previously, and is otherwise normal.  The liver, spleen, kidneys, adrenal
glands, stomach and intra-abdominal loops of small and large bowel are
unremarkable.  Multiple scattered mesenteric lymph nodes that do not meet CT
criteria for pathologic enlargement.  There is no free air in the abdomen.

In the pelvis, a small amount of free fluid is present.  Ascites fluid also
tracks into the right inguinal canal.  The right colon is distended up to the

caliber.  The rectum, sigmoid colon, bladder, and prostate gland are
unremarkable.  No pelvic lymph nodes meet CT criteria for pathologic
enlargement.

Examination of osseous structures reveals no lytic or sclerotic lesions.  Soft
tissues are unremarkable.
