text:
FINDINGS:
Grayscale and color Doppler sonograms were obtained of the left
internal jugular, subclavian, axillary, brachial, and basilic veins.  The left
cephalic vein was not clearly visualized on this study.  There is normal flow
and compressibility of the left internal jugular, subclavian, brachial, and
axillary veins. However, within the left basilic vein, heterogeneous
echogenicity centrally is seen, with no evidence of compression and flow,
consistent with a thrombus within the left basilic vein.  The extent of the
thrombus extends from approximately the level of the antecubital fossa to just
before its junction to become the axillary vein.

FINDINGS:
The hepatic echotexture is normal, without evidence of a focal
lesion.  The main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow.  The
gallbladder is distended, with small stones or hyperechoic sludge seen along
the dependent surface of the gallbladder.  There is gallbladder wall
thickening, with a trace amount of pericholecystic fluid noted. No sonographic
___ sign was evident. There is mild intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.
The CBD measures up to 5 mm.  However, within the mid portion of the CBD is a
rounded echogenic focus, measuring approximately 6 mm, which is concerning for
a stone within the CBD.

CHEST, PA AND LATERAL:
The heart is normal in size, with the aorta mildly
unfolded.  Surgical clips are seen within the right thoracic inlet, unchanged.
The lungs are mildly hyperexpanded, but clear without consolidation or edema. 
There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

FINDINGS:
There is diffusely increased hepatic echogenicity.  No focal liver
lesion is seen.  There is limited visualization of the pancreas, particularly
the distal pancreas.  Normal Doppler flow within the portal vein.  The
gallbladder is normal.  The proximal common duct is dilated, measuring up to
8.4 mm in diameter.  Spleen is normal, measuring 9.9 cm.

EXAMINATION:
LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN):

TECHNIQUE:
Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

FINDINGS:


LIVER:
The hepatic parenchyma appears coarsened. The contour of the liver is
smooth. There is no focal liver mass. There is no ascites.

BILE DUCTS:
There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CBD measures 6 mm
in diameter, borderline in diameter.

GALLBLADDER:
Several stones are noted within the gallbladder lumen without
evidence of cholecystitis. There is no gallbladder wall thickening.

PANCREAS:
Imaged portion of the pancreas demonstrate decreased echogenicity
suggestive of edema. No focal lesion is identified.  The pancreatic duct is
top normal in size.

SPLEEN:
Normal echogenicity, measuring 12 cm.

KIDNEYS:
The right kidney measures 13.1 cm. The left kidney measures 13.7 cm. 
Limited images demonstrates no hydronephrosis.

Patient is status post TIPS. Doppler evaluation demonstrates wall-to-wall
flow. Velocities measure 89, 77, and 99 cm/sec in the proximal, mid, and
distal portions respectively. When compared to prior study, these velocities
have decreased. Flow within the left portal vein is towards the TIPS shunt.
Flow within the right anterior a right posterior portal vein is towards the
TIPS. The hepatic veins are patent. The main portal vein is patent with
hepatopetal flow with velocity is 37 cm/sec.

FINDINGS:
Similar to prior exams, extensive surgical clips are identified in
the medial right upper quadrant.  There are numerous dystrophic calcifications
along the course of the pancreas and along the course of the various
mesenteric vessels, consistent with chronic ____ and atherosclerotic
disease respectively.  A non-obstructive bowel gas pattern is noted.  There is
significant fecal loading throughout the entirety of the included colon
including the rectum.  A surgical clip is identified in the left hemipelvis as
well.  The underlying osseous structures are unremarkable.  No free
intraperitoneal air detected.

TRANSPLANT PANCREATIC SONOGRAM:
Grayscale examination of the right pelvic
pancreatic transplant demonstrates no dilatation of the main pancreatic duct.
No parenchymal abnormality or peripancreatic fluid collection is noted.

Color Doppler examination demonstrates blood flow throughout the pancreas.
Pulse Doppler examination demonstrates patency of the portal vein, with normal
direction of flow towards the iliac vessels.  Normal arterial waveforms are
also demonstrated within the pancreatic parenchyma, with resistive indices
measuring 0.67, 0.67, and 0.64 in the head, body, and tail, respectively.

TRANSPLANT RENAL ULTRASOUND:
Grayscale sonographic exam over the left lower
quadrant renal transplant demonstrates no evidence of hydronephrosis, mass,
stone, or perinephric fluid collection.  The kidney measures 10.0 cm, which is
unchanged.

Color Doppler examination demonstrates flow throughout the kidney.  Normal
arterial intraparenchymal waveforms are demonstrated in the kidney, with
resistive indices measuring 0.70, 0.66, and 0.74 in the upper, mid, and lower
pole of the kidney respectively.  These are not changed from the prior study
of ___ where the resistive indices ranged between 0.62 and 0.67.  Normal
waveforms are also demonstrated in the main renal artery and vein.

TECHNIQUE:
Axial CT images were acquired through the abdomen and pelvis
following administration of 100 cc of intravenous Visipaque contrast.  Coronal
and sagittal reformatted images were also reviewed.

CT ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST:
The included portions of the lung bases are notable
for bibasilar atelectasis. The cardiac apex reveals extensive atherosclerotic
calcification of the mitral annulus as well as the coronary arteries.  The
stomach, duodenum, spleen are unremarkable.  The patient is status post
cholecystectomy.  The native pancreas is not identified.  Note is made of
pronounced atherosclerotic calcification throughout the abdomen.  The native
kidneys are present and markedly atrophic.  The adrenal glands are
unremarkable.  The liver is unremarkable.  Note is made of diffuse hypodensity
throughout the mesentery, suggestive of diffuse edema, in addition, there is
periportal edema noted through the liver.  There is no free gas in the
abdomen.  There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.

CT PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:
A transplant kidney is present in the left lower
quadrant.  The kidney enhances and excretes contrast, and there is no evidence
of hydronephrosis. The urinary bladder is notable for diffuse centrally
hypodense tubular structures adjacent to it on the right, likely anastomosed
duodenum secondary to pancreatic transplant.  Loops are notable for apparent
mural thickening and extensive surrounding fat stranding and hypodensity
suggestive of surrounding edema.  Notably, there is essentially isodense
material within these loops (2:68), which is non-specific in appearance.  The
transplanted pancreatic tissue itself is at the periphery of the zone of
inflammation, and appears unremarkable with no evidence of ductal dilation.
There is no discernable abscess.  There is no free gas in the pelvis.  Note is
made of a pessary device.  The rectum and colon are unremarkable, and the
appendix is not identified.  There is no pelvic side wall or inguinal
lymphadenopathy.  Note is made of diffuse subcutaneous fat stranding over the
anterior aspect of the pelvis.

OSSEOUS FINDINGS:
There is no suspicious sclerotic or lytic osseous lesion.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the abdomen and
pelvis following administration of intravenous contrast material.  Multiplanar
reformatted images were generated.

CT ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:
At the lung bases, lungs are clear, without
consolidation or pleural effusion.  The heart is normal in size, without
pericardial effusion.

In the abdomen, the liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, adrenal glands,
stomach and duodenum are unremarkable.  The patient has undergone prior
urinary diversion with bilateral ureters extending to a conduit in the right
lower quadrant. The kidneys enhance and excrete contrast relatively
symmetrically without stones, or renal masses. However, the right renal pelvis
and ureter are minimally larger than on the prior study, with slightly slower
egress of contrast through the ureter than on the left. This could reflect
reflux from the ileal conduit, vs mild stenosis at the anastomosis.
Bilaterally, renal cortical thinning is unchanged and consistent with
scarring, possibly from prior infection.

There is no free air or free fluid in the abdomen. The abdominal aorta and
major branches are within normal limits. There is no mesenteric or
retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy by size criteria.

CT PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:
Multiple loops of large and small bowel are
decompressed without evidence of obstruction.  The ostomy in the right lower
quadrant is stable. A large stool-filled structure tracks immediately anterior
to the uterus in the left pelvic midline. This is likely a large diverticulum,
given long-term stability in its appearance, with no change in size, position
and contents since ___.  The uterus again demonstrates multiple
fibroids. There are no adnexal abnormalities. There is no free fluid in the
pelvis. There is no inguinal or pelvic lymphadenopathy by size criteria.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Lumbosacral spina bifida with posterior meningocele is
unchanged.  There is no fracture or worrisome bony lesion.  Soft tissues are
unremarkable.

EXAM:
Chest frontal and lateral views.

FINDINGS:
The lungs are clear without focal consolidation.  No pleural
effusion or evidence of pneumothorax is seen.  The cardiac and mediastinal
silhouettes are stable and unremarkable.

RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND:
Three echogenic hepatic lesions compatible
with hemangiomas are unchanged from the prior ultrasound, the largest in the
right hepatic lobe measuring 7.0 x 5.6 x 4.6 cm.  Two small additional
echogenic lesions compatible with hemangiomas are identified, measuring 9 x 7
x 6 mm and 7 x 7 x 6 mm.  The gallbladder is distended, with small stones. 
There is no gallbladder wall edema.  Sonographic ___ sign is negative.  The
common duct is dilated, measuring 7 mm.  there is intrahepatic ductal
dilation.  There is a small amount of pericholecystic fluid, and free fluid in
___'s pouch.  The right kidney is normal, without hydronephrosis.  The
portal vein is patent, with anterograde flow.

EXAM:
Contrast-enhanced CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis.

TECHNIQUE:
Contiguous axial images of the chest were obtained prior to and
following the administration of 130 cc of Optiray intravenous contrast.
Contiguous axial images of the abdomen and pelvis were also obtained following
the administration of the aforementioned intravenous contrast.  No oral
contrast was administered.  Reformatted coronal, sagittal, and oblique images
of the chest are obtained.  Reformatted coronal and sagittal images of the
abdomen and pelvis were also obtained.

FINDINGS:


CHEST:
The aorta is normal in contour without evidence of dissection.  No
concerning filling defect in the pulmonary arteries or branches is seen to
suggest acute pulmonary embolism.  No pleural or pericardial effusion is seen.
No mediastinal or axillary lymphadenopathy is seen.  Prominent right hilar
lymph node measures 0.9 cm in short axis.  There is mild bibasilar
subsegmental atelectasis.  A coarse 7-mm calcification in the right breast is
noted.

ABDOMEN:
Four intrahepatic lesions are again seen, demonstrating peripheral
puddling of contrast, and which have been hyperechoic on ultrasound,
consistent with hemangiomas.  The largest is in segment VII and measures 6.1 x
3.6 cm (series 3B, image 79).  In segment VI, on series 3B, image 102, there
is a 2.2 x 1.4-cm hemangioma.  Hemangioma in segment IV/V measures 1.9 x
2.1-cm.  In segment II/III on series 3B, image 87, there is a 1.5 x 1.2-cm
lesion demonstrating non-continuous peripheral puddling, consistent with
hemangioma.

The gallbladder is distended.  Layering stones seen on ultrasound are not as
well appreciated on this CT due to differences in modality.  There is a small
amount of pericholecystic fluid. Mild central intrahepatic biliary dilatation
is noted.  The common bile duct is dilated, measuring up to 1.1 cm in
diameter, with relatively abrupt tapering distally.  Just beyond the level of
abrupt tapering, there is subtle high density in the distal CBD, best seen on
series 501B, image 21, which may represent intraluminal layering sludge/stone
or lesion.

The pancreas is enlarged in size compared to the previous study without
discrete pancreatic mass seen.  The pancreatic duct, including side branches
are prominent. The main pancreatic duct is prominent, but not frankly dilated,
measuring up to 2 mm in diameter.  Peripancreatic fluid is seen.  In
conjunction with patient's elevated serum lipase, findings are compatible with
____. No evidence of frank pancreatic necrosis is seen.  No
peripancreatic drainable fluid collection is identified.  Mesenteric/upper
abdominal free fluid is noted, measuring greater than that of simple fluid
(measuring Hounsfield units averaging from 35 to 51), consistent with complex
fluid, which may contain blood products.  No upper abdominal free air is seen.

The spleen, adrenal glands, and kidneys are unremarkable.

The portal and splenic veins are patent.

PELVIS:
The sigmoid and rectum are relatively collapsed.  The bowel is
difficult to trace, given lack of intra-abdominal fat and lack of oral
contrast. The transverse colon is at least partially collapsed, distally, and
is difficult to trace.  The cecum lies deep in the pelvis.  The appendix is
tentatively identified in the midline of the pelvis, is air filled, and not
dilated. Multiple loops of small bowel are prominent, but not dilated,
measuring up to 2.1 cm in diameter and contain "feces sign" with air and fecal
contents seen, which may be due to stasis, possibly from ileus from the upper
abdominal findings. 

The bladder is distended but unremarkable.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Mild degenerative changes at the lumbosacral junction are
noted with intervertebral disc space narrowing at L5/S1 and small anterior and
posterior osteophyte formation.  No concerning osteolytic or blastic lesion is
seen.

TECHNIQUE:

pubic symphysis following the uneventful administration of IV and oral
contrast.  Multiplanar reformations were provided.

CT ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:
The lung bases demonstrate moderate subsegmental
atelectasis.  The patient is post-cholecystectomy.  The CBD is dilated to 13
mm; comparison with the prior studies may be helpful.  The pancreatic duct
appears slightly prominent but is not overly dilated.  There is a pancreatic
duct stent, which protrudes approximately 2.2 cm into the lumen of the
duodenum (300b:27).

There is a large paraesophageal hiatal hernia (2:13). Oral contrast is seen
distally and therefor there is no obstruction. There is thickening of the left
anterior pararenal fascia (2:31) in this patient with chronic ____. 
Suture material is seen at the ileocolonic junction, and there has been prior
appendectomy.  There is no focal fluid collection or lymphadenopathy.

CT PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:
The uterus appears unremarkable.  The bladder and
rectum appear normal.

BONES:
There is grade I anterolisthesis of L4 upon L5 (301b:39).

ABDOMEN SUPINE AND ERECT FILMS.:


FINDINGS:
Comparison is made to abdominal CT scan from ___.

There is contrast material seen throughout the colon.  No colonic distention
is seen.  There are few diverticula within the sigmoid and descending colon.
There are a few non-enlarged small bowel loops which demonstrates gas filling.
There are no signs for bowel obstruction.  No free intra-abdominal air is
seen.

STUDY:
AP chest, ___.

FINDINGS:
No previous studies available for direct comparison.

The cardiac silhouette is enlarged.  There is streaky opacity at the left base
suggestive of atelectasis, however, early infiltrate is not entirely excluded.
No pneumothoraces are seen.  There is residual contrast material seen within
the colon.

TECHNIQUE:
Contiguous helical acquisition through the chest, abdomen and
pelvis was performed with intravenous and oral contrast.  Coronal and
sagittally reformatted images were created.

FINDINGS:


CT CHEST:
The heart is top normal in size.  Multiple prominent mediastinal
lymph nodes are identified measuring up to 9 mm in short axis in the
precarinal space.  The tracheobronchial tree is patent to level of the
subsegmental bronchi bilaterally.  There is interlobular septal thickening and
scattered ground-glass opacities most consistent with mild pulmonary edema.
Also noted are small bilateral pleural effusions and compressive atelectasis.
There is no pneumothorax.  No nodules or masses are identified.

CT ABDOMEN:
There is redemonstration of a large paraesophageal hiatal hernia.
Oral contrast passes beyond the hernia and there is no evidence of
obstruction.  The liver, spleen, adrenal glands, kidneys, and bowel are normal
in appearance.  The fat stranding fascial thickening involving the left
anterior perirenal fascia has resolved.  Again noted is a pancreatic stent
protruding approximately 2 cm into the duodenum.  The pancreatic duct is
prominent but not dilated.  The common bile duct measures 1.3 cm in diameter,
unchanged from the prior study.  Surgical clips are noted in the gallbladder
fossa, status post cholecystectomy.  No free fluid is noted in the abdomen.
There is no free air.  No mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy is
identified.  There is atherosclerotic calcification of the descending aorta.
Mild multilevel degenerative changes noted throughout the spine.  There is
grade 1 anterolisthesis of L4 on L5 likely degenerative in nature secondary to
facet arthropathy.  No suspicious lytic or sclerotic lesions are identified.

TECHNIQUE:
Contiguous axial images of the head were obtained without
administration of IV contrast.

FINDINGS:
There is no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage, edema, masses, or
mass effect.  The gray and white matter differentiation is well preserved. 
The ventricles are normal in size and configuration.  There are small
bilateral old lacunar infarcts in the basal ganglia.  The paranasal sinuses
and mastoid air cells are clear and well aerated.  The orbits are normal. 
There is mild atherosclerotic calcification of the cavernous segment of the
ICA bilaterally.  Incidental note is made of hyperostosis frontalis, usually
of no clinical significance.  Incidental note is made of prominent parotid
glands bilaterally, without evidence of stones in the parotid duct.

CXR, TWO VIEWS:


FINDINGS:
Heart is mildly enlarged.  Slight prominence of the upper zone
blood vessels and loss of sharp vascular margins consistent with interstitial
edema.  Minimal atelectasis noted at both lower lung bases.

ERCP:
14 spot fluoroscopic images were acquired during an ERCP procedure
without a radiologist present.  Images are submitted for further review.

There is a stent in the pancreatic duct.  The biliary tree is diffusely
moderate dilated, likely due to biliary stenosis.  Per ERCP report,
sphincterectomy and multiple balloon sweeps were performed.  Cytology samples
were obtained.

For further details, please refer to full ERCP note in OMR.

TECHNIQUE:
Supine and upright abdominal radiographs are provided.

There is a normal bowel gas pattern without evidence of obstruction.  Am
ileostomy is present in the right lower quadrant.  There is no free air.  The
visualized lung bases are clear.  Osseous structures are unremarkable.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN AND PELVIS:

Abdominal ultrasound.

The subsequent EGD study provides helpful additional information in

to a penetrating duodenal ulcer.  The penetrating ulcer could also have caused

the attending ___, Dr. ___ at 4:30 p.m. on ___.

text:
LEFT UPPER EXTREMITY ULTRASOUND:
Grayscale, color and Doppler ultrasound was
used to evaluate the left internal jugular, subclavian, axillary, basilic and
brachial veins.  The cephalic vein was not visualized.  The right subclavian
vein was also assessed.  Additionally, the left forearm was evaluated in the
area of concern.

The deep veins of the upper arm demonstrate normal compressibility, flow and
augmentation throughout.  In the more distal forearm, in area of concern, the
radial vein is expanded and is filled with somewhat hypoechoic material
demonstrating no color flow.  This is consistent with acute thrombus.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were acquired from the base of the lungs down to the
superior iliac crests with IV contrast in multiple phases. Multiplanar
reconstructions were obtained and reviewed.

Visualized lung bases and visualized heart are unremarkable.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:
Within the liver, again seen are multiple hypodense lesions.  While the
lesions in segment II (3a:21) and segment IVB (3a:33) are clearly hemangiomas,
there are other hypodense lesions with peripheral enhancing rims concerning
for metastases.  The possibilities include infected cyst, however an
ultrasound is recommended for further evaluation of the liver. There is
minimal intra hepatic biliary dilatation.

The spleen, right adrenal, right kidney are normal.  The left kidney has
several exophytic cysts, the largest of which measures 11 x 18 mm (3a:45).

There is an enlarged portacaval node measuring 17 x 23 mm.

Within the pancreas there is a dilated pancreatic duct leading into a
hypodense, hypoenhancing mass within the head of the pancreas.  Again seen is
air within the mass which is unchanged in size and appearance from prior.

Parts of the duodenum show abnormal enhancement (specifically 3a:58).  The
duodenum is not well distended in its entirety and it cannot be completely
evaluated.

The hypodense mass within the head of the pancreas does not involve the
superior mesenteric vein or other structures although a clear line of
separation cannot be seen between it and the duodenum.  The prior mentioned
cyst in the tail of the pancreas is not seen although a tiny 2-mm cyst is seen
in the head/uncinate process of the pancreas.  The liver has a normal vascular
anatomy with the left and right hepatic artery arising from the common
hepatic.  The left gastric artery arises directly from the aorta.

  e)  Portal vein involvement:  No.

bifurcation:  4 cm.

Pancreatic Vascular Table

a) Replaced right hepatic artery:  No.


The visualized small and large bowel appears minimally distended although no
obvious areas of obstruction are seen.  Multiple small lymph nodes within the
retroperitoneal area, which are not enlarged by CT criteria.  The left adrenal
again appears thickened measuring 11 Hounsfield units on the non-contrast
study consistent with an adrenal adenoma.

Upright and supine abdominal radiographs.

FINDINGS:
No free air is seen.  Multiple air-fluid levels are seen throughout
the small bowel.  The colon is gas-filled all way to the rectum.  Multiple
dilated loops of small bowel are noted.

FINDINGS:
Seven fluoroscopic spot images from ERCP are provided for review.  Radiologist
was not present during the procedure.  The biliary ducts are normal in
caliber.  Moderate segmental dilation of the common bile duct is noted
measuring 11 mm.  Per ERCP note, moderate amount of sludge was noted exiting
the ampulla after sphincterotomy.

PROCEDURE:
Chest PA and lateral ___.

FINDINGS:
The lungs are clear showing no focal or diffuse interstitial or
airspace disease.  Heart size is normal.  There is no pleural effusion.

GRAYSCALE AND DOPPLER ULTRASOUND OF THE RENAL TRANSPLANT:
The transplant
kidney measures 11.1 cm and is located in the left lower quadrant.  There is
no evidence of perinephric fluid collection or hydronephrosis or focal lesion.

FINDINGS:

consolidation.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal.  There is no
pleural effusion. Left deviation of the trachea, likely due to goiter

TECHNIQUE:

obtained.

FINDINGS:

intra- or extra-hepatic biliary dilatation with the common bile duct measuring
4 mm.  There is moderate gallbladder wall edema, but no evidence of
gallstones, gallbladder distention, or sludge.  ___ sign is negative.

TECHNIQUE:

CT ABDOMEN WITHOUT CONTRAST:

There is extensive emphysematous change of much of the body and tail of the

small foci of free intraperitoneal air likely stem from spread from the
retroperitoneal compartment. Additionally, there are multiple fluid
collections along the greater curvature of the stomach, measuring up to 81 x
___ cm in greatest axial ___, which demonstrate air- fluid levels

without intravenous contrast. Air is also noted within the gallbladder fundus.

CT PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST:

Foley is present within the bladder.  No pathologically enlarged pelvic lymph

Chest portable for line placement on ___.

SINGLE VIEW, CHEST:

MDCT axial images of the abdomen and pelvis before and after

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITHOUT AND WITH IV CONTRAST:

CT OF THE PELVIS WITHOUT AND WITH IV CONTRAST:

the rectosigmoid.  There is a Foley catheter within the urinary bladder.  The

BONE WINDOWS:
There are degenerative changes of the lumbar spine.  No
concerning lytic or sclerotic osseous lesions are seen.

SINGLE VIEW, CHEST:

region could be due to left lower lobe atelectasis is noted.  No other areas

lung fields demonstrate good aeration.  There is no pleural effusion.  There
is no pneumothorax.  Hilar contours are normal without evidence of hilar
adenopathy.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette, heart size is within normal limits.

STUDY:
Liver ultrasound

FINDINGS:
Extremely limited study due to poor acoustic windows, and bowel

without pericholecystic fluid or gallbladder wall thickening.  There is a
moderate amount of ascites.  Visualized portions of the hepatic parenchyma are

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT axial images were acquired through abdomen and pelvis
following intravenous contrast administration with split bolus technique.

Oral contrast was administered.

LOWER CHEST:

visualized on this examination.

The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout.

ERCP. The common bile duct dilation measures up to 2.3 cm without an obvious
obstructive lesion (series 9, image 37). The gallbladder appears distended
with contrast and has dependent small filling defects, consistent with
gallstones. No choledocholithiasis seen.

PANCREAS:
The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation.  There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN:
Two splenic hypodensities are visualized, statistically likely cysts.
An accessory spleen is incidentally noted.

ADRENALS:
A 14 mm right adrenal nodule demonstrates low internal density,
most compatible with an adenoma (series 7 image 19).  A 12 x 18 mm left
adrenal nodule has both low-density soft tissue and bulk fat, more compatible
with a myelolipoma (series 7 image 14).

URINARY:
The kidneys are atrophied, both containing multiple small
hypodensities, statistically likely cysts.

GASTROINTESTINAL:
Small bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber, wall
thickness and enhancement throughout.  Scattered colonic diverticuli are
visualized. No evidence for diverticulitis. Appendix contains air, has normal
caliber without evidence of fat stranding.

RETROPERITONEUM:
There are prominent para-aortic and aortocaval nodes
measuring up to 15 mm along the short axis (series 7 image 48).

VASCULAR:
There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  There is moderate
atherosclerotic (calcific and soft) burden in the abdominal aorta and great
abdominal arteries.

of pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis.

normal limits.

text:
ERCP:


FINDINGS:
Eight spot fluoroscopic radiographs were obtained during ERCP
without a radiologist present.  There is mild dilation of the CBD and
intrahepatic biliary ducts without evidence for stricture or filling defects.
Per the ERCP report, sludge was removed during a balloon sweep, but no stones
were present. For full details of the procedure, please refer to the ERCP note
from the same day.

RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND:


FINDINGS:
The study is limited due to the patient body habitus.  There is
likely fatty infiltration of the liver.  The common bile duct measures 8 mm
and the distal CBD is not visualized. There is no intrahepatic biliary
dilatation. The gallbladder contains numerous shadowing gallstones.  There is
no definite gallbladder wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid identified.
The pancreas appears heterogeneous in echotexture.  The tail is obscured by
overlying bowel gas. The portal vein is patent with normal hepatopetal flow.

CHEST PA AND LATERAL.:

The cardiac silhouette is top normal.  There are low lung volumes.
There is no focal consolidation, effusion, or pneumothorax.  The osseous
structures are grossly unremarkable.

ERCP cholangiogram biliary and pancreas by GI unit.

FINDINGS:
Nine fluoroscopic images are available for review obtained without
a radiologist present.  Scout image demonstrates no focal abnormality in the
right upper quadrant.  The common bile duct was cannulated with a microtome
and cholangiogram demonstrates mild common bile duct dilatation.  The
intrahepatic radicles appear amputated within the right lobe (image 7).

images.

There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary dilatation.  The common bile duct
measures 4 mm and is normal.  The main portal vein demonstrates normal
hepatopetal flow. The gallbladder demonstrates multiple gallstones. Minimal
pericholecystic fluid and gallbladder wall edema are present though the GB is
not overly distended.  The gallbladder wall measures approximately 6 mm.
___ sign is not definitively elicited as the patient has diffuse
tenderness over the upper abdomen.  The assessment of pancreas is limited due

Ultrasonography of the transplanted kidney and bladder.

FINDINGS:
A transplanted kidney is located within the right lower quadrant.
No surrounding fluid collections are seen.  Within the upper pole are two
adjacent simple cysts, measuring up to 2.8 cm in diameter.  Normal main
arterial and venous waveforms are seen.  The upper, mid, and lower segmental
arterial resistive indices measure 0.8, 1.0, and 1.0, respectively.  There is
decreased diastolic flow seen within the mid segment only.  There is no

PORTABLE CHEST X-RAY ___:
No prior studies for comparison.

FINDINGS:
Allowing for rightward rotation and portable technique,
cardiomediastinal contours are within normal limits.  Mild pulmonary vascular
congestion is present.  Multifocal areas of linear atelectasis are present,
especially in the mid lungs. More confluent opacities at the bases with air
bronchograms could reflect aspiration or infectious pneumonia in the
appropriate clinical setting.  Possible small right pleural effusion.

EXAM:
CHEST FRONTAL AND LATERAL VIEWS.:

FINDINGS:
Frontal and lateral views of the chest were obtained.  There is a
small left pleural effusion with overlying atelectasis.  Patchy left base
retrocardiac opacity may relate to effusion and atelectasis, although
consolidation cannot be excluded.  A trace right effusion may also be present.
Focal areas of linear atelectases/scarring are again seen, particularly in the
mid lungs bilaterally.

None.

FINDINGS:
Chest: There is mild cardiomegaly.  The mediastinal and hilar contours are
unremarkable.  There is no pneumothorax or large pleural effusion. The lungs
are well expanded.  There is no focal consolidation concerning for pneumonia.
Abdomen:  There is no pneumoperitoneum.  The bowel gas pattern is nonspecific
but nonobstructive.  There are no abnormal calcifications.  The visualized
osseous structures are unremarkable.

LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN):

Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

FINDINGS:


LIVER:
The echogenicity of the liver is homogeneous. The contour of the liver
is smooth.  Again seen is a cyst in the right lobe of the liver. There is no
concerning focal liver lesion.. Main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal
flow. There is new small volume ascites.

There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation. The CBD measures 4 mm.

There is cholelithiasis without evidence of cholecystitis.

Visualized portions of aorta and IVC are within normal
limits.

DLP: 385 mGy-cm (abdomen and pelvis.

FINDINGS:
There are bilateral moderate pleural effusions with severe right and left
lower lobe atelectasis (series 4, image 12). The heart size is normal. There

A 9 mm hypodensity arising from a hepatic segment VIII (series 4, image 35)
corresponds to a cyst, characterized on the ___ MRI examination. No
concerning hepatic mass is detected. There is no intra or extrahepatic bile

history of ____. The pancreatic parenchyma is swollen and edematous,
demonstrating uniform enhancement.  A hypodense focus at the distal tail
(series 4, image 42) corresponds to a cystic lesion seen on the ___
MRI. No pancreatic necrosis is detected. There is a moderate amount of
intra-abdominal ascites.

The splenic artery and vein appear patent.  A moderate-sized wedge shaped
hypodensity extending along the central spleen is most compatible with an

The adrenal glands, stomach, and intra-abdominal loops of small and large
bowel are within normal limits. A 12.4 x 10.5 cm simple cyst arises from the

Ill-defined hypodensities along the lateral aspect of the right kidney appear
new since the CT examination from ___ and MRI from ___,
suspicious for infarction or infection. There is moderate perinephric
stranding bilaterally. No collecting system obstruction is detected.

The abdominal aorta, celiac trunk, SMA, and renal arteries are patent and
normal in caliber. The SMV and portal veins are patent. Conventional hepatic

CHEST (PORTABLE AP):

FINDINGS:

placement of a right IJ catheter that extends to the right atrium.  It could

Continued low lung volumes with little change in the appearance of the heart

AP projection.

There is significant worsening of bilateral diffuse alveolar consolidations.

radiographs from ___ to present, this is concerning for ARDS. Depending
upon clinical volume status, this may also represent severe pulmonary edema.
Less likely is diffuse alveolar hemorrhage or bilateral widespread pneumonia.
There may also be a component of significant bilateral layering pleural

The cardiomediastinal silhouettes are not well visualized which limits

The above findings were discussed over the phone by Dr. ___

Interval repositioning of endotracheal tube terminating 3.6 cm

FINDINGS:
Lung bases: There is persistent moderate bilateral pleural effusions and

CT abdomen: The liver enhances homogeneously. A sub cm hypodensity in the

a cyst. The gallbladder contains multiple stones. A wedge-shaped hypodensity

mesentery, consistent with acute/sub____.

Abdominal aorta is of normal caliber throughout and celiac axis, SMA,
bilateral renal arteries, and ___ are patent. Portal vein, splenic vein, and

CT CHEST W/CONTRAST:

Contrast-enhanced chest CT was performed acquiring sequential
axial images from the thoracic inlet through the adrenal glands. Thin section

The thyroid gland is unremarkable.  There are no pathologically enlarged

scattered coronary artery calcifications. There is no pericardial effusion.

passive atelectasis of the bilateral lower lobes. The aerated portions of the

For a detailed discussion of the upper abdomen, please refer to the separate

FINDINGS:
Supine view of abdominal radiograph shows an NG tube in place.  The NG tube

demonstrates the tip terminating at the junction of the pylorus and the first

The spleen is normal in size. A wedge-shaped hypodensity within the
spleen is consistent with infarct and unchanged.  A stable.

The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

There is no evidence of retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR:
There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm.  There is no calcium burden
in the abdominal aorta and great abdominal arteries.  There is no evidence of
vascular complication secondary ____. Specifically, the splenic artery
and vein remain patent.

A Foley is present within a decompressed bladder. Air in the bladder is likely
due to recent instrumentation. There is no evidence of pelvic or inguinal

Reproductive organs are within normal limits. Fluid is
noted within the scrotum.

changes are noted. Diffuse anasarca is noted, extending to the proximal

specifically concerning for necrotizing fasciitis.

Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

FINDINGS:

Although somewhat limited by respiratory motion artifact due to

is smooth. Main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow. There is minimal

GALLBLADDER:
The gallbladder contains multiple shadowing gallstones and

PANCREAS:

Portable abdominal radiograph were obtained.

Moderate bilateral pleural effusions are similar in size to ___ with

TECHNIQUE:

through the pubic symphysis after administration of 130 cc Omnipaque

FINDINGS:
The lower chest is unremarkable.

There is no ascites, fluid collection, or pneumoperitoneum. 

The portal, splenic, and mesenteric veins are patent.  The abdominal aorta is

PELVIS:
There is marked sigmoid colonic wall thickening, mucosal hyperemia,
and extensive fat stranding.  This is on a background of extensive
diverticulosis.  There is an 18 x 12 mm pocket of fluid with small foci of air

formation (2:66, 601:39).

The bladder is normal.  Fibroid uterus.  There is a 3.0 x 2.4 cm simple cyst
in the left adnexa (2:64).  There is no pelvic free fluid or mass.  There is

MUSCULOSKELETAL:
There are no lytic or sclerotic osseous lesions concerning
for malignancy.

FINDINGS:
A single frontal view of the chest was performed.

Blunting of the costophrenic angles likely reflects atelectasis.  There is no

Orthopedic hardware of the spine is partially imaged.  There is no free air is

FINDINGS:

Substantial contrast material is seen within the bladder, presumably from

PA AND LATERAL VIEWS OF THE CHEST:
Lungs are clear without consolidation or
pleural effusion.  There is no pneumothorax.  The heart size is normal.  There

In the abdomen, the liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, adrenal glands,

A 6-cm segment of descending colon at the splenic
flexure demonstrates asymmetric wall thickening and edema and pronounced

the inflammatory change is not definitively seen.  There is no extraluminal

The urinary bladder, distal ureters, uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. 
There is a small amount of intermediate density fluid layering dependently in

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the abdomen and

the liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen and bilateral adrenal glands are

CT PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:
The urinary bladder, distal ureters, uterus,
sigmoid colon and rectum are normal.  There is a 4.6 x 3.0 cm hypodense cystic
structure in the right adnexa.  The left adnexa demonstrates a 1.7 x 1.5 cm

BONE WINDOWS:
No suspicious lytic or sclerotic osseous lesions identified. 
There is multilevel degenerative change of the thoracolumbar spine.

RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND:
The liver echotexture is hetereogeneous
without focal mass lesion.  There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary ductal
dilatation.  The common bile duct measures 5 mm.  The main portal vein is
patent with hepatopetal flow.  The gallbladder is normal without

PROCEDURE:

pneumothorax, or pleural effusion.  Cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the abdomen and

CT ABDOMEN / PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:  The lung bases are clear without focal

There is a significant amount of free intraperitoneal air with the largest
pocket in the anterior abdomen.  Small locules of gas are noted in the deep
pelvis where and in the sigmoid mesentery (2:63). There are two small fluid

perforated ____.

The liver demonstrates homogenous enhancement.  There is no intrahepatic
biliary ductal dilatation.  The common bile duct is dilated up to 1 cm which

seen. The pancreas, spleen, and bilateral adrenal glands are unremarkable. The
kidneys enhance and excrete contrast symmetrically without evidence of
hydronephrosis or hydroureter.  There is a low-density 1.9-cm lesion that

simple exophytic cyst.  There are extensive atherosclerotic calcifications of

stomach and intra-abdominal loops of small bowel are unremarkable.

exam_name: CT ABD & PELVIS W & W/O CONTRAST, ADDL SECTIONS
text:
TECHNIQUE:
MDCT axial images were obtained through the abdomen and pelvis
with and without the administration of IV contrast.  Multiplanar reformats
were generated and reviewed.

FINDINGS:


CT OF THE ABDOMEN:
The visualized lung bases show mild opacification of the
left lung base which may represent atelectasis versus infection in the correct
clinical setting.  The liver, spleen, pancreas, bilateral adrenal glands
appear unremarkable.  Gallstones are noted; however, gallbladder wall appears
unremarkable.  Subcentimeter hypodensities in bilateral kidneys are too small
to characterize but likely represent renal cysts.  Intra-abdominal loops of
small bowel are within normal limits.

CT OF THE PELVIS:
The bladder, distal ureters, rectum and sigmoid colon are
unremarkable.  There is evidence of sigmoid diverticulosis with surrounding
fat stranding.  Adjacent locule of gas and small 12mm focal fluid collection
(604b, 36 and 4,82) likely represents small nondrainable abscess or contained
perforation. 

There is no free fluid within the abdomen.  Retroperitoneal and mesenteric
lymph nodes do not meet CT size criteria for pathologic enlargement. 
Extensive atherosclerotic changes are noted within the abdominal aorta and its
branches.

No lytic or sclerotic osseous lesions are identified.  Multilevel degenerative
changes are noted.

PA AND LATERAL CHEST RADIOGRAPH:
The cardiac, mediastinal and hilar contours
are unremarkable.  Retrocardiac opacity may represent likely represents
crowding of structures. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax noted.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT helical images were acquired through the abdomen and pelvis
after administration of oral and 130 cc of Optiray intravenous contrast. 
Sagittal and coronal reformats were generated and reviewed.

FINDINGS:
A small-moderate amount of new intra-abdominal free air is seen,
consistent with perforated sigmoid ____.  Again seen is diffuse fat
stranding and mild wall thickening of a short segment of sigmoid colon, with
no significant interval change since the prior study.  Previously seen pelvic
12-mm fluid collection has resolved and no drainable fluid collections are
seen in the current study.  Small amount of fluid tracks along the left
paracolic gutter.  

The liver, spleen, adrenal glands, and pancreas are normal.  The gallbladder
contains two calcified gallstones, without evidence of acute cholecystitis. 
Few subcentimeter hypodensities in the lower pole of the left kidney, are too
small to characterize. No hydronephrosis or concerning renal masses are seen.
The stomach and small bowel are normal in appearance, without evidence of
bowel wall thickening or obstruction.  Moderate atherosclerotic calcification
is seen in the abdominal aorta, without aneurysmal dilation.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
The urinary bladder and distal
ureters are normal.  There is no pelvic lymphadenopathy. Small amount of air
within the vagina, raises concern for colovaginal fistula.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:
Mild compression deformity of T9 vertebral body,
unchanged since the prior study.  No bone lesions suspicious for infection or
malignancy are detected.

CHEST:


FINDINGS:
There is a new left-sided PICC line terminating in the upper SVC. 
These findings were discussed with ___ on the IV access team at 6:43 p.m.
by Dr. ___.  There is no pneumothorax.  There is retrocardiac opacity
consistent with volume loss/infiltrate/effusion.  There is pulmonary vascular
redistribution with some perihilar haze suggesting fluid overload.  There is
no pneumothorax.

CHEST ON ___:


FINDINGS:
Left-sided PICC line with tip at the cavoatrial junction.  There is
some retrocardiac opacity, but overall the aeration has improved compared to
the film from the prior day.  There is no pneumothorax.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT axial images were obtained from the iliac crest to the pelvic
outlet.  Rectal contrast was administered.  Coronal and sagittal reformations
were performed.

FINDINGS:
Redemonstration of sigmoid diverticulosis with persistent though
significantly improved wall edema with trace residual surrounding fat
stranding.  The previous region of maximal bowel wall inflammation and
associated fluid collection and likely perforation has resolved; however,
adjacent to a more superior portion of the descending colon, there is a new
2.4 x 4.2 cm fluid collection containing foci of air, likey representing a new
contained perforation (2:17).  Of note, the overlying soft tissues are
inflammed though no fistula with the sub/cutaneous tissues are noted at this
time. Trace inflammatory changes are also noted extending along the left
paracolic gutter.  The rectum, distal bladder are unremarkable.  There is no
pelvic sidewall or inguinal lymphadenopathy.  The uterus and adnexa are
unremarkable.  There is no suspicious lytic or blastic lesions identified.

TECHNIQUE:
Axial images from the lung bases to the symphysis pubis were
obtained after oral and intravenous contrast.

Comparison is made to previous CT dated ___.

FINDINGS:


LUNG BASES:
Small bilateral pleural effusions are seen.  Minimal right lower lobe
atelectasis is present.  No pulmonary nodules or masses are seen.

ABDOMEN:
Within the liver in segment VII, there is a poorly defined low-density lesion,
that measures 10 x 17 mm in diameter.  It is somewhat less well seen on the
previous CT(non-contrast), however, it was present then.  There are no new
liver lesions.  Cholecystectomy clips are seen.  The right kidney is
malrotated, however, no focal abnormality is seen in the right kidney.  The
left kidney is normal.  The spleen, pancreas, and both adrenal glands are
normal with no focal abnormality.

Again free air is seen throughout the peritoneal cavity however there is less
free air today.  No free fluid is seen within the abdomen.  There is
aneurysmal dilatation of the abdominal aorta, which is very focal, with
maximum transverse diameter of 30 x 32 mm in diameter.  There is calcification
of the abdominal aorta.No fat stranding is seen in the region of the duodenum
to suggest a perforated duodenal ulcer.

CT PELVIS:
Again there is significant artifact from the left total hip replacement,
obscuring fine detail.  

An air-filled collection is seen to lie in the left hemipelvis, lateral to the
sigmoid colon.  This measures 25 x 50 mm in diameter, when it previously
measured 16 x 55 mm in diameter.  This is almost completely filled with air
with only a trace of fluid within the dependent portion of this collection. 
The second collection, which lies anterior to the rectum also contains mainly
air with the fluid component also. It previously measured 36 x 56 mm in
diameter, and now measures 55 x 75 mm in diameter.  A third pelvic collecion
lying above the sigmoid colon measures73 x 21 mm in diamter and is nes since
the previous CT.

Three new smaller more anterior fluid collections are seen to lie anterior to
the uterus and above the urinary bladder.  These measure 22 x 23 mm in
diameter, 25 x 72 mm in diameter and 28 x 25 mm in diameter respectively.  The
sigmoid colon is markedly thickened with evidence of diverticular disease.

The dilated loops of small bowel have resolved.  Again, an abdominal wall
hernia seen in the suprapubic region containing small bowel which is not
obstructing.

Urinary bladder contains a urinary catheter within it and is decompressed.  No
large pelvic adenopathy, however, evaluation for adenopathy is limited due to
artifact from the hip prosthesis.

BONES:
There is extensive degenerative disease of the spine.  A wedge
compression fracture of L3 and L1 as well as T12, T10 and T9 are unchanged. 
No new concerning focal bony lesions.

ABDOMEN AND PELVIC CT.:


TECHNIQUE:
MDCT axial images were acquired from the lung bases to the
symphysis pubis, without administration of intravenous contrast.    Long
preparation with oral contrast was performed. Coronal and sagittal
reformations were also performed.

FINDINGS:
There is no evidence of pleural or pericardial effusion.  Coronary
artery calcifications are noted.  Minimal ground-glass opacities are
demonstrated in the lung bases.  Small hiatal hernia is seen.

Non-contrast view of the liver demonstrates a single hypodense lesion in
segment VII (series 2, image 22), which could not be characterized on current
study.  Non-contrast view of the spleen, adrenals and left kidney are
unremarkable.  Right kidney is malrotated without evidence. Visualized bowel
loops are unremarkable.  Pancreas is of normal attenuation and size.  There is
no evidence of retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  There is a
stable abdominal aortic aneurysm measuring up to 3 cm.

PELVIC CT:
Urinary bladder is very distended.

Sigmoid colon shows diffuse thickening, correlating to the area of previously
seen perforation.  A drainage catheter is seen in the right lower pelvis with
no residual fluid collection surrounding it.  There is residual fluid
collection in the left lower pelvis, currently measuring approximately 2.3 x
3.7 cm, previously measuring 2.5 x 7.2 cm.

Also seen ventral hernia (series 2, image 66) in the midline pelvis,
containing small bowel loops.  There is no evidence of obstruction or
incarceration.  There is no evidence of free fluid in the pelvis.

Extensive artifacts are seen from the metallic hardware in the hips.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Diffuse osteopenia is noted with numerous compression
fractures along thoracic and lumbar spine, unchanged from prior studies. Total
hip replacement in the left hip and internal nailing in the right femur.

exam_name: UNILAT UP EXT VEINS US RIGHT
text:
TECHNIQUE:
Ultrasonography of the right upper arm.

FINDINGS:
Grayscale and color Doppler ultrasonography reveals normal flow and
compressibility of the right subclavian, IJ and basilic veins.  A PICC line is
present extending to one branch of the brachial vein.  No clot is seen within
the region of the PICC.  However, distally, there is loss of flow on color
Doppler ultrasound and loss of compressibility.  There is mild echogenicity
within the vein at this level, within the antecubital fossa, which may
represent a thrombus.  The second branch of the right brachial vein is widely
patent.  The cephalic vein was not well visualized due to overlying edema.  No
focal fluid collections were detected.

FINDINGS:
There is still some free air under the diaphragm but less so than seen on the
prior study.  A right subpulmonic effusion is demonstrated.  Surgical clips
are noted in the left upper quadrant of the abdomen.  Some mild distension of
the pulmonary vasculature, particularly the left upper lobe pulmonary vessels
suggesting element of fluid overload.  Heart size remains somewhat enlarged.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH:


FINDINGS:
As compared to the previous radiograph, a PICC line has been placed
over the right upper extremity.  The tip of the line projects over the right
atrium, the line could be pulled back by approximately 5 cm.  There is no
evidence of complications, notably no pneumothorax.

The pre-existing free air on the right is no longer visible.  The referring
physician was paged and notified.

TECHNIQUE:
Sonographic images were obtained of the bilateral kidneys.

FINDINGS:
The right kidney is normal in appearance without hydronephrosis,
masses, or stones and measures 10 cm.  Note is made of prominent columns of
Bertin.  The left kidney is also normal in appearance measuring 10.8 cm in the
craniocaudal dimension, without masses, stones, or hydronephrosis.  A 1-cm
anechoic cyst is seen in the left upper pole.

The bladder demonstrates some irregular thickening at the inferior aspect,
possibly from treatment change or layering debris.  Limited images of the
gallbladder demonstrate no wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:


TECHNIQUE:
Multidetector scanning is performed from the diaphragm through the
symphysis during dynamic injection of 130 cc of Optiray.  No prior studies are
available for comparison.

DLP:
903.6 mGy-cm.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:
The lung bases are clear.  In segment VII
of the liver there is a 1.5-cm lesion which is hypodense and measures 58
Hounsfield units.  Emanating from the left portal vein and extending towards
the liver capsule there is a tubular hypodense area which may represent a
thrombosed portal vein branch.  There is some triangularly shaped area of
increased perfusion adjacent to it.  The gallbladder contains a high-density
material possibly vicarious excretion of contrast from prior CT examination. 
The spleen is normal in size.  The pancreas is unremarkable.  The duodenal
diverticulum is noted.  The adrenal glands are normal.  The right kidney is
unremarkable.  In the left kidney there is a mild hydronephrosis and there is
lack of excretion of the left kidney.  Only the cortex is enhancing.  No
contrast is seen in the collecting system as it is seen on the right kidney. 
In the upper pole of the left kidney there is a 0.9 cm hypodense lesion that
is too small to characterize.  The left ureter is mildly distended and can be
followed into the pelvis.  There is some fat stranding surrounding it.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:
There is massive wall thickening in the
sigmoid colon.  This is relatively hypodense.  In the sigmoid mesentery there
is a small collection that measures 2.5 x 2.3 cm and contains air inclusions. 
It has an enhancing rim and sits superior to the sigmoid colon.  A soft tissue
extending from the sigmoid colon to the bladder with enhancing fistula tract. 
Massive wall thickening of the bladder overlying the fistula tract.  This
measures about 4.0 cm in width and 1.5 cm in depth.  There is air in the
bladder.  The prostate gland is normal in size.  The wall thickening in the
colon is very eccentric and while the normal lumen of the colon is seen
towards the left side of the pelvis the wall thickening extends to the right
side and there is oral contrast seen within this area of the wall consistent
with a sinus tract.

On bone windows, there are no concerning osteolytic or osteosclerotic lesions.

RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND:
There are several well-circumscribed
echogenic round lesions in both lobes of the liver, three on the left and two
on the right.  The largest of these measures 1.6 x 1.3 x 1.2 cm in the right
lobe of the liver.  These lesions do not demonstrate internal vascularity,
although this assessment was somewhat limited by cardiac motion.  There is no
intra- or extra-hepatic bile duct dilation, and the common bile duct measures
3 mm.  The main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow.  The gallbladder
is  unremarkable without stones, sludge, wall thickening, or pericholecystic
fluid.  There is no ascites.  Limited evaluation of the pancreas due to
overlying bowel gas is unremarkable.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT of the neck was performed with 2.5 mm axial sections obtained
from the aorticopulmonary window through the mid orbital level, during the
dynamic IV administration of 70 cc of Omnipaque.  Reformatted coronal and
sagittal images were generated and reviewed.

DLP:
1003 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:
Evaluation of the aerodigestive tract demonstrates no exophytic
mucosal mass or mass effect.  Evaluation of the cervical lymph chains
demonstrate no pathologic lymphadenopathy by imaging criteria.  The thyroid
gland is normal.  The salivary glands are unremarkable in appearance.  The
neck vessels enhance bilaterally without significant stenosis or definite
evidence of dissection.

TECHNIQUE:
Contiguous axial MDCT images were obtained through the brain
without administration of IV contrast.  Reformatted coronal and sagittal and
thin section bone algorithm-reconstructed images were acquired.

DLP:
1003 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:
Area of hypodensity in the left frontal lobe involving gray-white
matter, concerning for cytotoxic edema in the setting of a subacute infarct. 
No definitive space occupying lesion is identified.  There is no evidence of
intracranial hemorrhage.  The ventricles and sulci are normal in size and
configuration. The basal cisterns appear patent. No fracture is identified. 
The visualized paranasal sinuses, mastoid air cells, and middle ear cavities
are clear.  The globes are unremarkable.

MRI OF THE BRAIN WITHOUT AND WITH CONTRAST, MRA OF THE BRAIN WITHOUT CONTRAST:


AND MRA OF THE NECK WITHOUT AND WITH CONTRAST, ___:


TECHNIQUE:
Routine ___ enhanced MR examination of the brain, comprising
T1-weighted axial SE and sagittal MP-RAGE sequences, post-contrast
administration, the latter with axial and coronal reformations.  Axial 3D- and
2D-time-of-flight MRA of the cervical and cranial vessels, respectively, and
coronal 3D VIBE MRA of the cervical vessels was performed during dynamic
intravenous contrast administration, with review of all axial and coronal
source and subtracted images, respectively, on a separate workstation.  In
addition, axial T1-weighted SE sequence with fat saturation was performed
through the cervical soft tissues, into slab acquisitions, prior to contrast
administration.

FINDINGS:
The study is compared with the cranial NECT and the cervical soft
tissue CECT, performed roughly 17 hours earlier.

Corresponding to the findings on the cranial CT is a somewhat rounded region
of T2- and FLAIR-hyperintensity involving left frontal gray and subjacent
white matter, with mass effect and effacement of the regional gyri.  This
process demonstrates no "blooming" susceptibility artifact to suggest blood
products and an unusual well-defined, ovoid 17 mm (AP), relatively "cystic"
focus, in its peripheral portion.  Allowing for the T2- "shine-through" of
both portions of this process, there is no focus of slow diffusion to suggest
acute ischemia.  The process demonstrates overall intermediate T1 signal,
other than in the more cystic component, above.  Following contrast
administration, there is only at most faint low-level enhancement of the
central portion of this process.  There is no pathologic parenchymal,
leptomeningeal or dural focus of enhancement, elsewhere.

Otherwise, there are only scattered both punctate and larger
T2-/FLAIR-hyperintense foci in bihemispheric, predominantly subcortical white
matter, without diffusion- or enhancing correlate; though nonspecific, these
likely represent sequela of chronic small vessel ischemic disease.  There is
no focus of slow diffusion, elsewhere.

There is normal flow-related enhancement in the included intracranial portions
of both internal carotid and proximal middle and anterior cerebral arteries. 
There is normal, symmetric arborization of MCA branches, with no significant
mural irregularity or flow-limiting stenosis.  There is normal flow-related
enhancement in the distal vertebral arteries, with dominant right and
hypoplastic left vessel, as well as the basilar and bilateral superior
cerebellar and posterior cerebral arteries, without significant mural
irregularity or flow-limiting stenosis.  Anterior and robust bilateral
posterior communicating vessels are demonstrated, with no aneurysm larger than
3 mm.

The axial fat-saturated and T1-weighted sequences demonstrate no abnormal
intramural hyperintensity associated with the cervical, vertebral or carotid
arteries to suggest blood products related to acute dissection.  The included
aortic arch and great vessel origins are unremarkable, without flow-limiting
stenosis.  The common and cervical internal and external carotid arteries are
normal in course, caliber, and contour.  They demonstrate normal flow-related
and contrast enhancement, without significant mural irregularity,
flow-limiting stenosis or evidence of dissection.  Slightly dominant right and
slightly hypoplastic left vertebral arteries demonstrate normal course,
caliber and contour from their subclavian origins through the vertebrobasilar
junction.  There is no significant mural irregularity, flow-limiting stenosis
or evidence of dissection.

TECHNIQUE:
Multi detector CT images were obtained from lung bases to the
proximal femurs after the administration of intravenous and oral contrast
material.  Multiplanar reformatted images in coronal and sagittal planes are
provided.

DLP:
___.___ mGy-cm

FINDINGS:
Please see the dedicated chest CT report for thoracic findings.

ABDOMEN:
The liver is normal in size and homogeneous in enhancement.  There
is a vague hypodensity in segment 4B which is too small to characterize(5:49),
and is of uncertain significance.  The portal and hepatic veins are patent and
there is no intra or extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  The gallbladder
is surgically absent.  The common bile duct is not dilated.  

The spleen is homogeneous in enhancement and normal in size.  The adrenal

FINDINGS:

FINDINGS:

Assessment of abdominal viscera is somewhat limited secondary to lack

Limited evaluation of the lung bases demonstrates minimal basilar atelectasis.

There is no evidence of worrisome lesions. Abdominal and pelvic wall is within

COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY OF THE THORAX:

The upper abdomen is described in detail in the abdominal CT report of the

text:
FINDINGS:
Gray-scale, color, and Doppler sonograms of the right subclavian,
axillary, brachial, basilic, and cephalic veins were performed.  There is
normal flow, compression, and augmentation seen in all of the vessels.  Note
is made that the right IJ was not imaged due to the presence of a line within

MDCT images are acquired from the lung bases to the pubic

provided for interpretation.

FINDINGS:
Direct comparison is made to a prior study dated ___.

Small bilateral pleural effusions are noted on the current exam with areas of
adjacent atelectasis.  Previously noted pneumoperitoneum is resolved. Numerous
small, hypoattenuating areas are again seen within the liver parenchyma which
are too small to characterize but likely represent simple cysts or
hemangiomas.

The adrenal glands are thickened without focal nodules seen.  The spleen and
pancreas appear grossly unremarkable.  Vicarious excretion of contrast is seen
within the gallbladder.  Numerous small, hypoattenuating areas are again seen
within the kidneys bilaterally which are too small to characterize but likely
represent simple cysts.

There is fluid predominantly within the pericolic gutters bilaterally which
appear to be loculated.  There is also small amount of fluid anteromedial to
the gallbladder.  This area measures 2.8 x 4.4 cm.  No significant peripheral
enhancement to suggest that this represents an organized abscess.

Evaluation of the pelvic structures reveals endometrial stripe to measure 6
mm.  Given the patient's age, pelvic ultrasound is recommended for further
evaluation of this finding.  The pelvic structures are otherwise grossly
unremarkable.  Post-surgical changes consistent with the patient's ___
procedure noted with soft tissue defect along the anterior abdominal wall.

No suspicious lytic or blastic bony lesions are identified.

ABDOMEN, SINGLE VIEW:
Distended and dilated loops of bowel are seen throughout
the abdomen. There is no gross osseous abnormality.

FINDINGS:
In comparison with study of ___, there is continued opacification
in the right mid lung zone consistent with atelectasis.  Streaks of
atelectasis persist at the left mid and lower lung zones.  Stable

Single portable AP chest radiograph.

FINDINGS:

There is mild bibasilar atelectasis and right lung scarring.  Stable elevation

SUPINE AND UPRIGHT VIEWS OF THE ABDOMEN:
In the left mid abdomen, a prominent
loop of bowel measuring up to 3.2 cm is noted, worrisome for obstruction.  Air
is noted throughout the bowel including the colon, extending to the rectum,
suggesting partial obstruction.  The descending colon appears decreased in
caliber, which could be related to wall thickening or peristalsis.

PA AND LATERAL VIEWS OF THE CHEST:
Lungs are clear without consolidation or
pleural effusion.  There is no pneumothorax. The heart size is normal.  There
is no hilar or mediastinal enlargement.  Pulmonary vascularity is normal.

In the upper abdomen, air-filled loops of bowel are noted.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the abdomen and
pelvis following administration of oral and intravenous contrast material.
Multiplanar reformatted images were generated.

CT ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:
At the lung bases, there is mild dependent
atelectasis, without consolidation or pleural effusion.  The heart size is
normal, without pericardial effusion.

In the abdomen, the liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, adrenal glands,
stomach, and duodenum are unremarkable.  The kidneys enhance and excrete
contrast symmetrically without hydronephrosis, stones, or renal masses.  At
the interpolar region of the left kidney, there is a 2.1 cm hypodensity with
intermediate attenuation characteristics.  There is no hydronephrosis or renal
stone.  The abdominal aorta and its major branches are normal, with trace
atherosclerotic calcification.  Small lymph nodes in the retroperitoneum and
mesentery do not meet size criteria for pathologic enlargement.

CT PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:
In the descending colon, there is a 10 cm segment
of asymmetric wall thickening and inflammatory change, centered around a
diverticulum, consistent with ____. A small amount of
extraluminal air and extraluminal fluid indicate focal perforation. The fluid
collection measures 1.1 x 1.5 x 2.6 cm. This does not have the appearance of
an abscess.

Elsewhere the bowel (for example, at the splenic flexure, and within the mid
small bowel), there are short segments demonstrating wall thickening, without
inflammatory changes.  These likely changes of chronic inflammatory bowel
disease, without active acute exacerbation.  By report, the patient has
undergone prior bowel resection and the right colon is absent. The anastomosis
is patent and there is no evidence of obstruction. Contrast material has
reached the rectum.

The urinary bladder, distal ureters, and prostate gland are unremarkable.
There is no free fluid in the pelvis.  There is no pelvic or inguinal
lymphadenopathy by size criteria.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is no fracture or worrisome bony lesion.  Soft
tissues are unremarkable.

CT PELVIS WITHOUT AND WITH CONTRAST:

TECHNIQUE:
Limited MDCT axial images were acquired through the pelvis prior
to intended drainage procedure.  Initial imaging was performed without
intravenous contrast.  Subsequently, 80 cc Omnipaque was injected
intravenously and scanning was again performed through the pelvis.  Coronal
and sagittal reformations were performed and submitted to PACS for review.  No
oral contrast was given.

FINDINGS:
This was originally intended for drainage procedure.  Preprocedure noncontrast
CT examination of the pelvis again showed numerous diverticula of the sigmoid
colon with bowel wall thickening of the mid sigmoid colon consistent with
____, with bulkiness in the region of abscess as shown on the prior
day's CT.  Informed consent for procedure had been obtained and preprocedure

collection on the noncontrast images, a contrast enhanced phase of imaging was
also acquired to confirm size and location of the collection, with coronal
reformations obtained.  These images confirmed that a left pelvic fluid
collection that had previously measured 3 cm has almost resolved since the
prior exam.  A tiny residual fluid focus is now seen along the sigmoid colon. 
A tiny fluid pocket measuring 1.1 cm at maximum is now seen at the location of
the prior fluid collection, now too small for image-guided drainage.  Trace
fluid in the pelvis is unchanged.

calcifications in the mid pelvis may represent calcified lymph nodes.

artery bifurcation.

PA and lateral chest radiograph.

Cardiac silhouette is enlarged but unchanged from ___.

noted within bilateral kidneys, which are stable since ___ and likely

CT OF THE PELVIS:
There is sigmoid diverticulosis with adjacent pericolonic
fat stranding and wall thickening, consistent with sigmoid ____.
Tiny locules of gas appear extraluminal, indicating microperforation (300B,
38).  A left adnexal cyst is once again noted and measures 20 x 20 mm,

FINDINGS:

placement of a right IJ catheter that extends to the lower portion of the SVC.

EXAM:

TECHNIQUE:
Following the administration of 130 cc of iodinated intravenous
contrast, 5-mm axial images were acquired of the abdomen and pelvis.  These
were reformatted in the coronal and sagittal planes.

FINDINGS:


LUNG BASES:
There is bibasilar atelectasis.  The visualized heart is normal
in appearance.

ABDOMEN:
The liver, spleen, gallbladder, pancreas, and adrenals are normal in
appearance.  The kidneys demonstrate symmetric contrast enhancement and brisk
excretion.  A 13-mm simple cyst is seen within the inferior pole of the left

PELVIS:

thickened.  A focus of gas is seen adjacent to the sigmoid, which raises

vacuum disc phenomenon and anterior osteophyte formation.  No concerning lytic
