it is not dilated and this likely represents a reactive change (61B; 13).

PELVIS:
The bladder, uterus, and rectum appear unremarkable.  There is no
free fluid or pelvic lymphadenopathy.

BONES:
There are no aggressive-appearing lytic or sclerotic lesions.

FINDINGS:
Right lower lobe streaky opacities are consistent with atelectasis.
Small bilateral pleural effusions are likely present.  Azygos fissure is again
noted.  Cardiac silhouette is normal in size.  No pneumothorax.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT axial images were acquired through the abdomen and pelvis
without administration of intravenous or oral contrast material.  Multiplanar
reformats were performed.

TOTAL DLP:
1107 mGy-cm.

ABDOMEN CT:
There is minimal bilateral lower lobe dependent atelectasis. 
Mitral annular and coronary artery calcifications are seen.  The heart is
mildy enlarged.  There is no pericardial effusion.  Compared to CT from ___, there is stable gynecomastia.

Lack of intravenous contrast material limits assessment of the abdominal
organs.  The liver, gallbladder, pancreas, and adrenal glands are
unremarkable.  The kidneys are slightly atrophic, but otherwise unremarkable. 
The spleen is mildly enlarged, measuring up to 16.7 cm (2:23).  The stomach is
grossly normal.

There is extensive wall thickening involving the cecum and proximal-to-mid
ascending colon with surrounding fat stranding, possibly secondary to
____ with mircoperforation versus colitis.  The distal most portion
of the terminal ileum is markedly thickened, possibly reactive from the
adjacent inflammatory/infectious process.  The remainder of the small bowel is
unremarkable.  There is a left inguinal hernia containing fat and loops of
distal descending and sigmoid colon, without wall thickening or fat stranding
to suggest strangulation (2:89).  Scattered high-density punctate foci
throughout the descending and sigmoid colon is likely related to ingested
content.  Similar high-density punctate structures are seen within loops of
small bowel (2:54).  There is thickening of the right anterior pararenal and
lateral conal fascia, without frank free fluid in the abdomen.  There is no
evidence of pneumoperitoneum or pneumatosis.  Multiple small retroperitoneal
and mesenteric lymph nodes do not meet CT size criteria.  Prominent pericecal
lymph nodes measure up to 9 mm (2:36).  The abdominal aorta is normal in
caliber.  Scattered aortic and bi-iliac artery calcifications are seen.

PELVIS CT:
There is a large bladder diverticulum arising from the left
posterolateral aspect of the bladder (2:66).  There is no free fluid in the
pelvis.  No pathologically enlarged pelvic lymph nodes are seen.

BONE WINDOW:
No suspicious lytic or blastic lesions are identified. 
Bilateral sacroiliac joint degenerative changes are noted.  There are
multilevel degenerative changes of the thoracolumbar spine.  There is also
grade 1 anterolisthesis of L4 on L5.

FINDINGS:
No dilated loops of bowel or evidence of free air is noted.  The
partially imaged lungs are clear.  No significant stool is noted.  Mildly
distended small bowel loops are noted.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were acquired through the abdomen and pelvis with IV
contrast.  Multiplanar reformations were obtained and reviewed.

FINDINGS:
The partially imaged lungs are clear.  The partially imaged heart
is unremarkable.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:
There is extensive intraperitoneal free
air in the upper abdomen. The liver contains several small hypodensities
(2:18, 25, 16), but which are too small to accurately characterize.  The
portal vein is patent without evidence of portal venous gas. The IMV appears
patent without gas or obvious thrombus.   The spleen, both adrenals, right
kidney, pancreas, and gallbladder are unremarkable.  The left kidney contains
a simple cyst in its upper pole.

Stomach, and small bowel are normal.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:
The rectum, bladder, uterus, and both
adnexa are unremarkable.  There is diverticulosis with ____ in
the sigmoid colon with fat stranding, macroperforation and active spillage of
fecal material into the pelvis. There is a small amount of free fluid in the
deep pelvis.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
The visible osseous structures show no suspicious lytic or
blastic lesions or fractures.

CHEST X-RAY REPORT:


TECHNIQUE:
Portable erect chest radiograph.

FINDINGS:
There is interval placement of a right-sided PICC line that appears
to terminate in the right atrium, pulling the catheter back 2 cm will ensure
that the tip is in the distal third of the SVC.  Lung volumes are slightly
low, but lungs appear better expanded compared to the previous study; there is
less crowding of the pulmonary vasculature and improved bibasilar atelectasis.
Cardiomediastinal contours are stable.  No pleural effusions and no
pneumothorax.

EXAM:
CT of the abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast.

TECHNIQUE:
64-row MDCT of the abdomen and pelvis was done with oral and
intravenous contrast.  Split bolus technique.  150 cc of Omnipaque. 
Multiplanar reconstructions.

DLP:
683 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:
The liver is normal in size with no focal mass or diffuse
abnormality.  There is no bile duct dilatation and the gallbladder is normal.

The pancreas is normal in size with no focal mass or diffuse abnormality. 
There is no peripancreatic stranding.

The spleen is not enlarged and appears homogeneous.

The adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

The kidneys are normal in size with no focal cortical mass, solid or cystic. 
There are equal and prompt nephrograms bilaterally.  The pelvicalyceal systems
and ureters are normal.

There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymph node enlargement or other
mass.  

The stomach and duodenum are normal.  The mucosal pattern of the jejunum and
ileum is normal with no signs of small bowel dilatation.  There is no
obstructing lesion in the colon.
The appendix is well visualized lateral and inferior to the cecum.  It
contains air within it.  It is of normal caliber with no primary or secondary
signs of appendicitis.  There is no periappendiceal stranding.  
In the left lower quadrant anterior to the sigmoid there is an area of
stranding with focal encapsulated fat within it with the classic appearance of
epiploic appendagitis.

In the pelvis there is no abnormal lymph node enlargement or other mass.  
The prostate is normal in size.  
The urinary bladder is unremarkable.  
There is small amount of free fluid in the rectovescical pouch.

TECHNIQUE:
PA and lateral chest radiographs were provided.

FINDINGS:
Lung volumes are low. There is no focal consolidation, pleural
effusion or pneumothorax.  The heart is normal in size.  The imaged upper
abdomen is unremarkable.

exam_name: CT ABD & PELVIS W & W/O CONTRAST, ADDL SECTIONS
text:
TECHNIQUE:
MDCT axial images of the abdomen and pelvis were obtained with and
without intravenous contrast.  Initial axial images were acquired in a
non-contrast phase followed by arterial, portal venous, and three-minute
delayed phase imaging through the liver.  Coronal and sagittal reformations
were prepared.

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH AND WITHOUT INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
Minimal
atelectasis is identified at the left lung base.  The imaged cardiac apex is
within normal limits.

A tiny hypedense focus in the gallbladder is similar to prior examination and
may represent a small stone or polyp.  Correlation with outside hospital right
upper quadrant ultrasound is recommended (3B:188).  The gallbladder is not
distended.  The adrenal glands are symmetric without focal nodule.  There is
symmetric enhancement of the kidneys without suspicious focal lesion or
hydronephrosis.  Previously seen hypoenhancement of the right kidney is no
longer evident and previously may have reflected a focal infection.  No focal
pyelonephritis or infarction is identified on the current examination.  The
pancreas is normal.  The abdominal aorta and branch vessels are non-aneurysmal
and grossly patent.  There is no abdominal free fluid or free air.  The
stomach and small bowel loops are normal in caliber and configuration without
evidence of obstruction or inflammation.  The appendix is well visualized and
is normal.  There are scattered mesenteric lymph nodes, though none are
pathologically enlarged by CT size criteria.  The rectum and colon are normal
in caliber and configuration without evidence of obstruction.  There are
scattered diverticula throughout the sigmoid colon, however, one large sigmoid
diverticulum appears acutely inflamed (3b:288).  No surrounding fluid or free
air is identified to suggest perforation.  The bladder is distended and
appears normal.  Prostate and seminal vesicles are unremarkable.  There is no
pelvic free fluid.  No suspicious pelvic adenopathy is identified.

LIVER:
The liver has a nodular heterogeneous appearance, findings consistent
with the history of cirrhosis.  There is evidence of portal hypertension
including splenomegaly measuring 15 cm.  Known thrombus within the anterior
and posterior branches of the right portal vein appears similar to the prior
examination.  Previously seen possible thrombus within the central portion of
the left portal vein is no longer evident.  There is a tiny focus of arterial
enhancement within segment V/VI (3A:49) with no clear correlate on delayed
phase imaging, likely a small perfusional anomaly.  No lesion concerning for
hepatocellular carcinoma is identified.  Adenopathy is seen in the region of
the porta hepatis with a representative lymph node measuring 1.9 x 1.2 cm,
similar to prior examination.

CTA:
The celiac axis and branch vessels are widely patent and demonstrate
normal conventional anatomy.  The SMA and bilateral single renal arteries are
also widely patent.  There is mild infrarenal atherosclerotic plaque within
the non-aneurysmal aorta.  The ___ is also patent.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:
No bone destructive lesion or acute fracture is
identified.

FINDINGS:
Frontal and lateral views of the chest showed no acute
cardiopulmonary process.  The pleural and pulmonary structures are
unremarkable.  Prominence of the right pulmonary artery is unchanged from
___.  The aorta is tortuous and the cardiac silhouette is normal.  There is
no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  No focal consolidation is evident.  A VP
shunt catheter is seen coursing along the right hemithorax.  Interval rib
fracture seen on left ___ and 7th ribs with healing callus.  Degenerative
changes of the glenohumeral joint and right acromioclavicular joint are again
noted.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained from the lung bases to
the pubic symphysis following the uneventful administration of 100 cc
Visipaque intravenous contrast.  Coronally and sagittally reformatted images
were generated and reviewed.

FINDINGS:


CT ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST:
Although this study is not tailored for the
evaluation of supradiaphragmatic contents, the visualized lung bases show
posterior dependent positional changes but no pleural effusion, focal
consolidation, or pulmonary nodules.  Limited evaluation of the heart shows no
pericardial effusion.  The descending thoracic aorta shows extensive atheroma
and calcified plaque narrowing the vessel lumen (2:5).

The liver enhances homogeneously without perfusion defects or focal liver
lesions.  The portal venous system opacifies satisfactorily with contrast.  No
intra- or extra-hepatic biliary dilation is seen.  The patient is status post
cholecystectomy.  A right-sided ventricular shunt catheter is unchanged in
position with the tip terminating anterior to the liver.  The pancreas is
fatty infiltrated but otherwise unremarkable.  The spleen and bilateral
adrenal glands are unremarkable.  Both kidneys enhance symmetrically and
excrete contrast normally without evidence of hydronephrosis or solid renal
mass.  The left kidney contains numerous subcentimeter hypodensities in the
cortex which are too small to fully characterize by CT.

The stomach and intra-abdominal loops of small and large bowel are
unremarkable without evidence of wall thickening or obstruction.  No free air
or ascites is present.  There is extensive atherosclerotic disease of the
descending aorta with ectasia of the distal infrarenal portion measuring 2.5 x
2.3 cm (2:41), which is not significantly changed from ___.  An
uncomplicated 6.5 cm fat-containing ventral hernia is noted through which the
VP shunt courses.

CT PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:
The patient is status post hysterectomy.  The
urinary bladder and rectum are unremarkable.  A left likely ovarian cyst is
increased in size from both prior studies, now measuring 6.2 x 3.6 cm (2:63),
which previously measured 3.0 x 2.5 cm in ___ and 1.5 x 1.1 cm in ___.  The
sigmoid colon contains multiple diverticula and a 5.5 x 4.2 x 3.1 cm rim
enhancing thick-walled collection of air and fecalized material with no
definite tract to the adjacent sigmoid colon.  This rim-enhancing collection
is closely approximated to the left posterior dome of the urinary bladder and
the sigmoid colon without evidence of air in urinary bladder to suggest
fistula.  There is pericolonic mesenteric fat stranding in this region.  There
is no free pelvic fluid or inguinal/pelvic lymphadenopathy.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is grade 1 anterolisthesis of L5 on S1 and
multilevel severe degenerative changes in the lumbar spine with loss of
intervertebral disc height, endplate sclerosis and osteophytosis.  No
suspicious lytic or sclerotic lesions are identified in the bone.

STUDY:
Transvaginal sonogram for the purposes of transvaginal diverticular
abscess drainage.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were obtained from the base of the lungs through the
pubic symphysis after the administration of oral and intravenous contrast. 
Reformatted coronal and sagittal images were also reviewed.

FINDINGS:
The bases of the lungs are clear.  The visualized heart and pericardium are
unremarkable.

CT ABDOMEN WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
The liver enhances homogeneously with
no evidence of focal lesions.  There is no intra or extrahepatic biliary
ductal dilatation.  The gallbladder is unremarkable.  The portal vein is
patent.  The spleen, bilateral adrenal glands and pancreas are normal in
appearance.  The kidneys present symmetric nephrograms, however the left
kidney is somewhat atrophic and there is a small amount of perinephric fluid,
likely chronic.  Additionally, there is a 8 mm cyst in the upper pole of the
left kidney which is unchanged compared to prior studies with minimal internal
complexity.  There are also 2 nonobstructing renal calculi in the left lower
pole (2:34), also unchanged.  Within the right kidney, multiple subcentimeter
cystic lesions are unchanged and are too small to characterize.  The stomach,
duodenum and small bowel are unremarkable with no evidence of wall thickening
or obstruction.  The intra-abdominal loops of large bowel are unremarkable
with no evidence of obstruction.  There is no intraperitoneal free air or free
fluid. 

There is no retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  The
intra-abdominal vasculature is significant for dense atherosclerotic
calcifications within the abdominal aorta, common iliac, internal and external
iliac arteries.

CT PELVIS WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
There is wall thickening and surrounding
inflammatory fat stranding along the sigmoid colon with a rim enhancing fluid
collection between the sigmoid colon and superior wall of the bladder which
measures 5.2 x 1.5 x 4.7 cm, compatible with perforated ____
(601b:28, 602b:44).  Chronic inflammation of the sigmoid colon with a
wide-mouth diverticulum or intramural fluid collection has been present since
___, but now this collection appears larger in size with an air-fluid
level and complete transgression of the colonic wall (___:28).  The superior
wall of the bladder and an adjacent loop of ileum is thickened with
surrounding fat stranding, due to reactive inflammatory change, with no
evidence of fistulous connection.  There is no pelvic free fluid.  There is
persistence of a 4 mm calcification adjacent to the right ureterovesicular
junction, unchanged since ___.  Calcifications are noted within the
prostate.   There is no pelvic sidewall or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
No lytic or blastic lesions suspicious for malignancy is
present.

EXAM:
Chest single semi-upright portable view.

FINDINGS:
Single semi-upright portable view of the chest was obtained.  There
are areas of linear/streaky bibasilar opacity.  No focal consolidation is
seen.  There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  The cardiac and
mediastinal silhouettes are stable and unremarkable.  There is no evidence of
free air beneath the diaphragms.

FINDINGS:
A single supine frontal radiograph of the abdomen demonstrates a nonspecific
bowel gas pattern.  Oral contrast is seen within the cecum and transverse
colon as well as the rectum.  A surgical drain overlies the left lower
quadrant.  Skin staples are seen overlying the midline.  No large collection
of free intraperitoneal air is identified.

TECHNIQUE:
Axial CT images through the abdomen and pelvis were obtained
without intravenous or oral contrast administration.  This was followed by
axial CT imaging through the pelvis after instillation of contrast into the
bladder via the Foley catheter.  Sagittal and coronal reformats were made.

DLP:
905.5 mGy-cm

FINDINGS:


LUNG BASES:
Atelectasis and a small right pleural effusion is seen at the
right lung base.

ABDOMEN:
The lack of iv contrast limits the examination of the solid viscera.
The liver, spleen, adrenals, gallbladder and biliary tree, pancreas appear
unremarkable.  The right kidney is within normal limits.  The left kidney
demonstrates nonobstructing calculi in its lower pole.  The largest measures 8
mm.  

Contrast is seen within the small and large bowel related to previous oral
contrast from the ___ CT. There is a colostomy within the left lower
quadrant. The upstream bowel appears unremarkable. In particular, there is no
evidence of a bowel obstruction. There is a small amount of free fluid within
the small bowel mesentery.

Aortic atherosclerosis, severe. Severe iliac atherosclerosis.

PELVIS:
A surgical drain sits within the pelvis.  There is persistent
inflammatory stranding within the pelvis, most marked surrounding the
rectosigmoid stump as well as the adjacent regional small bowel loops. The
rectum contains contrast material intermixed with stool.  While there is fluid
in the rectovesical pouch, there is no drainable abscess or fluid collection. 

There is a Foley catheter within the bladder.  The bladder contains air.  CT
cystogram demonstrates no fistulous communication between the bladder and
adjacent bowel. There is no evidence of extra vesicular contrast material.
There is a small left bladder diverticula. 

The prostate contains some calcifications.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:
Surgical clips are seen within the anterior abdominal
wall related to recent surgical intervention.  There is a left ischial
sclerotic focus, most compatible with a bone island.

STUDY:
Portable AP upright chest radiograph.

FINDINGS:
The heart size is large.  The mediastinal contours demonstrate
prominence of the SVC and azygous contours.  The perihilar regions demonstrate
vascular prominence and such is noted throughout the lung fields.  There is no
large pleural effusion or pneumothorax.

TECHNIQUE:
Multidetector CT-acquired axial images were obtained from the lung
bases to the level of the lesser trochanters following administration of oral
and intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformats were evaluated.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN:
There has been interval development of bilateral pleural effusions, larger on
the right side.  There is associated compressive atelectasis in both bases. 
No pericardial effusion.  Note is made of an 18 x 21 mm rounded density in the
left breast.  Of note, the patient has had recent mammography to further
characterize.  
There are no focal liver lesions.  A small amount of focal fatty infiltration
is noted adjacent to the falciform ligament (series 2, image 23).  Normal
appearance of both kidneys and both adrenal glands.  Normal appearance of the
spleen.  There is fatty infiltration of the pancreas.
The gallbladder is normal in size with a subtle hypodensity noted lying
dependently in the gallbladder body which may represent biliary sludge or a
small calculus.  Ultrasound may be of benefit to further characterize.  Note
is made of a small hiatal hernia.  Otherwise, the stomach and small bowel
outline normally.

CT OF THE PELVIS:
Foci of  uterine calcification are noted, likely within
fibroids.  There has been slight decrease in size of the complex
multiloculated pelvic fluid collection.  The collection has decreased in size
in maximal axial dimension from 6.6 x 2.7 cm to 5.6 x 2 cm (series 2, image
57).  The collection again tracks inferiorly along the right side of the
pelvis with a small focus of fluid lying adjacent to the lower rectum (series
2, image 67).  Again, this collection is not amenable to percutaneous drainage
given the collection position is surrounded by the bony pelvis and adjacent
small bowel loop. A small new pocket of fluid(measuring 2 x2.8 cm )is
identified at the uterine apex.
Multiple tiny pockets of fluid and gas are again adjacent to the inflamed
sigmoid colon.
Anasarca is seen involving the soft tissues of the lower pelvis.  
No pathologically enlarged inguinal or pelvic sidewall lymph nodes are
identified.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is lumbarization of S1.  Degenerative changes are
seen involving T10-T11 with anterior bridging osteophytes.

TECHNIQUE:
Portable chest x-ray.

FINDINGS:
Tip of the PICC line is at 10.6 mm within the left-sided
brachiocephalic vein.  Bibasilar opacities are consistent with a combination
of pleural effusions and basal atelectases.  Mediastinal vessels are engorged.
Cardiac size top normal, although the study is not appropriate for assessment
of heart size.

TECHNIQUE:
Portable chest x-ray.

FINDINGS:
The tip of the right side-placed PICC line is observed at least 5.5
cm into the left brachiocephalic vein.  There are bibasilar opacities
consistent with bilateral pleural effusions and atelectasis at the bases of
lungs, unchanged from prior exam.

IMPRESSION;:
1.  Tip of the PICC line 5.5 cm within the left brachiocephalic vein.
2.  Bilateral pleural effusions with attendant bibasilar atelectasis.

ONE VIEW OF THE CHEST:
The lungs are low in volume and show bilateral interstitial opacities.  Also
noted is a more confluent opacity in the left lower lobe.  The cardiac
silhouette is enlarged.  The mediastinal silhouette is normal.  The hilar
contours are prominent.  No definite pleural effusions are present.  No
pneumothorax is present.  An ET tube terminates 8 mm above the carina and
should be pulled back by 2 cm.  The stomach is mildly dilated.

ONE VIEW OF THE CHEST:
The lungs are low in volume and show mild bilateral focal airspace opacities
along with more confluent opacities in the right upper, lower and left lower
lobes.  The cardiac silhouette is enlarged.  The mediastinal silhouette and
hilar contours are normal.  No definite pleural effusions are present.  A
right-sided PICC line terminates with its tip in the proximal SVC, unchanged. 
No pneumothorax is present.

FINDINGS:
The right kidney measures 10.6 cm.  

The left kidney measures 10.3 cm.

Bilateral kidneys are normal with no evidence of hydronephrosis, stones, or
masses.  The bladder is only moderately well seen and fully evaluated.

EXAM:
Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis.

TECHNIQUE:
64 slice MDCT data were acquired from the abdomen and pelvis after
the administration of intravenous contrast.  Images were viewed in multiple
planes.

FINDINGS:


ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST:
There are dependent atelectatic changes in both lower
lobes.  No pleural effusion is present.  A sub-cm hypodensity in the dome of
the left lobe of the liver is too small to characterize, but likely benign.
Remainder of the liver is unremarkable.  The gallbladder, pancreas, spleen,
and adrenal glands are normal.  The kidneys enhance and excrete contrast
symmetrically.  The stomach and abdominal loops of small bowel are normal. 
There is no free air or free fluid. Abdominal aorta is normal in caliber. No
pathologically enlarged mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymph nodes are present.

PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:
There are multiple diverticula within the sigmoid colon
with a focal, approximately 9-cm inflamed segment of sigmoid colon
demonstrating marked wall edema, thickening, pericolonic fat stranding and
thickening of the sigmoid mesocolon compatible with ____. 
There is an air and fluid collection in the mid pelvis adjacent to the
inflamed sigmoid colon measuring 3 x 5 cm (2:68) which demonstrates mild rim
enhancement. Two other potential rim-enhancing lobulated collections are also
demonstrated within the wall of the thickened segment of sigmoid colon which
may represent small intramural abscesses measuring up to 2-cm(2:69 and 70). An
adjacent loop of small bowel which courses in the vicinity of the sigmoid
____ demonstrates mural edema (301B:31, 301B:44).  There is no free
pelvic fluid.  There is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

BONE WINDOWS:
There are no suspicious sclerotic or lytic lesions.  There are
no fractures.

TECHNIQUE:
Limited non-contrast followed by post-contrast imaging of the
lower abdomen and upper pelvis was performed to assess for feasibility of
abscess drainage.  100 cc of IV Optiray was administered.

FINDINGS:
As seen one day previously, there are multiple diverticula within
the sigmoid colon and a 9 cm inflamed segment of sigmoid colon demonstrating
marked wall edema thickening and pericolonic fat stranding, compatible with
____.  The previously seen air and fluid collection just
anterior to a sigmoid colon has decreased in size, now measuring 3 x 1.9 cm,
previously 5 x 3 cm (3:14) - the decrease in size  suggests communication with
the bowel and auto-decompression.  There is also a markedly inflamed loop of
small bowel anterior to this focus of air and fluid, making percutaneous
drainage now unfeasible.

There are also likely two small fluid collections within the wall of the
sigmoid colon likely representing intramural abscess (3:19 and 20).  There is
a small amount of free fluid within the pelvis.

TECHNIQUE:
Multiple MDCT axial images were obtained from the lung bases
through the proximal thighs after the administration of 130 cc of Optiray
intravenously.  Enteric contrast was not given.  Multiplanar reformats were
derived.

FINDINGS:


CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
In the visualized chest, there is mild bibasilar atelectasis, but no pulmonary
mass, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax.  There is a persistent right lower
lobe hyperdense foci, likely a granuloma.  The heart is normal in size and
there is no pericardial effusion.

In the abdomen, the liver, spleen, pancreas, and adrenals are normal. There
has been a cholecystectomy. There is a 4.6 cm hypodense lesion on the anterior
aspect of the left kidney in the interpolar region (2:30).  The cyst is simple
in appearance without septation or wall nodularity.  Other hypodensities are
seen in the kidneys bilaterally, too small to characterize, statistically
likely to be benign cysts.  The kidneys symmetrically take up and excrete
contrast without hydronephrosis.

In the left flank, there is a large 3.5 cm diameter spherical lesion with
internal stool and florid circumferential inflammatory fat stranding (2:51,
300B:29). Coronal reformations demonstrate a channel between the spherical
lesion and proximal small bowel (301B:54) suggesting that this is a small
bowel ____. Inside this lesion is a mixture of air and apparently
fecalized matter.  There is no definite microperforation.  There is no
abdominal free fluid. Mesenteric nodes are prominent by number (not size)
about this inflamed diverticulum (2:53; 300b:27)

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
There is extensive sigmoidal diverticulosis without evidence of
____.  The bladder and distal ureters are normal.  There is a penile
prosthesis.  There is no pelvic free air, free fluid, or pathologic
lymphadenopathy.

MUSCULOSKELETAL:
There is no suspicious osteolytic or osteoblastic lesion. There is multilevel
spinal degeneration.

FINDINGS:
Two frontal views of the chest were acquired.  On one, lung volumes
are relatively diminished, and linear atelectasis is seen at the lung bases.
This resolves on the second view.  No consolidation or edema is evident. There
is mild tortuosity of the thoracic aorta with prominence of the aortic arch.
The cardiac silhouette is grossly stable accounting for AP portable technique
and lung volumes.  It is borderline enlarged.  No effusion or pneumothorax is
noted.  Clips consistent with prior cholecystectomy are noted in the right
upper quadrant.

CT SCAN OF THE TORSO PERFORMED ON ___:
Comparison is made with a prior study from ___.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT was used to obtain contiguous axial images through the chest,
abdomen, and pelvis following the administration of IV contrast.  Multiplanar
reformations were provided.

Non-contrast imaging through the chest was also performed.

FINDINGS:


CHEST:
Non-contrast imaging through the chest demonstrates no evidence of
intramural aortic hematoma.

Following the administration of IV contrast, there is no filling defect within
the pulmonary arterial tree through the segmental level to suggest the
presence of a PE.  The aorta is normal in course and caliber without evidence
of dissection or aneurysm.  A bovine arch configuration along the aortic knob
is noted.  There is no gross lymphadenopathy in the chest.

Lung windows are notable for bibasilar atelectasis.  No evidence of pneumonia.
No pleural effusion.

ABDOMEN:
Within the liver, radiodense Ethiodol is again noted within the left
hepatic lobe, compatible with prior embolization.  There is adjacent
hypodensity within the liver which is somewhat ill-defined, raising the
possibility of recurrent tumor.  A TIPS is in place.  Portal vein appears
patent.  Perihepatic free fluid is noted as well as locules of free gas.  The
spleen is enlarged with perisplenic fluid.  The pancreas appears grossly
unremarkable.  There is a left upper pole exophytic renal cyst which appears
grossly stable.  Small reactive retroperitoneal lymph nodes are noted.  The
abdominal aorta and major branch vessels are widely patent.  There is a
circumaortic left renal vein noted.  The stomach appears moderately distended

Chest, semi-upright AP portable.

FINDINGS:
A new left-sided PICC line terminates in the mid superior vena
cava.  A feeding tube courses into the stomach.  There are at least three
double pigtail catheters in the left upper quadrant.  A moderate left-sided
pleural effusion is probably unchanged in size with patchy associated opacity
suggesting minor atelectasis.  There is no pneumothorax.

TECHNIQUE:
Axial helical MDCT images were obtained from the suprasternal
notch to the pubic symphysis after administration of IV and oral contrast. 
Multiplanar reformatted images in coronal and sagittal axis were generated

FINDINGS:
Heart and lungs:  Limited assessment of the lung bases demonstrate no focal
opacity.  Again seen is a large nonhemorrhagic left pleural effusion which has
mildly increased in size. Mild decrease in the subdiaphragmatic fluid
collection with a peripheral enhancing irregular rim and locules of air which
is consistent for an abscess.  No pericardial effusion.  

Liver:  The liver is homogeneous without focal opacity.  No portal venous air
or pneumobilia.  No intrahepatic biliary duct dilatation.  The gallbladder is
thin walled with multiple calcified gallstones which are unchanged from prior
study.  The main portal vein and its major branches are patent.  

Pancreas:  Again seen are multiple pseudocysts. There has been interval
decrease in the pancreatic head pseudocyst which now measures 4.1 x 3.4 cm
(previously 5.3 x 3.7 cm)(4:33) as well as a 2.5 x 2.1 cm (previously 2.7 x
2.1 cm) (4: 42) pseudocyst in the uncinate. The pseudocyst in the pancreatic
body has slightly increased in size now measuring 1.8 x 1.0 cm (previously 1.3
x 0.5cm. Again seen is a drainage ___ is seen is tail pseudocyst which is
unchanged in size and measures 2.7 x 1.2 cm (previously 2.9 x 1.2 cm)(4:27).
No new focal solid or cystic lesions. No peripancreatic fat stranding.     

Adrenal gland:  The adrenal glands are unremarkable.  

Spleen:  The spleen is homogeneous and normal in size.  The subdiaphragmatic
abscess is superior and distinct from the spleen.  

Kidney:  Again seen is a 2.7 x 2.3 cm (previously 2.8 x 2.3 when measured in a
similar fashion) lobulated cyst in the left mid kidney.  No additional focal
cystic or solid lesions.  Symmetric nephrograms and excretion of contrast. 
The proximal ureters are normal in caliber.  No pelvocaliceal dilatation or
perinephric stranding.

GI:
A feeding tube courses through the esophagus with the tip in the mid
jejunum.  The stomach is non distended.  The duodenum, small bowel are normal
in caliber without focal wall thickening or obstruction.  Few diverticula
without ____ are noted in the sigmoid colon.  The rectum, descending
and distal transverse colon are normal in caliber without focal wall
thickening, fat stranding, or mass lesion.  Again seen is thickening of the
proximal transverse colon bowel wall which is unchanged from prior study with
preserved passage of contrast distally.  Previously identified inflammation
surrounding the proximal transverse colon is now more organized with enhancing
internal vessels suggestive of walled off fat necrosis. No pneumatosis.  

Vascular:  The descending aorta and its major branches are normal in caliber
and patent.  No aneurysmal dilatation of the descending aorta.  The IVC,
hepatic veins, splenic vein, SMV and renal veins are patent.  

Retroperitoneum and abdomen:  No retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymph node
enlargement by CT criteria.  No ascites, free intraperitoneal air or abdominal
wall hernia.  

Osseous structures:  Mild degenerative changes of the lumbar spine is noted. 
No focal lytic or blastic lesions suspicious for malignancy.  

CT pelvis:  Air is seen in the vagina.  The bladder is decompressed and the
terminal ureters are not visualized.  No inguinal or pelvic wall lymph node
enlargement.  No pelvic free fluid.

FINDINGS:
Supine and upright frontal images of the abdomen demonstrate a nonobstructive
bowel gas pattern with gas in a few nondilated loops of small bowel and stool
and gas in the colon, predominantly the ascending colon.  There are no
significant air-fluid levels.  There is no evidence of free air beneath the
right hemidiaphragm.  Multiple clips in the right upper quadrant of the
abdomen are compatible with prior cholecystectomy.  Surgical clips are also
noted projecting to the right of the lower lumbar spine.  The patient is
status post left posterior fixation of the L5-S1 vertebral level.  The imaged
lung bases are unremarkable.

TECHNIQUE:
Frontal and lateral views of the chest.

FINDINGS:
Right middle lobe linear atelectasis/scarring is again seen.  There has been
interval resolution of previously seen left lower lobe pneumonia.  No pleural
effusion or pneumothorax is seen.  The cardiac and mediastinal silhouettes are
stable.  No evidence of free air beneath the diaphragms.

text:
STUDY:
CT of abdomen and pelvis without and with IV contrast (130 cc of
Optiray intravenous contrast); coronal and sagittal reformatted images were
also generated.

FINDINGS:


ABDOMEN:
The lung bases demonstrate mild bibasilar atelectasis.

The liver demonstrates a subtly nodular appearance with caudate lobe
hypertrophy, commonly seen in cirrhosis.  Additionally, the portal vein
branches appear irregular in their course but are patent.  There is no
intrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder shows no stones or wall
edema.  The spleen is enlarged.

The pancreas shows no masses or duct dilatation.  In the left adrenal gland,
there is an 18 x 9 mm nodule.  There is a fat density, compatible with
adenoma.

The kidneys enhance with contrast symmetrically.  There is mildly delayed
excretion of contrast on the right.  Additionally, there is mild
hydronephrosis and perinephric stranding.  The right ureter is noted to be
mildly prominent along its course.  A 3 mm stone is seen in the distal ureter
(4; 60).

The aorta and IVC and their major branches appear patent.  The small and large
intestine shows no sign of obstruction.  There is no lymphadenopathy, free
air, or free fluid.

PELVIS:
The bladder and rectum appear unremarkable.  The contour of the
uterus suggests a fibroid at its right aspect.  Sigmoid diverticulosis is
seen.  Focal area of thickened sigmoid wall is noted (4; 70 and 500B; 33).
There is no evidence of perforation or organized drainable fluid collection.
There is mild fat stranding around it as well as a small amount of free fluid
in the pelvis.  No pelvic masses or lymphadenopathy are seen.

BONES:
Mild degenerative changes are seen in the form of bridging anterior
osteophytes at the T11-12 level.  There is also grade 1 anterolisthesis of L5
on S1 with disc space narrowing and endplate sclerosis suggesting this is a
chronic finding.

TECHNIQUE:
PA and lateral views of the chest.

FINDINGS:
Heart size is normal.  Mediastinal and hilar contours are within normal
limits.  Lungs are clear.  Pulmonary vasculature is normal.  No pleural
effusion or pneumothorax is seen.  There are no acute osseous abnormalities.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images of the abdomen and pelvis were acquired after
administration of intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformatted
images were reviewed.

FINDINGS:
Abdomen:  The lung bases demonstrate dependent atelectasis without pleural
effusion.  No pericardial effusion is seen.  No acute abnormalities are
detected in the liver, gallbladder, pancreas, adrenal glands, kidneys, or
visualized portions of the ureters.  The spleen is absent.  No abnormalities
are detected of the stomach, small bowel, or appendix.  Central abdominal
vasculature appears patent and normal in caliber with an IVC filter and a left
external iliac venous stent, as seen previously.  There is no ascites. 
Anterior abdominal wall hernia repair with mesh is again noted.

Pelvis:  The urinary bladder, prostate, seminal vesicles, and rectum are
unremarkable. Scattered diverticula are noted in the colon. There is mild wall
thickening of the sigmoid colon with adjacent fat stranding and fascial
thickening in a region of diverticula.  There are adjacent foci of
extraluminal air without organized collection compatible with perforation.

No acute bony abnormality is detected.

FINDINGS:
Three frontal abdominal radiographs show a normal bowel gas pattern without
dilated loops of bowel or air-fluid levels.  No free air or pneumatosis is
identified.  The visualized osseous structures are unremarkable.  A radiopaque
density in the right iliac wing represents a bone island.

EXAMINATION:
CT of the abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast.

TECHNIQUE:
Helically acquired axial images were obtained from the lung bases
to the pubic symphysis after the administration of 130 mL of Optiray
intravenous contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were obtained.

FINDINGS:


CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
Located in the region of the
descending colon, there is extensive fat stranding and fluid seen surrounding
a focal segment of colon with associated wall edema and diverticula noted
compatible with a focal segment of ____/colitis.  No discrete
abnormal fluid collections that would be concerning for abscess formation.

Other than dependent atelectasis, the lung bases are clear without
consolidations, pleural effusions, or pulmonary nodules.

The liver, gallbladder, spleen, both adrenal glands, both kidneys, other than
a subcentimeter too small to characterize hypodense lesion within the
interpolar region on the right, and visualized portions of intra-abdominal
small bowel are unremarkable.  There is no intra-abdominal free air.  There is
no mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
There is a small amount of pelvic
free fluid noted.  The rectum, sigmoid colon, bladder, uterus, and bilateral
adnexa are unremarkable.  There is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

BONE WINDOWS:
Visualized osseous structures are unremarkable with no
suspicious lytic or sclerotic foci.  There is minimal degenerative change as
manifested by marginal osteophytic formation.

TECHNIQUE:
MD CT axial imaging was obtained from the lung bases through the
pubic symphysis without the administration of intravenous contrast material
coronal and sagittal reformats were completed.

FINDINGS:


CT ABDOMEN:
There is a ground-glass opacity with ___ opacities in the
right lower lobe which may represent an atypical infection.  There is no
pleural effusion.  The visualized heart and pericardium are unremarkable.  The
patient is status post CABG.  

This study is limited for evaluation of the intra-abdominal solid organs and
vasculature without the administration of intravenous contrast material. 
Within these limitations noncontrast appearance of the liver is unremarkable. 
There are layering gallstones within the gallbladder.  The pancreas spleen and
adrenal glands are unremarkable.  A punctate nonobstructing stone is present
within the upper pole of the left kidney (2:31).  Small nonobstructing
calculus at the lower pole of the right kidney as well.  Other calcifications
may be vascular vs nonobstructing stone.  The stomach is fluid-filled.  There
are prominent fluid-filled this loops of small bowel that are only mildly
dilated which may represent enteritis.  There is a 4.5 x 4.3 cm low density
lesion, potentially a cyst arising from the interpolar region of the left
kidney.  The normal caliber aorta is densely calcified as are the major
branches including the celiac artery and the superior mesenteric artery. 
There is no free fluid, free air lymphadenopathy within the abdomen.

CT PELVIS:
The rectum is unremarkable there is chronic diverticulosis of the
sigmoid colon without ____.  Multiple calcifications within the
uterus are likely fibroids.  The bladder is partially distended.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There are no concerning osseous lesions.  Bilateral L5
spondylolysis noted with grade one anterolisthesis of L5 on S1.

TECHNIQUE:
Multi detector CT imaging was of the abdomen and pelvis was
performed without intravenous contrast administration.  Multiplanar reformats
were also obtained.  Oral and rectal water-soluble contrast was administered.

DOSE:
DLP of 1643.36 mGy-cm

FINDINGS:


ABDOMEN:
Patchy nodular areas of consolidation are identified along the right major
fissure in the superior segment right lower lobe (2:5).  Findings likely
represent an endobronchial spread of infection or aspiration. 

Within the limitations of a noncontrast study, the liver demonstrates normal
attenuation.  No focal hepatic lesions are identified.  The gallbladder is
slightly distended, demonstrating dependent calculi/ milk of calcium.  Mild
nonspecific gallbladder wall edema is identified.  No intrahepatic or
extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  The adrenal glands and spleen are
unremarkable.  Pancreas is slightly atrophic, however no focal lesions are
identified.  

A 3 mm nonobstructing calculus is identified at the lower pole calyx of the
right kidney (02:46).  A 5 mm slightly irregular calculus identified at the
upper pole calyx of the left kidney (02:35).  Additional foci of
calcifications within both kidneys likely relate to vascular calcifications. 
No hydronephrosis.  A small hiatal hernia is identified.  The stomach is
unremarkable.  Caliber of small bowel is within normal limits.  Moderate to
advanced atheromatous calcification of the abdominal aorta is noted. 
Calcification of the celiac artery, common hepatic artery, splenic artery, SMA
and origin of renal arteries is noted.  Calcification of the common iliac,
external iliac and internal iliac arteries is also noted bilaterally.  No
ascites.  No mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  Few prominent retroperitoneal
para-aortic lymph nodes are identified (02:39), with the largest measuring 1
cm.  Locules of air are identified in the subcutaneous tissues in the anterior
and right abdominal wall (2:79 and 2:66), likely related to subcutaneous
injections.

PELVIS:
Partially distended urinary bladder is unremarkable.  Few dystrophic
calcifications within the postmenopausal uterus, related to fibroids. 
Additional foci of calcifications in the uterus are likely vascular.  Mild
stranding is identified in the sigmoid mesocolon at the level of mid sigmoid
colon (2:68), extending into the left lower quadrant, slightly increased since
the CT abdomen study from ___.  There is evidence of sigmoid colon
wall thickening, which was present previously, likely chronic.  Moderate
sigmoid diverticulosis is identified.  No loculated fluid collections are seen
in the pelvis.  The appendix is unremarkable.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Bilateral pars defects are identified at the L5 level.  There is grade 1
anterior spondylolisthesis of L5 on S1.  No suspicious osteolytic or
osteoblastic lesions are identified.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH:


FINDINGS:
As compared to the previous radiograph, the lung volumes have
decreased and the size of the cardiac silhouette has increased.  Areas of
non-characteristic opacities are seen at both the left and the right lung
bases.  The extent and distribution of the changes favors atelectasis over
pneumonia.  In addition, there are signs of vascular distention and blood flow
re-distribution, suggesting mild-to-moderate pulmonary edema.  No larger
effusions are seen.  Patient has undergone sternotomy.

FRONTAL CHEST RADIOGRAPH:
Interstitial and airspace opacities are worse and
most easily explained by worsening moderate pulmonary edema.  As the heart
size is smaller than prior, though still mildly enlarged, a superimposed acute
process cannot be excluded.  Specifically, a more focal area of consolidation
in the left lower lung may represent aspiration, pneumonia or asymmetric
pulmonary edema and attention should be paid to this area after diuresis.  No
large pleural effusion.  No pneumothorax.

FINDINGS:
Portable radiographs of the abdomen demonstrate normal bowel gas pattern
without evidence of ileus or obstruction.  There is no pneumatosis or
secondary signs of free air.  Oral contrast is seen extending through the
colon and into the rectum, and is filling multiple diverticula.  Median
sternotomy wires are in place.  The visualized osseous structures are
unremarkable.

PORTABLE CHEST, ___:


FINDINGS:
Stable cardiomegaly accompanied by worsening combined alveolar and
interstitial pattern probably reflecting pulmonary edema, although co-existing
pneumonia in the left lower lobe is possible in the appropriate clinical
setting.

PORTABLE CHEST, ___:


FINDINGS:
Stable cardiomegaly accompanied by worsening asymmetrical perihilar
edema, right greater than left.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the abdomen and
pelvis with intravenous contrast.  Oral contrast preparation could not be
tolerated by the patient.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
Limited evaluation of lung bases
appears unremarkable with resolution of previously pleural effusions.

Pigtail catheter is noted within the left upper quadrant abscess, which
displays persistent thick rim enhancement and locules of air within it.  It
has significantly decreased in size, currently measuring approximately 2 x 8
cm, previously approximately 5 x 10 cm.  It is again noted to be intimately
associated with the splenic flexure of the large bowel and was previously
shown to communicates with the bowel itself.  Collection abuts the greater
curvature of the stomach which displays some reactive thickening and loss of
fat plane.  Remaining intra-abdominal contents appear unremarkable.  The
patient is noted to be status post splenectomy with the liver, the gallbladder
with small stones, pancreas, adrenal glands, and kidneys appearing
unremarkable.  Mild atherosclerotic disease is again noted within the
intra-abdominal aorta.  There appears to be a single take-off to the celiac
axis and the SMA.  No pathologically enlarged lymph nodes or free air is
present.  A prominent left pericardial 9 mm node is unchanged.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST ONLY:
Intrapelvic large bowel,
uterus, and adnexa as well as bladder appear unremarkable.  Fat-containing
bilateral inguinal hernias are present, larger on the right.

BONE WINDOWS:
Radiopaque spinal hardware is noted about the L4-5 spinous
process and there is bilateral pars defects involving the L4 with grade 1
anterolisthesis of L4 on L5 as well as vacuum phenomenon and loss of disc
space involving L4-L5 and L5-S1 and some of the upper lumbar vertebral bodies.
No malignant-appearing osseous lesions are noted.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were acquired from the lung bases to the lower abdomen
after only administration of water-soluble oral contrast (Gastrografin).  No
IV contrast was administered.  Multiplanar reformatted images were obtained
for evaluation.

CT ABDOMEN WITH ORAL CONTRAST ONLY:
There is a slight increase of small left
pleural effusion compared to ___, but moderate decrease from the
original study in ___.  Trace right pleural effusion is noted.

The absence of IV contrast significantly limits evaluation of intra-abdominal
organs.  Allowing for the limitations, the liver is grossly normal.  There are
at least two small, partially calcified gallstones in a non-distended
gallbladder, without secondary signs for acute cholecystitis.  The stomach,
duodenum, and visualized loops of small bowel are normal and patent with oral
contrast.  The adrenal glands and kidneys are grossly normal.  There is no
evidence of hydronephrosis, hydroureter or renal stone.  The patient is status
post splenectomy.  

In the left subdiaphragmatic region, there is a complex collection with an
indwelling pigtail catheter, now measuring 8.9 x 2.4 cm, compared to 8.4 x 2.4
cm previously on ___ x 5.4 cm on ___ in the original
study.  There is interval decrease in fluid content but increase fecal
material within the abscess.  The tail of the normal-appearing pancreas is
again noted abutting the collection.

The visualized colon remains normal, and oral contrast is seen reaching up to
the transverse colon but not yet reached the splenic flexure where the abscess
abuts.

There is no free intra-abdominal air beyond the collection.  No free fluid is
noted.  Mesenteric lymph nodes are small.

BONE WINDOW:
Multilevel degenerative changes are moderate-to-severe, with
unchanged grade 2 anterolisthesis of L4 on L5.  Metallic density posterior to
the L5 spinous process is unchanged.  Moderate calcifications are noted along
the descending aorta and its major branches.

FINDINGS:
In comparison with the study of ___, there are persistent low lung
volumes.  Poor definition of both hemidiaphragms with increased opacification
at the bases is consistent with a combination of atelectasis and effusion. 
Ill-defined pulmonary vessels are consistent with elevated pulmonary venous
pressure.  No change in the appearance of the monitoring and support devices.

FINDINGS:
In comparison with the study of ___, there is little change. 
Monitoring and support devices remain in place.  Persistently low lung volumes
with poor definition of the hemidiaphragms and increased opacification at the
bases consistent with a combination of atelectasis and effusion.  Some
elevated pulmonary venous pressure is again noted.

TECHNIQUE:
Contiguous axial images were acquired through the head without
intravenous contrast.

FINDINGS:
No intracranial hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, or masses are
detected.  There is an area of ill-defined cortical hypodensity involving the
left frontoparietal region (2:21).  No significant volume loss or mass effect
is noted in this region.  Given the history of hypotension and the lack of
prior imaging studies this finding most likely represents a subacute infarct.
Encephalomalacic changes are seen in the right occipital region relating to
prior insult.  A punctate hypodensity within the right thalamus (2:16) likely
represents a lacunar infarct.  The ventricles and sulci are mildly prominent,
consistent with age-related involutional changes.  Basal cisterns are widely
patent.

Opacification of bilateral mastoid air cells, right greater than left is
noted.  

The visualized paranasal sinuses are unremarkable.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were acquired through the chest, abdomen, and pelvis
after administration of oral and 130 cc of Optiray intravenous contrast. 
Sagittal and coronal reformats were generated and reviewed.

CT OF THE CHEST WITH INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
The major airways are patent up to
subsegmental levels bilaterally.  The endotracheal tube ends 3.7 cm above the
carina.  Right IJ line and right PICC end in the mid SVC. Bilateral pleural
effusions are present, moderate on the right and small on the left.  The left
pleural effusion has elements of loculation (2:21) without abnormal
enhancement , likely secondary to the recent surgery.  There is no
pneumothorax.  There is near complete collapse of the entire right lower lobe
with minimal dependent atelectasis in the left lung. These findings have
progressed since the pre-operative  CT scan of ___. Ground glass opacity
within the right middle lobe, likely represents atelectasis vs pneumonitis.

Multiple mediastinal lymphadenopathy is present, prevascular, right
paratracheal regions, maximally measuring 11 mm in the prevascular region
(2:20), not significantly changed since the prior study.  Incidentally noted
is fat density lesion within the inter-atrial septa, which may represent an
inter-atrial lipoma or fatty hypertrophy of the septum.  An epicardial lymph
node measuring 8 mm (2:40) is seen along the left lateral aspect of the
pericardium.  Mild atherosclerotic calcification of the thoracic aorta and the
coronary arteries are noted.  The ascending thoracic aorta maximally measures
3.5 cm. Incidental note is made of a hypoattenuating left thyroid nodule
measuring 2.1 x 1.6 cm (2:25).

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH ORAL AND INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
The liver demonstrates
homogeneous attenuation without focal lesions or intrahepatic biliary
dilatation.  The gallbladder is mildly distended with multiple gallstones. 
There is a moderate amount of free fluid along the inferior margin of the
liver extending into the pericholecystic region and tracking along the right
paracolic gutter into the pelvis.   The patient is status post splenectomy
with multiple enhancing rounded densities within the left upper quadrant,
compatible with splenosis.  There is a hypoattenuating fluid collection
(301:34) with peripheral rim enhancement, measuring 6.5 x 1.5 x 1.3 cm in the
left upper quadrant.  Mild fat stranding in the adjacent tail of pancreas,
could be a secondary to inflammation, however superimposed acute pancreatitis
cannot be excluded. There has been interval removal of a pigtail catheter
which was present in this collection.  Minimal amount of fat stranding and
fluid is seen along the entire left paracolic gutter, which likely relates to
the patient's recent left hemicolectomy.

The stomach and small bowel loops are unremarkable without evidence of bowel
wall thickening, obstruction, with the contrast reaching the right lower
quadrant ileostomy.  Incidental note is made of multiple duodenal diverticula
involving the second and third portion of the duodenum. Nasogastric tube ends
in the gastric body.

Both adrenal glands are unremarkable.  Both kidneys show symmetric
opacification and excretion of contrast without evidence of
hydroureteronephrosis.

There is no intra-abdominal free air.  The abdominal aorta demonstrates
diffuse severe atherosclerotic calcification without aneurysmal dilation.
Extensive calcification is seen in the iliac arteries, with significant
narrowing of the left external iliac and celiac axis. The celiac axis branches
are reconstituted via collaterals from the SMA. Significant narrowing of
bilateral common femoral arteries are noted.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH ORAL AND INTRAVENOUS CONTRAST:
The patient is status
post left hemicolectomy with a diverting ileostomy.  The visualized portion of
the large bowel appears unremarkable.  The pelvic loops of small bowel are
unremarkable except for mild focal thickening of a short segment of small
bowel loop in the pelvis adjacent to left pelvic drain.

Left pelvic drain loops within the pelvis with tip terminating in the left
flank. Minimal subcutaneous soft tissue stranding is present in the left flank
around the left drainage catheter, however no drainable fluid collections or
abscesses are detected.  Small amount of pelvic free fluid is present.  The
uterus and adnexa are unremarkable.  The urinary bladder is empty with a Foley
catheter in place, and air visualized within the dome of the bladder relates
to the catheterization.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES AND SOFT TISSUES:
The patient is status post spinal
instrumentation at L4/L5 level.  The changes of the thoracolumbar spine are
present, worse at  L4-5 and L5-S1 levels.  There is mild grade 1
anterolisthesis on L4-L5 level.

LEFT UPPER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND:
Limited targeted portable examination of the
left upper quadrant was performed to evaluate the fluid collection.  There is
redemonstration of an oblong fluid collection in the left upper quadrant
measuring 6.2 x 1.3 x 2.3 cm, corresponding to the collection seen insinuating
along the greater curvature of the stomach.  The collection is adequately
visualized, however, the surrounding structures including the pancreatic tail
and stomach, which are closely associated with the collection, are not clearly
visualized and it is felt that this collection would be more safely approached
via CT-guided drainage.

These findings were discussed with Dr. ___ at 2:30 p.m. on ___.

FINDINGS:
Right moderate pleural effusion is increased in size since ___ exam. 
Moderate left pleural effusion is unchanged.  Bibasilar atelectasis is
increased since prior study.  Hilar, mediastinal and cardiac silhouettes are
unchanged.  Moderate pulmonary vascular congestion is stable.

ET tube is 4 cm from the carina.  Right IJ tip projects over mid SVC.  NG tube
is in non-distended stomach.  Multiple surgical clips project over left upper
abdomen.

FINDINGS:
In comparison with the study of ___, the monitoring and support
devices remain in place.  Given the upright technique, there is probably
little overall change in the moderate-to-large right pleural effusion and
similar effusion on the left.  Enlargement of the cardiac silhouette persists
and there is continued elevation of pulmonary venous pressure.

FINDINGS:
Comparison to serial radiographs dating back to ___ and most
recently ___.

Bilateral moderately enlarged pleural effusions, left lower lobe atelectasis,
moderate cardiomegaly, left subclavian central venous catheter with its distal
tip projected over the mid SVC, the endotracheal and nasogastric tubes and
left upper quadrant abdominal surgical clips are unchanged since ___. 
There is no evidence of interval deterioration.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT helical acquisition was performed from the thoracic inlet to
the pubic symphysis following the uneventful administration of oral and IV
contrast.  Multiplanar reformations were provided.

CT CHEST WITH IV CONTRAST:
The patient has an endotracheal tube which
terminates 3 cm above the carina in satisfactory position.  Left internal
jugular line terminates in the mid superior vena cava.  A right upper
extremity PICC has been removed.  There is similar degree of right greater
than left pleural effusions, causing compressive atelectasis and right lower
lobe collapse as well as left lower lobe subsegmental atelectasis.  The
remainder of the airways are patent.  There is a similar appearance of small
focus of ground-glass opacity in the right middle lobe.

Mediastinal lymph nodes previously described are again both prominent in size
and number; aorticopulmonary window lymph node measures 2.0 x 1.0 cm (2:18). 
There is lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum.  Prominent
epicardial lymph node is again seen (2:38).  There is atherosclerotic
calcification of the thoracic aorta and the coronary arteries.  The previously
described thyroid nodule is again seen (2:2).

CT ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:
A nasogastric tube terminates in the stomach. 
The patient is post left colectomy, with a colorectal anastomosis which
appears intact (2:100).  A diverting ileostomy in the right lower quadrant
appears unchanged, and there is no evidence of bowel obstruction.  Oral
contrast reaches the ileostomy site.

In the left upper quadrant, the CT-guided drain has been removed at time of
colectomy, and the rim-enhancing abscess is approximately stable in size,
measuring 6.5 x 1.1 x 1.6 cm.  There is a similar degree of mild ascites in
the left upper quadrant tracking along the left paracolic gutter.  There is a
moderate degree of ascites in the right paracolic gutter.  

A surgically placed in the left lower quadrant loops superiorly and terminates
in the left mid abdomen (2:70).  Fluid has accumulated in the left lower
quadrant abdominal wall at site where drain enters, measuring 8.0 x 3.6 cm. 
This is somewhat ill-defined and may represent postoperative collection
measuring, with currently no thick enhancing rim to suggest abscess (2:91).

Inferior to the last midline abdominal wall staple, a 2.6 x 1.8 cm soft tissue
defect is filled with heterogenous material which may represent packing
material/gauze or debris, possibly even infected.  This determination could be
made on visual inspection, as it reaches the skin surface.

The liver is similar in appearance, without focal lesion.  The gallbladder is
not dilated, but again demonstrates multiple gallstones.  The patient is
status post remote splenectomy.  Mild fat stranding in the region of the tail
of the pancreas is unchanged and most likely reactive in this setting unless
there is concern for pancreatitis.  The kidneys enhance normally and excrete
IV contrast normally.  There is no intra-abdominal free air.

Atherosclerotic disease of the abdominal aorta and its branches is unchanged.

CT PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:
The colorectal anastomosis appears unremarkable. 
The uterus appears within normal limits.  No pelvic abscess is identified. 
There is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.  Small amount of pelvic free
fluid is similar to the prior study.  The urinary bladder demonstrates Foley
catheter and expected air.

Osseous structures again demonstrate instrumentation of the posterior elements
at L4-L5.  Degenerative changes at the lumbosacral junction appear similar,
with grade I anterolisthesis of L4 on L5.

CHEST SINGLE VIEW ON ___:


FINDINGS:
The endotracheal tube is 5 cm above the carina.  There are
bilateral pleural effusions slightly improved compared to prior.  There
continues to be pulmonary vascular redistribution and mild cardiomegaly
consistent with fluid overload.

CT-GUIDED DRAINAGE:
Informed consent was obtained from the patient's healthcare proxy over the
phone with two witnesses present.  The patient was placed supine on the CT
table in a slightly right decubital position and limited preprocedural CT scan
was obtained for procedure planning purposes.  This demonstrates persistent
moderate-sized right effusion with compression atelectasis involving portions
of the right lower lobe as well as small left effusion and lower lobe
atelectasis.  Clips from prior surgical procedure are noted and an orogastric
tube in place.  The overall size of the thick-rimmed left upper quadrant
collection abutting the greater curvature of the stomach displays no short
interval change from the most recent CT examination with surrounding

The overlying skin was prepped and draped in normal sterile fashion and
approximately 10 mL of 1% lidocaine was instilled into the local subcutaneous
tissues for local anesthesia.  Subsequently, under CT fluoroscopic guidance,
an 18-gauge ___ needle was advanced using an anterolateral approach into
the collection with aspiration of purulent material of approximately 3 cc
which was sent for culture and sensitivity.  The needle was removed and a
0.035 ___ wire was then advanced and coiled within the collection. 
Sequential tract dilatation with 6 and 8 ___ dilators was then performed. 
Using Seldinger technique, an 8 ___ ___ pigtail catheter was advanced
into the collection with the pigtail appropriately positioned as confirmed by
CT fluoroscopic images.  An additional 20 mL of bloody purulent material was
aspirated and discarded.  The catheter was placed to JP suction and secured to
the skin using a StatLock device and a sterile dressing was applied.  The
patient tolerated the procedure well with no immediate post-procedure
complications.

The patient came down to the CT interventional suite on Versed and fentanyl
which was continued to be administered by the ICU nurse during the procedure
for patient comfort.  The procedure was performed by Dr. ___ supervised
by Dr. ___ attending radiologist, who was present and participating
throughout.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH:


FINDINGS:
As compared to the previous radiograph, the monitoring and support
devices are in unchanged position.  Unchanged size of the cardiac silhouette,

Contrast-enhanced CT of the torso.

TECHNIQUE:
Contiguous axial images obtained from the lung apices to the pubic
symphysis after the administration of IV contrast.  Coronal and sagittal
reformations were obtained for review.

FINDINGS:


CHEST:
Since prior exam, the patient has been extubated.  The patient has a
nasogastric tube coursing through the esophagus.  There is right greater than
left pleural effusion with right lower lobe atelectasis and volume loss is
essentially stable since last exam.  There is a stable focus of ground-glass
in the right lower lobe.  There is a focus of high density in the medial left

versus aspiration of contrast.  Note is again made of prominent lymph node in
the aorticopulmonary window and lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial
septum. There is a prominent epicardial lymph node (2:41).  There is
calcification of the thoracic aorta and coronary arteries.  Thyroid nodule
seen on prior exam is again seen in the left lobe.

ABDOMEN:
The nasogastric tube terminates in the stomach. 

In the left upper quadrant there is a persistent rim-enhancing abscess.  The
collection is approximately stable in size since prior exam with interval
placement of CT-guided drain.  There is an increased area of fluid tracking
into the left paracolic gutter.

In the right upper quadrant along the anterior abdominal wall just inferior to
the liver margin is a 7.3 x 3.6 cm fluid collection with mild rim enhancement.
The fluid collection was seen on prior exam and essentially stable in size
with a mild increase in rim enhancement.  There is a mild degree of ascites in
the right paracolic gutter.

A surgically placed drain in the left lower quadrant has been removed since
prior exam.  The subcutaneous fluid collection in the left abdominal wall at
the site of surgical drain has since been debrided with an open wound now
present in the left abdominal wall.  A midline abdominal suture line has been
opened inferiorly with interval debridement of a 2.6 x 1.8-cm soft tissue
defect with heterogeneous material which was seen on ___.

No focal liver lesions.  The gallbladder has multiple stones but is not
dilated.  No evidence of cholecystitis.  The patient is status post
splenectomy with a small spenule visible.  Mild fat stranding in the region of
the tail of the pancreas is unchanged and most likely reactive in the setting.
The kidneys are normal in appearance and enhancement pattern.  There is no
intra-abdominal free air.  There is stable atherosclerotic disease of the
aorta and its branches.

PELVIS:
The patient is status post left colectomy with colorectal anastomosis
which appears intact (2:100).  Oral contrast reaches the ileostomy site.  The
uterus is within normal limits.  No pelvic abscess is identified.  There is no
pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.  Small amount of pelvic free fluid similar
to prior study.  Foley catheter in the bladder.

BONE WINDOWS:
Evidence of prior instrumentation of the posterior elements of
L4-L5. Degenerative changes at the lumbosacral junction appear similar with
grade 1 anterolisthesis of L4 on L5.

STUDY:
AP chest, ___.

Comparison is made to previous study from ___.

the lumbar spine.

AP chest, ___.

Comparison is made to prior study of ___.

The Dobbhoff tube has been readjusted and now is seen within the distal

Chest, PA and lateral radiograph obtained.

FINDINGS:
Comparison to recent radiographs dated ___.  The feeding tube
