exam_name: UNILAT UP EXT VEINS US RIGHT
text:
FINDINGS:
Grayscale and color Doppler sonograms were performed of the right
internal jugular, subclavian, axillary, brachial, and cephalic veins,
demonstrating normal color flow and compressibility.  There is occlusive
thrombus about an indwelling PICC along the entire extent of the right basilic
vein. There is symmetric color flow in the left subclavian vein.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were acquired from the thoracic inlet through the
pubic symphysis following administration of intravenous contrast.  Multiplanar
reformations were generated.

CT CHEST:
A 19-mm left thyroid nodule is unchanged.  The heart is normal in
size without pericardial effusion.  Multivessel coronary arterial disease and
mitral annulus as well as aortic valve calcifications are noted.  Multiple
small mediastinal and hilar lymph nodes are slightly smaller as compared to
___.  There is no axillary lymphadenopathy.  A small focal
ground-glass opacity in the right upper lung (2:32) appears unchanged. 
Bilateral pleural effusions with compressive atelectasis are improved since
___.  Central airways remain patent.

CT ABDOMEN:
The liver demonstrates no focal lesion.  A small gallstone is
present within an otherwise unremarkable-appearing gallbladder.  Patient is
status post splenectomy with residual splenic tissues in the splenic fossa. 
The pancreas appears slightly atrophic.  The adrenal glands are unremarkable. 
Bilateral kidneys appear minimally lobulated, but enhance symmetrically
without hydronephrosis or hydroureter.  There is no mesenteric or
retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.

A left percutaneous transabdominal drainage catheter terminates in a left
upper quadrant fluid collection that has significantly decreased in size since
___.  Mild stranding and a few foci of gas adjacent to the
catheter entry site are likely post-procedural changes.  Within the right
lower quadrant, there is a second percutaneous transabdominal pigtail catheter
within a separate fluid collection, which is also decreased in size since a
week prior.  No new focal fluid collection is identified within the abdomen.  

Patient is status post colectomy with an unremarkable appearing right-sided
diverting ileostomy and colorectal anastomosis (2, 107).  Small and large
bowel loops are normal in caliber.  Midline and left hemiabdominal wall
defects are persist, but appear smaller in size as compared to the most recent
prior exam.

CT PELVIS:
A triangular pocket of low-density fluid within the pelvis is
redemonstrated, similar in appearance as compared to ___.   The
bladder is partially collapsed with a Foley catheter in place.  Air is present
is present in the nondependent portion of the bladder, possibly related to
recent instrumentation, but unchanged.  There is no inguinal or pelvic
lymphadenopathy.  There is no free fluid within the pelvis.

BONE WINDOW:
No suspicious focal lytic or blastic lesions.  Severe multilevel
lumbar spondylosis, disc space narrowing, and vacuum phenomenon appear
unchanged.  Partial fusion of L3 and L4 vertebral bodies as well as grade 1
anterolisthesis of L4 on L5 are redemonstrated.  Hardware posterior to L5
spinous process is noted.

EXAM:
MRI brain.

TECHNIQUE:
T1 sagittal and FLAIR T2 susceptibility and diffusion axial images
of the brain were acquired.  3D time-of-flight MRA of the circle of ___
obtained.  Correlation was made with the head CT of ___.

FINDINGS:


BRAIN MRI:
There are several areas of hyperintensity on diffusion images in the left
parietal region, predominantly in the subcortical white matter as well as a
small focus in the left occipital region.  Most of these areas are isointense
on ADC map with several periventricular abnormalities, particularly in the
left periatrial region, are of low signal on ADC map indicative of subacute
infarcts.  There is no evidence of chronic blood products in the region. 
There is no evidence of mass effect or midline shift.  Mild-to-moderate
changes of small vessel disease and moderate brain atrophy identified. 
Extensive bilateral mastoid soft tissue changes are identified.  The
suprasellar and craniocervical regions are normal.  A chronic infarct is seen
in the right occipital lobe.

MRA HEAD:
The head MRA demonstrates absence of flow signal in the left internal carotid
artery indicative of occlusion in the neck.  There is flow signal identified
in the left middle cerebral artery, most likely due to collateral flow through
the anterior communicating artery.  There is no posterior communicating artery
identified on that side.  The right internal carotid, right middle cerebral
artery, both anterior cerebral arteries and posterior circulation arteries
demonstrate normal flow signal.

TECHNIQUE:
CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast.  No oral contrast was
administered.

FINDINGS:
Bibasilar atelectasis at the lung bases.  There is no pleural or
pericardial effusion.

There are two heterogenously hypodense liver lesions, one in segment VII
measuring 3.5 x 3.5 cm (2:14) and second near confluence of the portal vein,
measuring 1.8 x 1.8 (2:13); incompletely characterized on this single phase
study.  There is no evidence of intra- or extra-hepatic biliary duct
dilatation.  The gallbladder, spleen and bilateral adrenal glands appear
normal.  The pancreas, stomach and loops of small bowel are normal.  The
kidneys enhance symmetrically and excrete contrast symmetrically with no
evidence of hydronephrosis.  There is a left peripelvic renal cyst.  There are
small lymph nodes in the retroperitoneum; however, do not meet the CT criteria
for pathologic enlargement.  There is no free air or free fluid.

CT PELVIS:
There are scattered diverticula in the colon.  There is a segment
of the sigmoid colon (2:56), with marked wall thickening and adjacent mild fat
stranding which could be due to ____; however, an underlying
mass is not excluded.  No free air or drainable collection is seen. There is
no free fluid in the pelvis.  There is a 4 x 3 cm hypodense lesion in the left
adnexa (2:62); incompletely characterized.  The urinary bladder and loops of
small bowel appear normal.  There are no pathologically enlarged lymph nodes
in the pelvic or inguinal area according to CT size criteria.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
No suspicious lytic or sclerotic lesions are seen.  There
are severe degenerative changes in the thoracolumbar spine.  There is
compression deformity of L1 with angulation at this level (300b:37), which
appears chronic; however, unable to determine chronicity since no prior images
are available for comparison.

FINDINGS:
Two views of the chest are reviewed without comparison.  The lungs
are clear, but the lung volumes are low.  The heart is mildly enlarged with a
left ventricular configuration and the aorta is tortuous.  The pulmonary
vasculature is normal.  There is diffuse demineralization.  There is deformity
of the right humeral head.  Surgical clips are present in the right upper
quadrant.

TECHNIQUE:
Non-contrast MDCT of the lumbar spine displayed in multiplanar
collimation and reconstructions

FINDINGS:
The patient is status post L2 and L3 with posterior fusion rods and
pedicle screws. There are multilevel degenerative changes with diffuse
osteopenia.  The patient is status post laminectomies L2 to S1 with associated
scar tissue in the surgical bed.  The patient is status bone graft harvest
right iliac.

At T9 to T11, there are mild-to-moderate degenerative changes with mild
posterior disc bulges.

At the T11-T12 level, there is mild canal stenosis secondary to broad- based
posterior disc bulge and thickening of the ligamentum flavum.  There is
bilateral moderate neural foraminal compression.

At T12-L1, there are mild degenerative changes.  The exiting neural foramina
appear patent.

At L1-L2, there is intervertebral disc space narrowing with endplate sclerosis
and subchondral cyst formation with vacuum disc phenomena. There is severe
neural foraminal stenosis bilaterally, but worse on the right.

At L2- L3, there is grade I anterolisthesis.  The patient is status post
posterior fusion.  The neural foramina are patent.  There is a loss of the
intervertebral disc at this level with partial fusion.

At L3-L4, there is near complete fusion of the vertebral discs.  The neural
foramina are grossly patent.

At L4-L5, there are severe degenerative changes, including intervertebral disc
space narrowing, endplate sclerosis, osteophyte formation, and subchondral
cyst formation.  There is significant narrowing of the left neural foramen.

L5-S1, there are severe degenerative changes, but the exiting neural foramina
are patent. There is no canal stenosis.

There is an abnormal soft tissue structure in the deep right pelvis measuring
5.0 x 3.8 cm abutting a thickened rectosigmoid.  There is associated
inflammatory fat stranding.  In the ___ this process is a 16 mm round
cystic structure.  The ureter courses into this mass and is compressed.  The
proximal ureter is dilated and there is moderate hydronephrosis.  Given the
position of this cystic structure in relation to the proximal ureter, this may
represent dilation of the ureter within this structure.

The patient is status post cholecystectomy. There is atherosclerotic disease
of the aorta and major branches.  There is mild bibasilar atelectasis with
small right pleural effusion.  Note is made of a neural stimulating device.

No suspicious lesions are identified in the bones.  Please note that CT can be
insensitive for evaluation of multiple myeloma.

FINDINGS:
There is evidence of moderate hydronephrosis and proximal
hydroureter on the right side.  The most proximal portion of the right ureter
was evaluable; however, the mid and the distal portions could not be
evaluated.  There is no hydronephrosis on the left side.  There are no renal
calculi.  No renal masses or perirenal fluid is identified.  The right kidney
measures 9.14 cm.  The left kidney measures 9.8 cm.  The bladder is moderately
distended.  There is no evidence of bladder masses.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT-acquired axial images from the lung bases to the pubic
symphysis were acquired with oral contrast material and without IV contrast
material due to renal failure.

CT ABDOMEN WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:
There are minimal bilateral basilar
atelectatic changes.  The patient is status post cholecystectomy.  There are
marked atherosclerotic coronary calcifications.  The heart is normal in size
and the pericardium is unremarkable.  Within the limitations of a non-contrast
study, further limited by streak artifacts from cholecystectomy clips, the
outline of the liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands, stomach, and small and
large bowel loops is unremarkable.  There is moderate right-sided
hydronephrosis and hydroureter.  There is no perirenal fluid.  The contour of
the left renal cortex is bulging in the interpolar region.  A lesion in this
location is possible and would not be detectable with non-contrast study.
There is no abdominal ascites.

CT PELVIS WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:
There is a large soft tissue abnormality
measuring approximately 7 x 5 cm in the axial plane centered along the course
of the sigmoid colon.  The evaluation of this abnormality is extremely limited
due to the absence of oral contrast in this location as well as absence of IV
contrast.  There is probable extraluminal air and there is a small adjacent
fluid collection measuring 1.1 x 0.9 cm (2:62).  Given the limitations of the
study, it is unclear whether the uterus is involved, and if an area of
multiple small pockets of air is extraluminal or intraluminal  (2:68)  The
bladder wall abutting the soft tissue abnormality is slightly thickened. There
is no air within the bladder to suggest the presence of a fistula at this
point.  The rectum appears unremarkable.

BONE WINDOWS:
There is a left-sided total hip endoprosthesis.  There are old
fractures of the right superior and inferior pubic rami.  Hardware material
and a nerve stimulator are in place in the lumbar spine.  There are very
severe degenerative changes throughout the lumbar spine, sacroiliac and pubic
symphysis joints.

STUDY:
CT abdomen and pelvis.

TECHNIQUE:
Axial multidetector CT acquisitions of the abdomen and pelvis were
acquired after the administration of oral contrast only.

REPORT:


CT LUNG BASES:
Some dependent changes identified in the lung bases which may be minimal
thickening of the pleura bilaterally.  The patient's breast tissue appears
particularly dense given the age, but no discrete masses are seen.  Heavy
coronary artery and vascular calcifications seen.

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS:
The liver appears unremarkable.  No focal hepatic masses are seen.  Streak
artifact from cholecystectomy clips limits evaluation of parts of the liver.

There is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary dilatation evident but evaluation
of the solid abdominal viscera is somewhat limited by lack of IV contrast. The
spleen is unremarkable.  The adrenals appear unremarkable.

Left kidney appears normal.  There is hydronephrosis of the right kidney. This
can be traced down to an inflammatory pelvic mass.

CT PELVIS:
There is a circumferential thickening of much of the distal sigmoid, with
focal areas of extraluminal low attenuation measuring 12 mm to the right
probably represents a small abscess and of localized free air probably
representing a small contained microperforation.  The findings are most
consistent with ____ and extensive pericolonic stranding is also
seen.  Followup examination after appropriate treatment will be necessary to
exclude an underlying mass.  The remainder of the colon appears essentially
unremarkable.

CT BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:
The patient has extensive multilevel degenerative disease status post
multilevel laminectomy, transpedicular screw fixation, bone harvesting from
the right sacrum and also has a spinal pacemaker device in situ.  Furthermore,
there is evidence of degenerative disease in the SI joints, long-standing
fracture with ununited fracture fragments in the inferior pubic and the
superior pubic ramus on the right side and partially healed inferior pubic
ramus fracture on the left side.

ADDENDUM:
Original wet reading provided was incorrectly provided with PFI
correct which states unremarkable ultrasound of the liver and gallbladder. 
Splenomegaly with the spleen measuring up to 16 cm.

FINDINGS:
In comparison with the study of ___, there is again evidence
of two prosthetic valves with intact metallic wires.  Nasogastric tube extends
to the upper stomach, though the side hole is above the esophagogastric
junction.  Low lung volumes are seen without appreciable vascular congestion
or pneumonia.

FINDINGS:
Comparison with the study of ___, there is again low lung volumes. 
Enlarged cardiac silhouette persists with prosthetic valves in place. 
Specifically, no evidence of vascular congestion.  Nasogastric tube remains in
place, with the side hole apparently above the esophagogastric junction.

RENAL ULTRASOUND:


FINDINGS:
The right kidney measures 10.1 cm.  Left kidney measures 13.1 cm.  There is no
evidence of hydronephrosis bilaterally.  No focal renal lesions are seen. 
There is a 1.6 cm non-obstructing intrarenal calculus within the interpolar
region of the left kidney.

SINGLE FRONTAL CHEST RADIOGRAPH:
Low lung volumes and left upper and lower lobe atelectasis with possible
associated effusion are seen.  Cardiomegaly is unchanged from prior.  A right
venous line terminates at the cavoatrial junction.  An NG tube terminates with
its tip within the stomach with a side port which is may be at or above the GE
junction.

SINGLE FRONTAL CHEST RADIOGRAPH:
Bibasilar consolidation representing atelectasis is unchanged.  An NG tube
terminates in the stomach although side ports may be proximal to the
gastroesophageal junction.  A right central catheter terminates at the right
cavoatrial junction.  Linear, mild left upper lobe atelectasis is unchanged. 
Mediastinal silhouette, hilar contours and visible pleural surfaces are
normal.

EXAMINATION:
Focused abdominal ultrasound of the right upper quadrant.

FINDINGS:
The liver demonstrates no focal or textural abnormalities.  There
is no intra- or extra-hepatic biliary dilatation.  The main portal vein is
patent with appropriate hepatopetal flow.  The common bile duct measures up to
3 mm.  The spleen is unremarkable in appearance, but measures up to 16 cm. 
The gallbladder is unremarkable with no evidence of stones.

SINGLE FRONTAL PORTABLE CHEST RADIOGRAPH:
The mild cardiomegaly and mediastinal vascular engorgement without pulmonary
edema is unchanged.  Atelectasis of both lower lobes is unchanged with
interval increase in small pleural effusion on the left.  An NG tube, right
subclavian catheter terminates appropriately, unchanged.

SUPINE AND UPRIGHT AP VIEWS OF THE ABDOMEN:
There are multiple dilated loops
of small bowel primarily within the left hemiabdomen, with several
differential air-fluid levels noted.  Air is seen within relatively
decompressed loops of colon.  There is no free intraperitoneal air or
pneumatosis.  Probable small left pleural effusion and left basilar
atelectasis is noted.  There are no acute osseous findings.  Degenerative
changes are seen in the lumbar spine.

TECHNIQUE:
PA and lateral radiographs were compared to prior examinations,
most recent radiographs dated ___.

FINDINGS:
There is elevation of the left hemidiaphragm with blunting of the
left costophrenic angle consistent with a small pleural effusion.  Left base
atelectasis/scarring is also present.  No pneumothorax or pulmonary edema is
seen.  No focal consolidation to suggest pneumonia is identified.  The heart
size is normal.  No free air is seen below the diaphragm.  Prominent loops of
small bowel are partially imaged.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT images were acquired from the lung bases through the pubic
symphysis following administration of intravenous contrast.  Multiplanar
reformations were generated.

CT ABDOMEN:
Bibasilar dependent atelectasis, left greater than right, are
present.  There is no pleural effusion.  The heart is normal in size without
pericardial effusion.

The liver enhances homogeneously with the exception of a subcentimeter
hypodensity too small to fully characterize.  The gallbladder, spleen,
pancreas, and adrenal glands appear unremarkable.  Bilateral parapelvic renal
cysts are noted.  However in comparison with ___, there appears to
be an additional element of mild left hydronephrosis.  Mild delay in excretion
is also noted in the left kidney compared to the right.  A subcentimeter
hypodensity within the right kidney is too small to fully characterize.

A nasogastric tube terminates within the stomach. 

Within the lower abdomen is a segment of sigmoid colon contining numerous
diverticula with circumferential mural thickening and extensive surrounding
inflammatory changes, most consistent with ____.  Extraluminal foci
of gas with fluid are consistent with developing abscess, measuring 5.7 x 4.0
cm, although no fully organized collection is present. Dilated small bowel
loops predominantly in the left hemiabdomen measure up to 3.8 cm, with a
transition point in the lower abdomen (2, 66) in the area of active sigmoid
____ and phelgmonous changes, consistent with small bowel
obstruction. The left ureter is also minimally dilated up to the level of
inflammation within the pelvis.

Small amount of perihepatic ascites is present.  No mesenteric or
retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy by CT size criteria.  No evidence of gonadal
vein thrombosis.  Great vessels are normal in caliber and patent.

PELVIS:
The bladder is collapsed with a Foley catheter in place.  The rectum
appears unremarkable.  The prostate is mildly enlarged, consistent with BPH. 
A large, small bowel-containing right inguinal hernia demonstrates no evidence
for obstruction but contains a some fluid within.  No inguinal or pelvic
lymphadenopathy.

BONE WINDOW:
Moderate thoracolumbar spondylosis with bridging osteophytosis
is most prominent at L1-2 and ___.  No concerning focal lytic or blastic
lesion.

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT-acquired axial images were obtained through the abdomen and
pelvis following administration of intravenous contrast material.  Multiplanar
reformatted images were generated.

CT ABDOMEN WITH IV CONTRAST:
The lung bases are clear without consolidation
or pleural effusion.  The heart is normal in size, without pericardial
effusion.

In the abdomen, the liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, adrenal glands,
stomach, and duodenum are unremarkable.  The kidneys enhance and excrete
contrast symmetrically without hydronephrosis, stones, or renal masses.  There
are duplicated collecting systems bilaterally, with fusion at the proximal
ureter.  Ureters are otherwise unremarkable.

The aorta is normal in caliber throughout.  There is no free air or free fluid
in the abdomen.  There is no mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy by
size criteria.  Small retroperitoneal lymph nodes adjacent to the aorta
measure up to 6 mm.

CT PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:
An approximately 7-cm segment of the distal
descending colon demonstrates wall thickening and inflammatory changes of the
supporting fat and mesentery, centered around a single anteriorly positioned
diverticulum.  This is consistent with ____.  There is no
extraluminal air, or fluid collection to suggest complication.  Otherwise,
scattered small diverticula are noted in the sigmoid colon, and the large
bowel is otherwise unremarkable.  Multiple loops of small bowel are within
normal limits.  There is no free fluid in the pelvis.  The urinary bladder,
distal ureters and prostate glands are unremarkable.  There is no pelvic or
inguinal lymphadenopathy by size criteria.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is no fracture or worrisome bony lesion.  Mild
degenerative changes are noted in the lower lumbar spine.  Soft tissues are
unremarkable.

EXAMINATION:
CHEST (PORTABLE AP):

FINDINGS:
AP portable upright view of the chest.   Patient is slightly leftward rotated.
There is no focal consolidation, effusion, or pneumothorax. The
cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal. Imaged osseous structures are intact. 
No free air is seen below the right hemidiaphragm.

EXAMINATION:
CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS:

TECHNIQUE:
MDCT axial images were acquired through abdomen and pelvis
following intravenous contrast administration using a split bolus technique.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and submitted to PACS for

PROCEDURE:
Ultrasound-guided transvaginal drainage of pelvic collection.

TECHNIQUE:
The risks, benefits, and alternatives of the procedure were
explained to the patient. After a detailed discussion, informed written
consent was obtained. A pre-procedure timeout using three patient identifiers
was performed per ___ protocol.

The patient was placed in a lithotomy  position on the US scan table. Limited
preprocedure transvaginal ultrasound was performed to localize the collection.
The scans demonstrated a 1cm communication from the sigmoid colon to the
abscess and a distal communication from the abscess to the vagina.  Based on
the ultrasound findings an appropriate skin entry site for the drain placement
was chosen. The site was marked. Local anesthesia was administered with 1%
Lidocaine solution.

Using continuous sonographic guidance, ___ drainage catheter was
advanced via trocar technique into the collection. A sample of fluid was
aspirated, confirming catheter position within the collection. The pigtail was
deployed. The position of the pigtail was confirmed within the collection via
ultrasound.

Approximately 30 cc of tan, purulent fluid was drained with a sample sent for
microbiology evaluation. The catheter was secured by a StatLock. The catheter
was attached to suction bulb. Sterile dressing was applied.

The procedure was tolerated well, and there were no immediate post-procedural
complications.

SEDATION:
Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of 4
mg Versed and 200 mcg fentanyl throughout the total intra-service time of 18
minutes during which patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse.
